title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子路問君子子曰脩己以敬曰如斯而已
乎曰脩己以安人曰如斯而已乎曰脩
己以安百姓
楊子充
同考試官教諭崔批寫出聖賢問答君子之意無遺
同考試官教諭劉批辭簡理明知敬學者
考試官學正孫批渾厚
===
考試官教授張批古淡可錄
聖人於賢者論君子而推至其極不越乎敬而
已夫自脩己以至安人安百姓敬之成始而成
終也所以為君子者寧有餘乎昔者子路學為
君子而未得其道故問焉而欲知所往也夫子
以為身者萬事之本也敬者聖學之要也脩己
以敬則君子之道本諸身天下之德聚於敬斯
其所以為君子矣子路乃曰脩己以敬止於己
耳彼君子之道大矣而豈如斯已乎夫子告之
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子路問君子。子曰：「脩己以敬。」曰：「如斯而已乎？」曰：「脩己以安人。」曰：「如斯而已乎？」曰：「脩己以安百姓。」

楊子充

同考試官教諭崔批：寫出聖賢問答君子之意無遺。
同考試官教諭劉批：辭簡理明，知敬學者。
考試官學正孫批：渾厚。
考試官教授張批：古淡可錄。

聖人於賢者論君子，而推至其極，不越乎敬而已。夫自脩己以至安人、安百姓，敬之成始而成終也。所以為君子者，寧有餘乎？昔者子路學為君子而未得其道，故問焉而欲知所往也。夫子以為身者萬事之本也，敬者聖學之要也。脩己以敬，則君子之道本諸身，天下之德聚於敬，斯其所以為君子矣。子路乃曰：「脩己以敬，止於己耳。彼君子之道大矣，而豈如斯已乎？」夫子告之
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Zilu asked about the gentleman. The Master said, “Cultivate oneself through reverent attentiveness.” Zilu asked, “Is that all?” The Master said, “Cultivate oneself so as to bring peace to others.” Zilu asked, “Is that all?” The Master said, “Cultivate oneself so as to bring peace to the common people.”

Yang Zichong

Comment by Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor: “Fully conveys the meaning of the exchange between the sage and the worthy concerning the gentleman, leaving nothing out.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “Concise in expression and clear in principle: a scholar who understands reverent attentiveness.”
Comment by Examiner Sun, School Director: “Substantial and profound.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: “Classically plain and restrained; worthy of inclusion.”

In discussing the gentleman with a worthy, the sage carried the matter to its ultimate extent, yet went no further than reverent attentiveness. From cultivating oneself to bringing peace to others and to the common people, it is reverent attentiveness that brings both the beginning and the completion to fulfillment. Could anything more be needed to constitute a gentleman?

Formerly, Zilu was learning to become a gentleman but had not yet grasped the way. Thus he asked about it, wishing to know the direction in which to proceed. The Master considered the self to be the foundation of all affairs, and reverent attentiveness to be the essential point of the learning of the sages. If one cultivates oneself through reverent attentiveness, the way of the gentleman is rooted in oneself, and all the virtues under Heaven converge in reverent attentiveness. This is what makes one a gentleman.

Zilu then said, “Cultivating oneself through reverent attentiveness extends only to oneself. The way of the gentleman is great: how could it amount to no more than this?” The Master told him …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
蓋謂人固猶夫我也梏有我之私者其分隔以
絕夫旣脩己以敬矣則舉此加彼而行之自利
己立而立人己達而達人所以使道行於彼而
人以安者此也敬可以安人而謂不足以盡君
子乎子路又曰脩己以安人止於人耳彼君子
之道博矣而豈如斯已乎夫子告之蓋謂百姓
固猶夫人也昧同人之公者其勢疎以暌夫旣
脩己以安人矣則篤近舉遠而推之自通脩禮
以達義體信以達順所以使化無不被而百姓
===
安者亦此也敬可以安百姓而謂不足以盡君
子乎是知脩己以敬夫子一言盡天下之理矣
而安人安百姓特舉而措之耳豈復有所加哉
惜子路未之思也大抵聖門之徒以賜之達而
以博施濟衆求仁以由之果而不足於脩己之
敬是皆好勇好智過高之病也故夫子均極言
之而曰堯舜其猶病諸抑之也非聖言之有遺
也堯舜之仁敬未可以易語由賜也故曰於己
脩之於近譬之亦足矣能爲由賜之仁敬而後
punctuated: 蓋謂人固猶夫我也，梏有我之私者，其分隔以絕。夫旣脩己以敬矣，則舉此加彼而行之自利，己立而立人，己達而達人，所以使道行於彼而人以安者，此也。敬可以安人，而謂不足以盡君子乎？子路又曰：「脩己以安人，止於人耳。彼君子之道博矣，而豈如斯已乎？」夫子告之，蓋謂百姓固猶夫人也，昧同人之公者，其勢疎以暌。夫旣脩己以安人矣，則篤近舉遠而推之自通，脩禮以達義，體信以達順，所以使化無不被而百姓安者，亦此也。敬可以安百姓，而謂不足以盡君子乎？是知脩己以敬，夫子一言盡天下之理矣，而安人、安百姓，特舉而措之耳，豈復有所加哉？惜子路未之思也！大抵聖門之徒，以賜之達，而以博施濟衆求仁；以由之果，而不足於脩己之敬，是皆好勇好智過高之病也。故夫子均極言之，而曰：「堯舜其猶病諸！」抑之也，非聖言之有遺也。堯舜之仁敬，未可以易語由賜也。故曰：「於己脩之，於近譬之，亦足矣。」能爲由賜之仁敬，而後
translation_en:
…His meaning was that other people are fundamentally like oneself. Those imprisoned by the selfishness of recognizing only themselves become divided and cut off from others. Once one has cultivated oneself through reverence, extending this to others will naturally proceed smoothly: establishing oneself, one establishes others; attaining success oneself, one enables others to succeed. This is how the Way is put into practice among others and they are brought to peace. If reverence can bring others to peace, can it be said to fall short of all that constitutes a gentleman? Zilu again said: “Cultivating oneself to bring others to peace extends only to those others. The gentleman’s Way is broad indeed; could it end with this?” The Master instructed him, meaning that the common people are fundamentally like those other people. Those blind to the impartiality of sharing a common humanity become estranged and separated from them. Once one has cultivated oneself to bring others to peace, one strengthens one’s concern for those nearby and embraces those far away, and this extension naturally encounters no obstruction. One cultivates ritual propriety to realize righteousness and embodies trustworthiness to realize harmonious accord. This, too, is how transforming influence reaches everywhere and the common people are brought to peace. If reverence can bring the common people to peace, can it be said to fall short of all that constitutes a gentleman?

Thus we know that, in the single statement “cultivate oneself through reverence,” the Master exhausted all the principles under Heaven. Bringing others and the common people to peace is merely putting this into practice. What further addition could there be? It is regrettable that Zilu had not reflected upon this! Generally speaking, among the disciples of the sage, Ci, for all his understanding, sought benevolence through generously bestowing benefits and aiding the multitude; You, for all his decisiveness, considered cultivating oneself through reverence insufficient. These were both failings of esteeming courage and wisdom and aiming excessively high. Thus the Master pressed his explanation to its furthest point in both cases, saying: “Even Yao and Shun would have found this difficult!” He was restraining their ambitions; it was not that the sage’s words had left anything out. The benevolence and reverence of Yao and Shun could not readily be discussed with You and Ci. Hence he said: “Cultivate it in oneself and draw analogies from what is near at hand: this is sufficient.” Only after being able to practice the benevolence and reverence appropriate to You and Ci …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
可以語堯舜之仁之敬矣
辟如天地之無不持載無不覆幬辟如四
時之錯行如日月之代明
鄭富
同考試官教諭沈批不腐不奇可謂文矣
同考試官教諭文批善作中庸義者僅見此篇
考試官學正孫批善言聖人之大者
考試官教授張批形容聖德即是當時語意
中庸擬聖人之德同造化之大也甚矣聖人之
===
德之大也非假造化以擬之抑何以盡其形容
哉中庸發明夫道至此蓋謂聖人人之至也仲
尼聖之至也是故曰祖述曰憲章帝王之道其
兼之矣曰上律曰下襲天地之道其盡之矣則
其所以為德也抑將何以擬之哉其辟諸天地
乎彼其極負荷之重萬物資博厚而生成此地
之無不持載也極帡冒之大萬物仰高明而變
化此天之無不覆幬也而仲尼之德如之則易
簡盡天地之理而範圍不過固有與之異位而
punctuated:
可以語堯舜之仁之敬矣。
辟如天地之無不持載、無不覆幬，辟如四時之錯行，如日月之代明。
鄭富
同考試官教諭沈批：「不腐不奇，可謂文矣。」
同考試官教諭文批：「善作中庸義者，僅見此篇。」
考試官學正孫批：「善言聖人之大者。」
考試官教授張批：「形容聖德，即是當時語意。」
中庸擬聖人之德，同造化之大也。甚矣，聖人之德之大也！非假造化以擬之，抑何以盡其形容哉？中庸發明夫道至此，蓋謂聖人，人之至也；仲尼，聖之至也。是故曰祖述，曰憲章，帝王之道其兼之矣；曰上律，曰下襲，天地之道其盡之矣。則其所以為德也，抑將何以擬之哉？其辟諸天地乎？彼其極負荷之重，萬物資博厚而生成，此地之無不持載也；極帡冒之大，萬物仰高明而變化，此天之無不覆幬也。而仲尼之德如之，則易簡盡天地之理，而範圍不過，固有與之異位而
translation_en:
…one can then speak of the benevolence and reverence of Yao and Shun.

“Like earth and heaven, which sustain and shelter everything; like the four seasons proceeding in alternation, and the sun and moon shining in turn.”

Zheng Fu

Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “Neither stale nor eccentric: this deserves to be called accomplished writing.”

Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor, comments: “Of essays that skillfully expound the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean, I have seen scarcely any but this one.”

Examiner Sun, School Director, comments: “An able exposition of the sage’s greatness.”

Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “Its portrayal of sagely virtue captures the meaning of the words in their original setting.”

The Doctrine of the Mean likens the sage’s virtue to the greatness of the transforming work of heaven and earth. How great indeed is the sage’s virtue! Without borrowing this transforming work as a comparison, how could one describe it fully? In elucidating the Way to this point, the Doctrine of the Mean means that the sage is the highest attainment of humanity, and Zhongni is the highest attainment of sagehood. Thus, when it speaks of his ‘continuing and transmitting’ and his ‘taking as models,’ it means that he comprehensively embraces the Way of the ancient emperors and kings. When it speaks of his ‘conforming above’ and ‘following below,’ it means that he fully embodies the Way of heaven and earth. To what, then, shall we liken the virtue that makes him what he is? Shall we compare it to heaven and earth? Earth bears the utmost weight of its burden; the myriad things depend upon its breadth and depth to come into being and grow. This is earth sustaining everything. Heaven extends its shelter to the utmost reach; the myriad things look up to its loftiness and brightness to change and transform. This is heaven sheltering everything. Zhongni’s virtue resembles them: through ease and simplicity, it comprehends fully the principles of heaven and earth, encompassing them without exceeding their bounds. Indeed, though occupying a different position from them, it…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
同體者矣所謂與天地合其德者非與其辟諸
四時日月乎彼其寒暑相禪貞元神動靜之機
此四時之錯行也晝夜相推貞明妙屈伸之感
此日月之代明也而仲尼之德如之則中正貫
天下之道而旁行不流固有與之異氣而同運
者矣所謂與四時合其序日月合其明者非與
夫天也地也四時日月也一道也聖人覆如天
載如地運行如四時日月亦惟體道之一耳子
思立言至此其知人而知天者與抑聖人於造
===
化豈特如之而已哉蓋其以天地爲體而賴以
常位以四時爲柄而賴以常運以日月爲紀而
賴以常明微聖人則道不可見化機亦幾乎息
矣是故天地盡物者也聖人盡道者也知道爲
天地之本則知聖人有功於天地
君子深造之以道欲其自得之也自得之
則居之安居之安則資之深資之深則
取之左右逢其原故君子欲其自得之
也
punctuated:
同體者矣。所謂與天地合其德者，非與？其辟諸四時日月乎？彼其寒暑相禪，貞元神動靜之機，此四時之錯行也；晝夜相推，貞明妙屈伸之感，此日月之代明也。而仲尼之德如之，則中正貫天下之道，而旁行不流，固有與之異氣而同運者矣。所謂與四時合其序、日月合其明者，非與？夫天也，地也，四時日月也，一道也。聖人覆如天，載如地，運行如四時日月，亦惟體道之一耳。子思立言至此，其知人而知天者與？抑聖人於造化，豈特如之而已哉？蓋其以天地爲體，而賴以常位；以四時爲柄，而賴以常運；以日月爲紀，而賴以常明。微聖人，則道不可見，化機亦幾乎息矣。是故天地盡物者也，聖人盡道者也。知道爲天地之本，則知聖人有功於天地。

君子深造之以道，欲其自得之也。自得之，則居之安；居之安，則資之深；資之深，則取之左右逢其原。故君子欲其自得之也。
translation_en:
…yet share the same substance. Is this not what is meant by matching Heaven and Earth in his virtue? Might he be compared to the four seasons and the sun and moon? Cold and heat succeed one another; completion and renewal give wondrous efficacy to the workings of movement and stillness: such is the alternating course of the four seasons. Day and night impel one another onward; constant brightness renders wondrous the interaction of contraction and expansion: such is the alternating illumination of sun and moon. Zhongni’s virtue is like these. Thus, centrality and correctness run through the Way of all under Heaven; it extends in every direction without going astray. Though differing from them in vital force, he indeed shares their operation. Is this not what is meant by matching the four seasons in their sequence and the sun and moon in their brightness?

Heaven, Earth, the four seasons, and the sun and moon embody a single Way. The sage shelters like Heaven, bears up like Earth, and moves and operates like the four seasons and the sun and moon, simply embodying the unity of the Way. Having carried his exposition this far, does Zisi not understand both humanity and Heaven? Yet in relation to the creative transformations of nature, does the sage merely resemble them? He takes Heaven and Earth as his substance, and they depend upon him to remain in their constant positions; he takes the four seasons as his handles, and they depend upon him to maintain their constant revolutions; he takes the sun and moon as his ordering framework, and they depend upon him to maintain their constant illumination. Without the sage, the Way could not be made manifest, and the workings of transformation would almost cease. Thus Heaven and Earth bring things to their fullest realization, while the sage brings the Way to its fullest realization. To understand that the Way is the foundation of Heaven and Earth is to understand that the sage renders service to Heaven and Earth.

The gentleman advances deeply in learning by following the Way, wishing to attain understanding for himself. Having attained it for himself, he abides in it securely; abiding in it securely, he draws deeply upon its resources; drawing deeply upon its resources, he finds its source wherever he turns. Thus the gentleman wishes to attain understanding for himself.

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
薛欽
同考試官教諭沈批辯析渾融非苟作者
同考試官學正蔡批文字從心學中來機軸自别
考試官學正孫批君子之學是如此
考試官教授張批體貼自得之學始終有據
大賢論君子學貴於自得必詳言其妙而重致
其意焉蓋學不要於自得則其充實之妙有難
以輕語者豈君子之所貴哉孟子示人以君子
之學如此蓋謂天下無身外之道君子無心外
===
之學是故學莫病於急遽而尤患於躐等君子
則務造之以積久之功而必究竟於進為之道
窮之以歳月之力而不妄意於言意之表是豈
徒哉蓋欲有所持循焉優游以俟夫默契之妙
得以據守焉涵泳以趣於貫通之境學與道相
忘而道與心為一也夫旣自得矣則見道明而
操守定物誘小而事變輕天下之至貞在我矣
居之有不安乎居安矣則涵養充而萬物備取
無窮而用不竭天下之至靜在我矣資之有不
punctuated:
薛欽

同考試官教諭沈批：辯析渾融，非苟作者。
同考試官學正蔡批：文字從心學中來，機軸自别。
考試官學正孫批：君子之學是如此。
考試官教授張批：體貼自得之學，始終有據。

大賢論君子學貴於自得，必詳言其妙而重致其意焉。蓋學不要於自得，則其充實之妙有難以輕語者，豈君子之所貴哉？孟子示人以君子之學如此，蓋謂天下無身外之道，君子無心外之學。是故學莫病於急遽，而尤患於躐等。君子則務造之以積久之功，而必究竟於進為之道；窮之以歳月之力，而不妄意於言意之表。是豈徒哉？蓋欲有所持循焉，優游以俟夫默契之妙；得以據守焉，涵泳以趣於貫通之境。學與道相忘，而道與心為一也。夫旣自得矣，則見道明而操守定，物誘小而事變輕，天下之至貞在我矣。居之有不安乎？居安矣，則涵養充而萬物備，取無窮而用不竭，天下之至靜在我矣。資之有不
translation_en:
Xue Qin

Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor of a County Confucian School, comments: “The analysis is thoroughly integrated; this is no carelessly composed work.”
Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor of a Subprefectural Confucian School, comments: “The writing comes from learning of the mind; its organizing conception is distinctive.”
Examiner Sun, Instructor of a Subprefectural Confucian School, comments: “Such indeed is the learning of the gentleman.”
Examiner Zhang, Professor of a Prefectural Confucian School, comments: “He sympathetically grasps the learning of personal realization; the argument has a firm basis throughout.”

When the great worthy discusses how the gentleman’s learning values personal realization, he necessarily explains its subtleties in detail and repeatedly stresses its significance. For if learning does not aim at personal realization, the subtlety of its fullness and substance can hardly be spoken of lightly. How could such learning be what the gentleman prizes? This is how Mengzi presents the gentleman’s learning to others. His meaning is that nowhere under Heaven is there a Way outside oneself, and for the gentleman there is no learning outside the mind. Thus nothing harms learning more than haste, and skipping stages is an especially serious concern. The gentleman therefore strives to advance through efforts accumulated over a long time, always pursuing to its conclusion the proper course of progress. He plumbs its depths through years of exertion, without indulging in fanciful conjectures about what lies beyond words and meanings. Could this be purposeless? He wishes to have something to follow and uphold, proceeding at ease as he awaits the subtle experience of tacit accord; to have something on which to take his stand, immersing himself in it to approach comprehensive understanding. Learning and the Way lose their distinction, and the Way and the mind become one.

Once he has attained personal realization, his perception of the Way is clear and his moral resolve is firm. The allure of external things diminishes, and changing circumstances carry little weight: the utmost steadfastness under Heaven is within him. Could he fail to dwell in it securely? Once he dwells securely, his inner cultivation becomes full and the myriad things are complete within him. What he draws upon is boundless, and what he puts to use is inexhaustible: the utmost stillness under Heaven is within him. Could his drawing upon it fail to be…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
深乎所資者既深則其達之於日用施之於應
酬取之左而左無不逢其原取之右而右無不
值其本蓋萬化萃無窮之感而一理通天下之
故也夫居安也資深也逢原也皆本於自得如
此故君子之學不以强探力取爲能而必要於
心有所得不事虛無鹵莽之習而必欲其理得
於我者其功豈容或巳哉是則學而至於自得
其爲學也大矣君子庶可以語斯道之責而無
憾矣乎嗟夫心學之不易以講也後世爲學之
===
弊見小者安於不可得欲速者狃於苟得均之
不可言學也况心學乎孔門之學惟務自得有
悟性與天道之微言者有唯一貫之指授者傳
至孟氏既發之於宋人養苗之喻又申之以深
造自得之說此固聖賢相傳爲學之標的也非
孟氏一人之言也此實有志於道者所當自力
焉者也
易
君子體仁足以長人嘉會足以合禮利物
punctuated:
深乎？所資者既深，則其達之於日用，施之於應酬，取之左而左無不逢其原，取之右而右無不值其本。蓋萬化萃無窮之感，而一理通天下之故也。夫居安也，資深也，逢原也，皆本於自得如此。故君子之學，不以强探力取爲能，而必要於心有所得；不事虛無鹵莽之習，而必欲其理得於我者，其功豈容或巳哉？是則學而至於自得，其爲學也大矣。君子庶可以語斯道之責而無憾矣乎！嗟夫！心學之不易以講也！後世爲學之弊，見小者安於不可得，欲速者狃於苟得，均之不可言學也，况心學乎？孔門之學，惟務自得，有悟性與天道之微言者，有唯一貫之指授者。傳至孟氏，既發之於宋人養苗之喻，又申之以深造自得之說。此固聖賢相傳爲學之標的也，非孟氏一人之言也。此實有志於道者所當自力焉者也。

易
君子體仁，足以長人；嘉會，足以合禮；利物
translation_en:
…deep? Once the resources upon which he draws are deep, he brings this understanding into everyday life and applies it in his dealings with others. Drawing upon it to the left, he invariably encounters its source; drawing upon it to the right, he invariably meets its root. For the myriad transformations gather together inexhaustible interactions, while a single principle runs through all the affairs of the world. Dwelling securely, drawing deeply, and encountering the source—all are thus rooted in attaining understanding for oneself. Hence, in learning, the gentleman does not regard strenuous probing and forcible acquisition as marks of ability, but insists upon gaining something in his own heart. He does not pursue habits of emptiness and heedlessness, but insists that principle be grasped within himself. How could his efforts ever be allowed to cease? When learning reaches such personal attainment, great indeed is that learning! May the gentleman then be said to have fulfilled his responsibility toward this Way without regret?

Alas, how difficult it is to expound the learning of the heart-mind! Among the faults of learning in later ages, those of narrow vision resign themselves to being unable to attain understanding, while those who desire speed grow accustomed to haphazard attainment. Neither can be said to engage in learning, much less in the learning of the heart-mind! Learning in the school of Confucius strove solely for personal attainment. There were those who comprehended the subtle words concerning human nature and the Way of Heaven, and those who received the instruction concerning the single thread running through all things. When this teaching was transmitted to Master Meng, he first elucidated it through the analogy of the man of Song tending his seedlings, then further explained it through his account of advancing deeply in learning and attaining understanding for oneself. This is indeed the aim of learning transmitted from sage to worthy, not merely the teaching of Master Meng alone. It is truly something toward which those committed to the Way must exert themselves.

Book of Changes

The gentleman embodies benevolence and is thereby able to lead others; he brings together what is excellent and is thereby able to accord with ritual propriety; he benefits things…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
足以和義貞固足以幹事
薛欽
同考試官訓導李批君子學易希天之功于此可見
同考試官教諭沈批詞不費而理自足
同考試官學正蔡批是君子法乾意思
考試官學正孫批精粹
考試官教授張批詳明
文言論君子於天德各極其躬行之實焉夫德
原於天而具於人也自非君子孰能行之極其
===
實而無愧乎天哉吾夫子作文言發乾道之蘊
如此意謂天之賦予於人也固未嘗不全而人
之奉承乎天也每患於難盡其惟君子乎是故
在天之元於人爲仁而所以統天下之善者此
也君子一身淨盡乎私欲之間隔而充足於生
意之流通是吾之體皆是仁也而惠愛之貫徹
天下猶一家也中國爲一人也謂不足以長人
也邪在天之亨於人爲禮而所以飾天下之動
者此也君子一身周旋於百爲之萃集而各中
punctuated:
足以和義，貞固足以幹事。
薛欽
同考試官訓導李批：「君子學易希天之功，于此可見。」
同考試官教諭沈批：「詞不費而理自足。」
同考試官學正蔡批：「是君子法乾意思。」
考試官學正孫批：「精粹。」
考試官教授張批：「詳明。」
文言論君子於天德，各極其躬行之實焉。夫德原於天而具於人也，自非君子，孰能行之，極其實而無愧乎天哉？吾夫子作文言，發乾道之蘊如此。意謂天之賦予於人也，固未嘗不全，而人之奉承乎天也，每患於難盡，其惟君子乎！是故在天之元，於人爲仁，而所以統天下之善者，此也。君子一身，淨盡乎私欲之間隔，而充足於生意之流通，是吾之體皆是仁也。而惠愛之貫徹，天下猶一家也，中國爲一人也，謂不足以長人也邪？在天之亨，於人爲禮，而所以飾天下之動者，此也。君子一身，周旋於百爲之萃集，而各中
translation_en:
…is sufficient to harmonize righteousness; steadfast firmness is sufficient to carry out affairs.

Xue Qin

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Here one can see the achievement of the noble man in studying the Changes and aspiring to emulate Heaven.”
Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “The wording is economical, yet the reasoning is complete.”
Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “This conveys the meaning of the noble man taking Qian as his model.”
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “Refined and pure.”
Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “Detailed and clear.”

The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan), in discussing the noble man’s relation to Heaven’s virtues, shows how he fully realizes each through his own conduct. Virtue originates in Heaven and is endowed in human beings. Who but the noble man can put it into practice, fully realize its substance, and stand without shame before Heaven? Such are the hidden meanings of the Way of Qian that our Master brought to light in composing the Wenyan. His meaning is that Heaven’s endowment of human beings has never been incomplete, yet people constantly find it difficult to fulfill all that Heaven has entrusted to them. Surely only the noble man can do so!

Thus, what in Heaven is origination (yuan) is benevolence in human beings: this is what unites all the goodness under Heaven. In his whole person, the noble man utterly clears away the obstructions of selfish desires and is filled with the free flow of life-giving vitality. Thus, my entire embodied being is benevolence. With kindness and love extending everywhere, all under Heaven is like one family, and the Central Kingdom is as one person. Could one say that this is insufficient to lead others?

What in Heaven is flourishing (heng) is ritual propriety in human beings: this is what gives fitting form to all activity under Heaven. In his whole person, the noble man moves amid the convergence of a hundred undertakings, and in each duly accords with…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
其相接之體裁是吾之會無不嘉也而經緯之
品制三百其雍雍也三千其秩秩也謂不足以
合禮也邪天道有利在人則為義所以整齊乎
天下者每嫌於不和矣君子雜處乎萬有不齊
之變隨其位序之宜付以各得之分則志定於
等威之辨情安於職守之明截然之中而有泰
然者在也義之和也孰大焉天道有貞在人則
為智所以運量乎天下者每病於難濟矣君子
明燭乎物理民彝之正堅其一定之守確乎趨
===
向之的則物來有順應之妙事至無眩瞀之惑
大本不虧而大業其日起也事之立也孰尚焉
君子之行乎四德者如此則性在人命在天而
我能一之矣雖然四德之賦天非有私厚於君
子也君子之能全其所賦亦非有所增益於人
也蓋本其剛健足以勝其任不息有以純於天
與衆人之懦焉昏焉甘于棄天焉者不同耳嗚
呼體仁也嘉會也利物也貞固也此實聖人裁
成輔相之道程子所謂乾道施之人事者也有
punctuated:
其相接之體裁，是吾之會無不嘉也。而經緯之品制，三百其雍雍也，三千其秩秩也，謂不足以合禮也邪？天道有利，在人則為義，所以整齊乎天下者，每嫌於不和矣。君子雜處乎萬有不齊之變，隨其位序之宜，付以各得之分，則志定於等威之辨，情安於職守之明，截然之中而有泰然者在也。義之和也，孰大焉？天道有貞，在人則為智，所以運量乎天下者，每病於難濟矣。君子明燭乎物理民彝之正，堅其一定之守，確乎趨向之的，則物來有順應之妙，事至無眩瞀之惑，大本不虧，而大業其日起也。事之立也，孰尚焉？君子之行乎四德者如此，則性在人，命在天，而我能一之矣。

雖然，四德之賦，天非有私厚於君子也；君子之能全其所賦，亦非有所增益於人也。蓋本其剛健，足以勝其任；不息，有以純於天，與衆人之懦焉、昏焉、甘于棄天焉者不同耳。

嗚呼！體仁也，嘉會也，利物也，貞固也，此實聖人裁成輔相之道，程子所謂乾道施之人事者也。有
translation_en:
…the proper forms of their mutual dealings: thus none of my gatherings is other than excellent. The graded institutions that order them—the three hundred major rites in their harmony and the three thousand minor observances in their orderly array—could these be deemed insufficient to accord with ritual propriety? In the Way of Heaven there is benefit (li); in human beings it becomes righteousness. Yet the means used to bring order to all under Heaven are often found wanting in harmony. The gentleman lives amid the manifold changes of things in all their diversity. According to what befits their positions and ranks, he assigns each its proper share. Thus aspirations are settled through clear distinctions of rank and dignity, and feelings are at ease through clarity about duties and responsibilities. Amid sharply drawn distinctions there is tranquillity. What harmony of righteousness could be greater than this? In the Way of Heaven there is constancy (zhen); in human beings it becomes wisdom. Yet deliberations concerning all under Heaven often suffer from difficulty in bringing matters to fruition. The gentleman clearly illuminates the principles of things and the correctness of the enduring human norms; he holds firmly to his settled commitments and fixes securely the goal toward which he strives. Thus, when things come before him, he responds with fitting subtlety; when affairs arise, he suffers no bewilderment or confusion. The great foundation remains unimpaired, and the great undertaking advances daily. What could surpass this in establishing affairs? Such is the gentleman’s practice of the four virtues. Human nature resides in human beings, and the mandate resides in Heaven, yet I can unite them.

Nevertheless, in endowing beings with the four virtues, Heaven shows no special generosity toward the gentleman. Nor does the gentleman, in fully realizing his endowment, add anything to what human beings possess. Rather, rooted in firmness and strength, he is capable of bearing his responsibilities; through unceasing effort, he can accord purely with Heaven. He differs only in this from ordinary people who are weak, benighted, and content to forsake Heaven.

Ah! Embodying benevolence, making gatherings excellent, benefiting things, and remaining constant and firm: these are indeed the sage’s way of shaping and completing, assisting and supporting the workings of Heaven and Earth—what Master Cheng called applying the Way of Qian to human affairs. Those who have…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
世道之責者其毋忽於此哉
是故聖人以通天下之志以定天下之業
以斷天下之疑
徐麟
同考試官訓導李批能發聖人憂世之心
同考試官教諭沈批通志定業斷疑歸重聖人良是
同考試官學正蔡批講易之用於人親切可取
考試官學正孫批整索
考試官教授張批知易
===
大傳原聖人作易而以周天下之用焉盖易爲
斯民而作也通其志定其業斷其疑斯天下之
用周矣聖人之作易其至矣哉大傳此章專言
卜筮以爲易也者固開物成務冒天下之道者
也然豈不致之民哉是故凡有所向者民之志
也迷而不覺者固多矣聖人以易而通焉彰之
以貞勝之理形之以趨時之規得也告之吉失
也告之凶指迷途而頓悟開窒塞以前知使明
諸心知所往焉不有以通天下之志邪凡措之
punctuated:
世道之責者，其毋忽於此哉！

「是故聖人以通天下之志，以定天下之業，以斷天下之疑。」
徐麟

同考試官訓導李批：能發聖人憂世之心。
同考試官教諭沈批：通志、定業、斷疑，歸重聖人，良是。
同考試官學正蔡批：講易之用於人，親切可取。
考試官學正孫批：整索。
考試官教授張批：知易。

大傳原聖人作易，而以周天下之用焉。盖易爲斯民而作也，通其志，定其業，斷其疑，斯天下之用周矣。聖人之作易，其至矣哉！大傳此章專言卜筮，以爲易也者，固開物成務、冒天下之道者也，然豈不致之民哉？是故凡有所向者，民之志也，迷而不覺者固多矣。聖人以易而通焉，彰之以貞勝之理，形之以趨時之規，得也告之吉，失也告之凶，指迷途而頓悟，開窒塞以前知，使明諸心，知所往焉，不有以通天下之志邪？凡措之
translation_en:
…those who bear responsibility for the moral order of the world should surely not neglect this!

“Therefore the sages used it to give free course to the aspirations of all under Heaven, to settle the undertakings of all under Heaven, and to resolve the doubts of all under Heaven.”
Xu Lin

Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “It brings out the sages’ concern for the world.”
Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: “In giving free course to aspirations, settling undertakings, and resolving doubts, it places the emphasis on the sages. This is indeed correct.”
Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor, comments: “Its explanation of the application of the Changes to human affairs is pertinent and commendable.”
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “Orderly and searching [?].”
Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “He understands the Changes.”

The Great Commentary traces the sages’ purpose in composing the Changes: thereby to provide fully for the needs of all under Heaven. For the Changes was composed for the people. Give free course to their aspirations, settle their undertakings, and resolve their doubts: then the needs of all under Heaven are fully provided for. How consummate was the sages’ composition of the Changes!

This chapter of the Great Commentary speaks exclusively of divination by tortoise shell and milfoil stalks. It holds that the Changes indeed discloses things, brings affairs to completion, and encompasses the Way of all under Heaven. Yet surely this must be brought to bear upon the people? Thus, whatever people direct themselves toward constitutes their aspirations; certainly many are lost and unaware. The sages use the Changes to give these aspirations free course. They illuminate them through the principle that constancy prevails and give them form through the rule of acting in accordance with the time. When people act rightly, it tells them of good fortune; when they err, it tells them of misfortune. It points out their mistaken paths so that they suddenly awaken, and clears their obstructions so that they know beforehand. It enables them to understand in their hearts and know where to go. Does this not give free course to the aspirations of all under Heaven? Whatever is put into…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
行者民之業也隳而无成者亦衆矣聖人以易
而定焉觀所會以行其常因其窮而裁之變吉
則欲其趨凶則欲其避誘掖以輔其行也鼓舞
以妙其用也使力行以底其績焉不有以定天
下之業邪以至慮因識而未瑩事值豫而難圖
民不能以無疑也疑而能决者或寡矣聖人以
易而斷焉燭事理之幾以會其極辨憂虞之介
以要其歸得之吉而决其趨失之凶而决其避
别是非於指掌定從違以殊途使猶豫者釋而
===
進退者果矣不有以斷天下之疑乎夫聖人假
乎易以周乎用如此是其功之有益于天下亦
豈淺淺者倫哉抑考天地設位而易行乎其中
矣又曰天地設位聖人成能是知天地有待于
聖人而聖人成能乎天地其所以作易而致之
民者殆非偶然也大傳是章專言卜筮而先設
爲問答以啓之至此則言易書之用如此其大
而聖人之功於是爲極下文且又反覆言之不
一而足無非發明此意而已彼以卜筮小吾易
punctuated: 行者，民之業也。隳而无成者亦衆矣，聖人以易而定焉。觀所會以行其常，因其窮而裁之變；吉則欲其趨，凶則欲其避。誘掖以輔其行也，鼓舞以妙其用也，使力行以底其績焉，不有以定天下之業邪？以至慮因識而未瑩，事值豫而難圖，民不能以無疑也。疑而能决者或寡矣，聖人以易而斷焉。燭事理之幾以會其極，辨憂虞之介以要其歸。得之吉而决其趨，失之凶而决其避。别是非於指掌，定從違以殊途，使猶豫者釋而進退者果矣，不有以斷天下之疑乎？夫聖人假乎易以周乎用如此，是其功之有益于天下，亦豈淺淺者倫哉？抑考「天地設位，而易行乎其中矣」，又曰「天地設位，聖人成能」，是知天地有待于聖人，而聖人成能乎天地。其所以作易而致之民者，殆非偶然也。大傳是章專言卜筮，而先設爲問答以啓之。至此則言易書之用如此其大，而聖人之功於是爲極。下文且又反覆言之，不一而足，無非發明此意而已。彼以卜筮小吾易
translation_en:
…what they put into practice constitutes the people’s undertakings. Many let these fall into ruin and accomplish nothing; the sages used the Changes to give them stability. They observed how circumstances converged so as to put constant principles into practice, and, when circumstances reached an impasse, determined the appropriate changes. What was auspicious they wished the people to pursue; what was inauspicious they wished them to avoid. They guided and supported the people to assist their conduct, and encouraged and inspired them to make their use of the Changes effective, enabling them to strive in practice and attain results. Did this not serve to stabilize the undertakings of all under Heaven? Furthermore, deliberations remain unclear because of limitations in understanding, and affairs become difficult to plan when beset by hesitation [?]; the people cannot be without doubts. Few, perhaps, can resolve their doubts, so the sages used the Changes to settle them. They illuminated the subtle beginnings of the principles governing affairs so as to grasp their ultimate import, and distinguished the fine boundaries of grounds for anxiety so as to ascertain their outcome. Through the auspiciousness of getting things right, they resolved what to pursue; through the inauspiciousness of going wrong, they resolved what to avoid. They distinguished right from wrong as clearly as something displayed in the palm of the hand, and determined what to follow and what to reject along their different courses. Thus those who hesitated were freed from doubt, and those deciding whether to advance or withdraw became resolute. Did this not serve to settle the doubts of all under Heaven?

Such was the way the sages drew upon the Changes to encompass every practical need. Could the benefit their achievement brought to all under Heaven be ranked with anything paltry? Consider, moreover, the statement, “Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and change operates between them,” and again, “Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and the sages bring their capacities to completion.” From this we know that Heaven and Earth depend upon the sages, and that the sages bring the capacities of Heaven and Earth to completion. Their creation of the Changes and its transmission to the people were surely no accident. This chapter of the Great Commentary speaks specifically of divination by tortoise shell and milfoil, beginning with a question and answer to introduce the subject. At this point it explains how vast the uses of the book of Changes are, and how the sages’ achievement thereby reaches its utmost. The text that follows returns to this repeatedly, not content with a single statement; all of it serves only to elucidate this meaning. Those who belittle our Changes on account of its use in divination…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
者謂之何哉
書
朕言惠可底行禹曰兪乃言底可績
鄭富
同考試官教諭文批宛然虞廷矢謨氣象
考試官學正孫批雋永
考試官教授張批精密
大臣自信其謨之有用同列深與其謨之有成
夫知人安民之謨治道備矣大臣自信而同列
===
復深與之得無引君之意哉昔皐陶陳謨而終
之以此若曰進言本乎不欺用言貴乎致治如
所謂迪德以盡知人安民之事六者有翕受敷
施之義無教無曠之戒焉有典禮命討之辨聰
明明畏之嚴焉吾爲此言豈徒華國而已蓋言
者行之表也言之無文行弗遠矣安望其底行
邪玆則取諸人必本諸己秩秩然皆協乎良圖
慎厥事惟旣厥心鑿鑿乎不違于國是以官俊
乂綽有持循以惠黎元殆無牴牾蓋不徒托之
punctuated:
者，謂之何哉？
書
「朕言惠可底行。」禹曰：「兪！乃言底可績。」
鄭富
同考試官教諭文批：宛然虞廷矢謨氣象。
考試官學正孫批：雋永。
考試官教授張批：精密。
大臣自信其謨之有用，同列深與其謨之有成。夫知人安民之謨，治道備矣。大臣自信，而同列復深與之，得無引君之意哉？昔皐陶陳謨，而終之以此，若曰：進言本乎不欺，用言貴乎致治。如所謂迪德，以盡知人安民之事，六者有翕受敷施之義、無教無曠之戒焉，有典禮命討之辨、聰明明畏之嚴焉。吾爲此言，豈徒華國而已？蓋言者，行之表也。言之無文，行弗遠矣，安望其底行邪？玆則取諸人，必本諸己，秩秩然皆協乎良圖；慎厥事，惟旣厥心，鑿鑿乎不違于國是。以官俊乂，綽有持循；以惠黎元，殆無牴牾。蓋不徒托之
translation_en:
…what can be said of those who belittle our Changes by treating it merely as a book of divination?
Book of Documents
“My words accord with what is right and can be put into practice.” Yu said: “Yes! Your words, when put into practice, can bring accomplishment.”
Zheng Fu
Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: “It vividly conveys the atmosphere of presenting counsels at the court of Shun.”
Comment by Examiner Sun, Schoolmaster: “Rich in lasting significance.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: “Refined and meticulous.”
A great minister trusts that his counsels are useful, and his colleague warmly endorses their capacity to produce results. Counsels concerning the discernment of men and the securing of the people’s peace encompass the whole way of government. When the great minister trusts in them and his colleague warmly endorses them, might there not be an intention to guide their ruler?
Long ago, Gao Yao presented his counsels and concluded with these words. It was as though he said: “Offering advice rests upon freedom from deception; the value of applying advice lies in achieving good government. As for what is called following virtue, thereby fully carrying out the tasks of discerning men and securing the people’s peace, these six matters embody the principle of receiving all and extending benefits widely, and the admonition against ‘no instruction’ [?] and neglect. They include distinctions concerning established norms, rites, appointments, and punishments, and the strict requirements of perceptive hearing and sight, manifest authority, and awe.
“When I offer these words, is it merely to adorn the state? Words are the outward expression of conduct. Without literary form, words do not travel far: how then could one expect them to be put into practice? Here, what one takes from others must be rooted in oneself, so that everything accords, in due order, with sound plans. In attending carefully to affairs, one must fully exert one’s mind, so that one assuredly does not depart from what is right for the state. In appointing outstanding and capable men to office, there is ample guidance to follow; in benefiting the common people, there is scarcely any conflict. For these counsels are not merely committed to…”

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
空言眞可見之行事惠而可行者也其能弗聽
乎哉皐陶自信如此禹聞而俞之以爲大言無
當則博而寡要行其所知則進而有功乃若迪
德以行知人安民之事云者脩齊治平由此而
推兢業敬畏由此而達汝爲是言匪徒足聞而
已彼績者言之徵也善而有徵可信從矣不能
保其厎績邪吾知出乎身者加乎民百僚以之
而能敘發乎邇者要諸遠黎民於是乎允懷在
朝足以收其凝之績在野足以致從治之休蓋
===
弗爲則胡成試之而必效言之厎績者也而可
弗庸哉大禹之深與又如此此無他皐陶之自
信不知善之在己也大禹之深與不知善之在
人也其要歸于勉君而已古人同心之義如是
夫抑有虞之時元愷登庸鰥寡無蓋知人安民
之事盡之矣而胡皐陶之喋喋邪蓋臣子忠愛
之至不以君之已聖而弗言而聖人從諫之心
亦不以世之極治而弗納交相勉勵所以共成
雍熈之盛也視彼世未小康而君臣動色相賀
punctuated:
空言，眞可見之行事，惠而可行者也，其能弗聽乎哉？皐陶自信如此。禹聞而俞之，以爲大言無當，則博而寡要；行其所知，則進而有功。乃若迪德以行知人安民之事云者，脩齊治平由此而推，兢業敬畏由此而達。汝爲是言，匪徒足聞而已。彼績者，言之徵也。善而有徵，可信從矣，不能保其厎績邪？吾知出乎身者加乎民，百僚以之而能敘；發乎邇者要諸遠，黎民於是乎允懷。在朝足以收其凝之績，在野足以致從治之休。蓋弗爲則胡成？試之而必效，言之厎績者也，而可弗庸哉？大禹之深與又如此。
此無他，皐陶之自信，不知善之在己也；大禹之深與，不知善之在人也。其要歸于勉君而已，古人同心之義如是夫！抑有虞之時，元愷登庸，鰥寡無蓋，知人安民之事盡之矣，而胡皐陶之喋喋邪？蓋臣子忠愛之至，不以君之已聖而弗言；而聖人從諫之心，亦不以世之極治而弗納。交相勉勵，所以共成雍熈之盛也。視彼世未小康而君臣動色相賀
translation_en:
…empty words: these principles can truly be manifested in action; they are beneficial and practicable. How could one fail to heed them? Such was Gao Yao’s confidence. Yu heard him and assented, considering that grand pronouncements without practical relevance are wide-ranging but lack essentials, whereas putting what one knows into practice brings progress and achievement. As for following virtue in order to recognize worthy men and bring peace to the people, self-cultivation, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world all extend from this; vigilance, conscientiousness, reverence, and awe all find expression through it. These words of yours are more than merely worth hearing. Accomplishments are the verification of words. When words are good and verifiable, they deserve trust and compliance. Can one not be assured that they will yield results? I know that what proceeds from one’s own person reaches the people, enabling the hundred officials to take their proper places; what begins nearby is brought to bear upon those far away, so that the common people truly turn to their ruler. At court, this suffices to achieve firm governance; among the people, it suffices to bring about the blessings of obedience to that governance. For how can anything be accomplished without action? Put these words to the test, and they will surely prove effective: they are words that yield results. How could one fail to employ them? Such, in turn, was the depth of the Great Yu’s approval.
There was no other reason for this: in his confidence, Gao Yao was unconscious of goodness as belonging to himself; in his profound approval, the Great Yu was unconscious of goodness as belonging to another. Their essential purpose was simply to encourage their ruler. Such was the meaning of the ancients’ unity of purpose! Yet in the time of Youyu, the Eight Excellent Ones and Eight Good Ones had been raised to office, and no widower or widow remained overlooked. The work of recognizing worthy men and bringing peace to the people had been fully accomplished. Why, then, did Gao Yao speak at such length? In their utmost loyalty and affection, ministers do not refrain from speaking merely because their ruler is already a sage; nor does the sage, with his readiness to accept remonstrance, refuse it merely because the age has attained perfect order. Through mutual encouragement, they together brought about the flourishing of harmony and peace. Compare this with those whose age has not yet attained even modest tranquillity, yet whose ruler and ministers visibly brighten as they congratulate one another…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
者何如哉噫有天下者可以觀矣
人之有能有為使羞其行而邦其昌
葉春澤
同考試官教諭文批發揮使字昌字處入肯綮
考試官學正孫批有思致
考試官教授張批不浮
臣有善而進之其國利矣夫善人國之紀也因
其人而進之於國豈小補哉箕子衍皇極以詔
武王及此蓋謂治亂之源係於庶官而造就之
===
術存乎人主不特民焉爾也是故自天授之之
謂能其才智足稱也臣固有有能者矣不曰彼
能是是亦可也自人作之之謂為其施設可觀
也臣亦有有為者矣不曰彼善是是亦足也人
君於此有機焉迎而覺之以盡鼓舞之神有權
焉舉而運之以盡變通之利使其敦而不怠自
致曲而充之以成其全能也作之不已由一偏
而進之以妙其百為也是則有以納之于極矣
豈無益於人國哉蓋賢以造而成則國以賢而
punctuated:
者何如哉？噫！有天下者可以觀矣。

人之有能有為，使羞其行，而邦其昌。
葉春澤

同考試官教諭文批：發揮使字、昌字處入肯綮。
考試官學正孫批：有思致。
考試官教授張批：不浮。

臣有善而進之，其國利矣。夫善人，國之紀也。因其人而進之於國，豈小補哉？箕子衍皇極以詔武王，及此，蓋謂治亂之源係於庶官，而造就之術存乎人主，不特民焉爾也。是故自天授之之謂能，其才智足稱也，臣固有有能者矣。不曰「彼能是，是亦可也」。自人作之之謂為，其施設可觀也，臣亦有有為者矣。不曰「彼善是，是亦足也」。人君於此有機焉，迎而覺之，以盡鼓舞之神；有權焉，舉而運之，以盡變通之利。使其敦而不怠，自致曲而充之，以成其全能也；作之不已，由一偏而進之，以妙其百為也。是則有以納之于極矣，豈無益於人國哉？蓋賢以造而成，則國以賢而
translation_en:
…how do they compare? Ah! Those who possess All-under-Heaven may take a lesson from this.

“When men have ability and accomplishment, cause them to advance in their conduct, and your state will flourish.”
Ye Chunze

Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: His exposition of the words “cause” and “flourish” gets to the heart of the matter.
Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: Shows thoughtful insight.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: Not superficial.

When ministers possess good qualities and are advanced, their state benefits. Good men are the guiding framework of a state. If, taking account of their qualities, one advances them in the state’s service, can the benefit be small? When Jizi expounded the Sovereign’s Ultimate Standard to instruct King Wu, he addressed this point. His meaning was that the source of order and disorder lies with the officials, while the means of forming and perfecting them rests with the ruler. His concern was not confined to the common people.

Thus, what Heaven endows is called “ability”: a man’s talent and intelligence merit praise. Among ministers there certainly are men of ability. The ruler must not say, “He can do this; this will suffice.” What a person brings about through his own efforts is called “accomplishment”: his undertakings and arrangements deserve attention. Among ministers there are also men of accomplishment. The ruler must not say, “He is good at this; this is enough.”

Here the ruler has opportunities: he must recognize them as they arise, fully exercising his wondrous power to inspire and encourage. He has discretionary authority: he must bring it into play, fully realizing the benefits of adapting to circumstances. He must cause these men to apply themselves earnestly and without slackening, extending what they have developed in a particular respect until their abilities reach full development. He must rouse them unceasingly, advancing them beyond a single specialty until they attain excellence in their many undertakings. In this way he can bring them into accord with the Ultimate Standard. How could this fail to benefit a ruler’s state? For worthy men are perfected through cultivation, and the state, through worthy men…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
實由是拔茅彙征旣足以啓其亨泰之會而含
章時發又足以收其明作之功能者位事爲者
宣力休明之治恒必由之矣入使治焉出使長
焉靈長之慶終將賴之矣惟邦之昌豈非其理
有必至者哉是則國保於賢而賢成於君是二
者未始不相須也建極者盍亦惟是之務乎抑
考傳有之曰不有君子其能國乎國資賢也而
養賢及民聖人於頤重焉賢資養也然則養而
後善不旣淺乎豪傑之士無文王猶興是知皇
===
極羞行之說爲中人設也雖然我入自外室人
交徧謫我則無以安位而行志故爲臣者固不
可以中人自待人君其亦無薄於待士而使室
人之交謫哉
詩
瞻彼洛矣維水泱泱君子至止福祿旣同
君子萬年保其家邦
楊子充
同考試官敎諭劉 批 說詩人頌美之意稱其情矣
punctuated:
實。由是拔茅彙征，旣足以啓其亨泰之會；而含章時發，又足以收其明作之功。能者位事，爲者宣力，休明之治恒必由之矣。入使治焉，出使長焉，靈長之慶終將賴之矣。惟邦之昌，豈非其理有必至者哉？是則國保於賢，而賢成於君，是二者未始不相須也。建極者盍亦惟是之務乎？抑考傳有之，曰：「不有君子，其能國乎？」國資賢也。而養賢及民，聖人於頤重焉，賢資養也。然則養而後善，不旣淺乎？豪傑之士，無文王猶興，是知皇極羞行之說爲中人設也。雖然，「我入自外，室人交徧謫我」，則無以安位而行志。故爲臣者固不可以中人自待，人君其亦無薄於待士，而使室人之交謫哉！

詩
瞻彼洛矣，維水泱泱。君子至止，福祿旣同。君子萬年，保其家邦。
楊子充
同考試官敎諭劉 批：說詩人頌美之意，稱其情矣。
translation_en:
…is made substantial. Thus, when worthy men advance together, like clumps of thatch pulled up with their intertwined roots, this suffices to open an auspicious occasion of flourishing peace. When they hold their excellence within and reveal it at the proper time, this also suffices to achieve the work of enlightened action. The capable occupy offices and attend to affairs; those who accomplish things exert their strength in service. Auspicious and enlightened government must always proceed from this. Employed at court, they govern; sent out, they preside over others. The blessings of enduring rule will ultimately depend upon them. Is the flourishing of the state not an inevitable consequence of this principle? Thus the state is preserved by worthy men, and worthy men are brought to fulfillment by the ruler: these two have never ceased to depend upon each other. Should not those who establish the supreme standard devote themselves to this task?

Moreover, examining the commentary, we find it said: “Without gentlemen, could one maintain a state?” The state depends upon worthy men. As for nourishing the worthy and extending nourishment to the people, the sage places great weight upon this in the hexagram Nourishment: worthy men depend upon nurture. Yet is it not rather shallow to become good only after being nurtured? Men of outstanding ability rise even without a King Wen. We thus know that the teaching in the “Supreme Standard” concerning presenting good conduct is intended for men of middling capacity. Nevertheless, “When I come in from outside, those of my household all join in reproaching me”: in such circumstances, one cannot remain secure in office and carry out one’s aspirations. Thus, those who serve as ministers certainly must not regard themselves as merely men of middling capacity; yet should not the ruler likewise refrain from treating scholars so poorly that their households join in reproaching them?

Book of Odes

Look upon the Luo River,
Its waters broad and deep.
The lord has arrived;
Blessings and emoluments have gathered together.
May the lord live ten thousand years,
Preserving his house and state.

Yang Zichong

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: His explanation of the poet’s intention to praise fittingly conveys the poet’s feelings.

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭崔批雅義之最優者
考試官學正孫批雅麗而歸於理
考試官教授張批詞義明暢
周臣美天子涖天下之中有以隆大慶而永大
業也甚矣有天下者貴圖大也周天子涖東都
而會朝講武其隆福而保業也宜哉此諸侯所
以美之而有是詩意蓋謂我周宅是鎬京旣已
慮天下之遠矣而營玆洛邑則又示天下以公
也然豈無所於慮而不足以享雍熈悠久之盛
===
哉瞻彼洛矣卜之瀍澗之間維水泱泱有此都
城之勝天下中而四方之道里均也新邑壯而
一代之典刑在焉今我君子至此東都端萬乘
以朝諸侯作六師而講武事百辟承式王章昭
也國家閒暇于以揚厲乎皇威人心協而君道
泰世旣治平矣世之治者福之臻也萬國來王
侯度飭也宇宙太和于以布昭乎聖武體統正
而朝廷尊時稱乂安矣時之安者祿之萃也福
祿旣同其今日東都之足徵乎然我君子可以
punctuated:
同考試官教諭崔批：雅義之最優者。
考試官學正孫批：雅麗而歸於理。
考試官教授張批：詞義明暢。
周臣美天子涖天下之中，有以隆大慶而永大業也。甚矣，有天下者貴圖大也！周天子涖東都而會朝講武，其隆福而保業也宜哉！此諸侯所以美之而有是詩。意蓋謂我周宅是鎬京，旣已慮天下之遠矣；而營玆洛邑，則又示天下以公也。然豈無所於慮而不足以享雍熈悠久之盛哉？瞻彼洛矣，卜之瀍澗之間；維水泱泱，有此都城之勝。天下中而四方之道里均也，新邑壯而一代之典刑在焉。今我君子至此東都，端萬乘以朝諸侯，作六師而講武事。百辟承式，王章昭也；國家閒暇，于以揚厲乎皇威。人心協而君道泰，世旣治平矣。世之治者，福之臻也。萬國來王，侯度飭也；宇宙太和，于以布昭乎聖武。體統正而朝廷尊，時稱乂安矣。時之安者，祿之萃也。福祿旣同，其今日東都之足徵乎！然我君子可以
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor, comments: “Among the finest in its exposition of the meaning of the Court Hymns.”
Examiner Sun, School Instructor, comments: “Elegant and polished, yet grounded in principle.”
Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “Its language and meaning are clear and fluent.”
A minister of Zhou praises the Son of Heaven for coming to the center of All-under-Heaven, thereby increasing his great blessings and perpetuating his great undertaking. How essential it is for one who possesses All-under-Heaven to plan on a grand scale! The Son of Heaven of Zhou comes to the Eastern Capital to hold court assemblies and conduct military exercises. How fitting that he should thereby increase his blessings and preserve his undertaking! This is why the feudal lords praise him in this poem. Its meaning is, broadly, as follows: Our Zhou established its residence at Haojing, already taking thought for the distant reaches of All-under-Heaven; by building this city of Luoyi, it further demonstrated its impartiality to the realm. Could it, then, have made no provision and lack the means to enjoy enduring prosperity in harmony and peace [?]?
“Look upon that Luo!” The site was chosen by divination between the Chan and Jian rivers. “Its waters are vast”: such is the splendid setting of this capital. It lies at the center of All-under-Heaven, with equal traveling distances from the four quarters. The new city is magnificent, and within it reside the institutions and models of the dynasty. Now our lord has come to this Eastern Capital. In the dignity of the ruler of ten thousand chariots, he receives the feudal lords at court; he musters the Six Armies and conducts military exercises. The many lords conform to his models, and royal statutes shine forth. The state enjoys tranquility, and he uses this occasion to display imperial might. The people’s hearts are united, the ruler’s way proceeds unhindered, and the age has attained order and peace. The good order of the age is the arrival of blessings. The myriad states come to acknowledge their king, and the rules governing the feudal lords are duly observed. All beneath heaven is in supreme harmony, and he uses this occasion to make manifest his sagely martial prowess. The hierarchy is properly ordered and the court honored: these times may be called peaceful and well governed. The peace of the times is the gathering of emoluments. “Blessings and emoluments have come together”: surely the Eastern Capital today provides ample proof of this! Yet our lord can …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
卜世備有事於無事之日謹防患於思患之先
安不忘危則其安必久是殆於萬斯年維繫人
心固結而不可解合四海以為家者永長存也
治不忘亂則其治必長蓋將萬有千歲培植國
本安固而不可摇奠千里之邦畿者無終極也
永保家邦其東都作事之所留乎是則周王之
有天下惟其無所恃而後有所保有道之長不
偶然也諸臣詠歌及此豈溢美哉考之人君之
有天下文武並用長久之術也周諸侯以天子
===
之講武而謂足以保天下於萬年豈固無賴於
文歟蓋治至成康文有餘矣武不足也其勢將
趨於弱故老成長慮不得已於洛邑之詠歌也
噫有周傳世三十歷年八百亦曰有道以致之
日就月將學有緝熙于光明
陳堦
同考試官教諭劉批說成王勉學處足破羣疑
同考試官教諭崔批緝熙之學此亦可求
考試官學正孫批意見不羣
punctuated:
卜世，備有事於無事之日，謹防患於思患之先。安不忘危，則其安必久，是殆於萬斯年，維繫人心，固結而不可解，合四海以為家者永長存也。治不忘亂，則其治必長，蓋將萬有千歲，培植國本，安固而不可摇，奠千里之邦畿者無終極也。永保家邦，其東都作事之所留乎？是則周王之有天下，惟其無所恃而後有所保，有道之長不偶然也。諸臣詠歌及此，豈溢美哉？考之人君之有天下，文武並用，長久之術也。周諸侯以天子之講武而謂足以保天下於萬年，豈固無賴於文歟？蓋治至成康，文有餘矣，武不足也，其勢將趨於弱，故老成長慮，不得已於洛邑之詠歌也。噫！有周傳世三十，歷年八百，亦曰有道以致之。

日就月將，學有緝熙于光明。
陳堦

同考試官教諭劉批：說成王勉學處，足破羣疑。
同考試官教諭崔批：緝熙之學，此亦可求。
考試官學正孫批：意見不羣。
translation_en:
…foretell the dynasty’s duration, prepare for troubled times in days without trouble, and take care to prevent calamities even before thoughts of them arise. If, in peace, one does not forget danger, that peace will surely endure. Thus, perhaps for ten thousand years, the people’s hearts will remain bound together, firmly united beyond dissolution, and the house that embraces all within the Four Seas as one family will endure forever. If, in orderly times, one does not forget disorder, that order will surely last. Thus, for ten thousand and a thousand years, the foundations of the state will be nurtured, secure and unshakable, and the establishment of the royal domain extending a thousand li will have no end. Might the perpetual preservation of the ruling house and its realm be the lasting legacy [?] of the undertakings at the eastern capital? Thus, the Zhou king possessed all under Heaven: only by relying on nothing as a guarantee could he secure its preservation. The longevity of a dynasty possessing the Way is no accident. When the ministers’ songs of praise reached this point, could they have been excessive?

Considering how rulers possess all under Heaven, the joint employment of civil and military means is the art of enduring rule. The lords of Zhou regarded the Son of Heaven’s military exercises as sufficient to preserve all under Heaven for ten thousand years. Could they really have considered civil governance unnecessary? By the reigns of Kings Cheng and Kang, civil governance was abundant, but military preparedness was inadequate. The tendency was toward weakness. Thus, seasoned elders, taking the long view, could not refrain from expressing their concerns in songs at Luoyi. Ah! Zhou transmitted its rule through thirty generations and endured for eight hundred years. We may indeed say that it achieved this through possessing the Way.

“Advancing daily and progressing monthly, through learning one continues toward ever greater brightness.”
Chen Jie

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, an Instructor: “The explanation of King Cheng’s efforts to encourage himself in learning is sufficient to dispel the many doubts.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Cui, an Instructor: “Here, too, one may seek the learning that leads to continuous illumination.”
Comment by Examiner Sun, a School Instructor: “The insight is uncommon.”

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授張批立說精當
周王答羣臣欲勉於學以至乎其極也蓋德至
于明聖學之極功也周王務此其求所以能敬
乎昔成王旣述羣臣之戒而乃自爲答臣之言
意蓋曰帝王之敬莫大於格天聖賢之學恒在
於明德吾願學焉而入敬也其將何脩而庶幾
乎故夫吾心之德或有時而昏則脩德之功當
以時而敏苟一日不學則蔽固日深矣是必遜
乃志焉省察於意念之發保夜氣於旦晝之梏
===
亡而使日有所就弗就弗已也一月不學則昏
昧月滋矣是必殫厥心焉體驗乎善端之萌充
道心於或月之一至而使月有所將弗將弗措
也日新不已始終典于學勉勉乎緝而熈之閑
其邪也而必欲有以存其誠月計有餘顯微無
所間亹亹乎續而明之克乎己也而必欲有以
復乎禮由是眞積力久而渣滓自融一疵不存
萬理明盡心體復虛靈之初洞然光明斯可矣
積學功至而邪穢自化一理渾然萬欲淨盡性
punctuated:
考試官敎授張批：立說精當。

周王答羣臣，欲勉於學以至乎其極也。蓋德至于明，聖學之極功也。周王務此，其求所以能敬乎？昔成王旣述羣臣之戒，而乃自爲答臣之言，意蓋曰：帝王之敬，莫大於格天；聖賢之學，恒在於明德。吾願學焉而入敬也，其將何脩而庶幾乎？故夫吾心之德，或有時而昏，則脩德之功，當以時而敏。苟一日不學，則蔽固日深矣。是必遜乃志焉，省察於意念之發，保夜氣於旦晝之梏亡，而使日有所就，弗就弗已也。一月不學，則昏昧月滋矣。是必殫厥心焉，體驗乎善端之萌，充道心於或月之一至，而使月有所將，弗將弗措也。日新不已，始終典于學，勉勉乎緝而熈之，閑其邪也，而必欲有以存其誠；月計有餘，顯微無所間，亹亹乎續而明之，克乎己也，而必欲有以復乎禮。由是眞積力久，而渣滓自融，一疵不存，萬理明盡，心體復虛靈之初，洞然光明，斯可矣。積學功至，而邪穢自化，一理渾然，萬欲淨盡，性
translation_en:
Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “The argument is precisely and aptly formulated.”

In replying to his assembled ministers, the king of Zhou wished to exert himself in learning so as to reach its highest attainment. For bringing virtue to illumination is the ultimate achievement of sagely learning. In pursuing this, was the king of Zhou seeking the means to practice reverence? Having recounted his ministers’ admonitions, King Cheng then formulated his own reply to them. His meaning was approximately this: For emperors and kings, nothing in the practice of reverence is greater than reaching Heaven; the learning of sages and worthies always lies in illuminating virtue. I wish to learn and thereby enter into reverence. What, then, must I cultivate to approach it?

If the virtue of my heart sometimes becomes obscured, my efforts to cultivate virtue must be correspondingly diligent. If I fail to learn for a single day, my obscuration and obstinacy will deepen daily. I must therefore make my resolve humble, scrutinize thoughts and intentions as they arise, and preserve the vital energy nurtured at night against its fettering and destruction during the day. Thus I must make some attainment each day, never stopping until I have done so. If I fail to learn for a month, my benightedness will increase month by month. I must therefore devote my whole heart to the task, experience and examine the first stirrings of goodness, and expand the moral mind when it appears perhaps only once a month. Thus I must make some advance each month, never setting the task aside until I have advanced.

Renewing myself daily without cease, I must consistently attend to learning from beginning to end, diligently continuing and brightening it, guarding against perversity so that I may preserve sincerity. Reckoning my progress by the month, I must have a surplus of achievement, with no gap between the manifest and the hidden, tirelessly continuing and illuminating my learning, overcoming the self so that I may return to ritual propriety. Through this, genuine accumulation and sustained effort will cause the dross to dissolve of itself. Not one flaw will remain; the myriad principles will be fully illuminated. The substance of the heart will recover its original emptiness and spiritual responsiveness, becoming thoroughly luminous: only then will it suffice. When accumulated learning reaches its full achievement, perversity and impurity will transform of themselves. The single principle will be whole and undivided, the myriad desires entirely cleansed away, and the nature…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
天昭湛一之眞瑩然純明斯止矣蓋至是而吾
德已明有以得聖人之心學吾學已至有以收
作聖之全功矣敬其可能而爾羣臣之戒可無
負哉吁勉學如成王亦何敬之不可及而天命
之不可保乎抑論敬者聖學傳心之要帝王祈
天永命之本也周之文武體道立極而創業垂
統率皆有得乎此成王幼冲踐阼而有臣如周
召者惓惓以皇自敬德王敬作所交相陳告誠
慮其忝厥祖父而不保天下固忠愛之至也然
===
則此詩之作殆其時乎厥後成王知勉於敬而
基命宥密享有道之長爲成周令主是其學問
之力不可誣也而周召輔相之功於是爲大
春秋
冬十有一月諸侯盟于扈文公十五年晉
人齊人宋人衞人鄭人曹人莒人邾人
滕人薛人杞人小邾人會于澶淵宋災
故襄公三十年秋季孫意如會晉韓起
齊國弱宋華亥衞北宮佗鄭罕虎曹人
punctuated:
天昭湛一之眞，瑩然純明斯止矣。蓋至是而吾德已明，有以得聖人之心學；吾學已至，有以收作聖之全功矣。「敬其可能」，而爾羣臣之戒可無負哉！吁！勉學如成王，亦何敬之不可及，而天命之不可保乎？抑論敬者，聖學傳心之要，帝王祈天永命之本也。周之文武，體道立極，而創業垂統，率皆有得乎此。成王幼冲踐阼，而有臣如周召者，惓惓以「皇自敬德」、「王敬作所」交相陳告，誠慮其忝厥祖父而不保天下，固忠愛之至也。然則此詩之作，殆其時乎？厥後成王知勉於敬，而基命宥密，享有道之長，爲成周令主，是其學問之力不可誣也，而周召輔相之功於是爲大。
春秋
冬十有一月，諸侯盟于扈。文公十五年。晉人、齊人、宋人、衞人、鄭人、曹人、莒人、邾人、滕人、薛人、杞人、小邾人會于澶淵，宋災故。襄公三十年。秋，季孫意如會晉韓起、齊國弱、宋華亥、衞北宮佗、鄭罕虎、曹人
translation_en:
…the Heaven-endowed nature reveals its true, tranquil unity; only when it shines with pure clarity does the work reach its end. At this point, my virtue has been made bright, enabling me to grasp the sages’ learning of the mind; my learning has reached its culmination, enabling me to accomplish fully the work of becoming a sage. “Reverence—may I attain it”: can I then avoid disappointing the admonitions of you, my assembled ministers? Ah! If one strives at learning as King Cheng did, how could reverence be unattainable or Heaven’s mandate impossible to preserve?
Now reverence is the essential means by which the learning of the sages transmits the understanding of the mind, and the foundation upon which emperors and kings petition Heaven to prolong their mandate. Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou embodied the Way and established the supreme standard, founding their enterprise and bequeathing their succession: in all this, they had grasped this principle. King Cheng ascended the throne while still a child. Ministers such as the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao earnestly took turns admonishing him: “Greatly revere your own virtue,” and “Let the king reverently establish his position.” They truly feared that he might disgrace his grandfather and father and fail to preserve the realm. This was indeed the utmost loyalty and affection. Was it not, then, at approximately this time that this poem was composed?
Thereafter King Cheng understood that he must strive for reverence. He established his mandate in profound tranquillity, long enjoyed the benefits of possessing the Way, and became an excellent ruler of Zhou. The efficacy of his learning cannot be denied; and herein lay the greatness of the assistance rendered by the Dukes of Zhou and Shao.

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
杞人于厥憖昭公十一年
趙恒
同考試官教諭汪批得聖人立法嚴恕之意
考試官學正孫批森整
考試官教授張批嚴謹
列國討罪恤患之事不同春秋原情示法之旨
亦異于以見扈之盟諸侯昧於仁澶淵之會諸
大夫昧於智而會厥憖之諸國則無惡也春秋
得不各致意於書法間哉嘗聞仁以長人諸侯
===
職也孰意世入春秋昧此者有如盟扈之諸侯
邪夫仁莫大於義利之辨當是時商人弑君諸
侯亦既形之載書矣九伐之法載在周官義莫
正焉者彼齊人亂賊之賂何足以易天下之大
義而竟為是落落邪其不仁亦甚矣經故畧八
國而不序也又聞智以帥人大夫職也孰意世
入春秋昧此者有如會澶淵之諸大夫邪夫智
莫大於輕重之別當是時蔡般弑父諸大夫亦
既聞其訃告矣三綱淪絕禽獸逼人事莫重焉
punctuated:
杞人于厥憖。昭公十一年。
趙恒。
同考試官教諭汪批：得聖人立法嚴恕之意。
考試官學正孫批：森整。
考試官教授張批：嚴謹。
列國討罪恤患之事不同，《春秋》原情示法之旨亦異。于以見扈之盟，諸侯昧於仁；澶淵之會，諸大夫昧於智；而會厥憖之諸國，則無惡也。《春秋》得不各致意於書法間哉？嘗聞仁以長人，諸侯職也。孰意世入春秋，昧此者有如盟扈之諸侯邪？夫仁莫大於義利之辨。當是時，商人弑君，諸侯亦既形之載書矣。九伐之法，載在《周官》，義莫正焉者。彼齊人亂賊之賂，何足以易天下之大義，而竟為是落落邪？其不仁亦甚矣！經故畧八國而不序也。又聞智以帥人，大夫職也。孰意世入春秋，昧此者有如會澶淵之諸大夫邪？夫智莫大於輕重之別。當是時，蔡般弑父，諸大夫亦既聞其訃告矣。三綱淪絕，禽獸逼人，事莫重焉
translation_en:
…and men of Qi at Jueyin. Eleventh year of Duke Zhao.
Zhao Heng.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: He grasps the Sage’s intent in establishing standards of judgment with both rigor and forbearance.
Comment by Examiner Sun, Director of Studies: Imposing and orderly.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: Rigorous and meticulous.
The affairs in which the various states punished wrongdoing and relieved distress differed, and so too did the purposes of the Spring and Autumn Annals in considering motives and setting forth standards of judgment. Thus we see that at the covenant at Hu, the feudal lords failed to understand benevolence; at the meeting at Chanyuan, the grandees failed to understand wisdom; but the states that met at Jueyin were without fault. Could the Spring and Autumn Annals fail to convey its judgment of each through its manner of recording them?
I have heard that leading others through benevolence is the duty of feudal lords. Who would have imagined that, as the age entered the Spring and Autumn period, there would be lords as ignorant of this as those who covenanted at Hu? In benevolence, nothing is more important than distinguishing righteousness from personal gain. At that time, Shangren had murdered his ruler, and the feudal lords had already set this down in the covenant document. The rules for the nine kinds of punitive expedition are recorded in the Offices of Zhou; no principle of righteousness could be more correct. How could bribes from those rebels and regicides of Qi suffice to overturn the great righteousness binding all under Heaven, so that the lords ultimately became so indifferent? Their lack of benevolence was indeed extreme! Thus the Classic omits the names of the eight states rather than listing them in order.
I have also heard that guiding others through wisdom is the duty of grandees. Who would have imagined that, as the age entered the Spring and Autumn period, there would be grandees as ignorant of this as those who met at Chanyuan? In wisdom, nothing is more important than distinguishing the weighty from the trivial. At that time, Ban of Cai had murdered his father, and the grandees had already received the notification of his death. The Three Bonds had collapsed and been severed, and the ways of beasts were encroaching upon humanity. No matter could be graver…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
著彼宋人不戒之災何足以勤諸國之大會而
徒爲是僕僕邪其不智亦甚矣經故人諸大夫
而諱魯也乃若厥愁有會諸侯謀蔡難也狐父
無功晉之不能甚矣經又曷爲諸國猶序而大
夫無貶乎誠以君子之所自盡者心也彼其自
遠而會遣使以請則諸侯救蔡之心固有不可
誣者天下之不可强者力也要之蔡德旣棄楚
惡方周以霸業積衰之餘其獨如之何邪夫有
其心則非昧輕重之別比矣格於力則非亡義
===
利之分比矣經所以諸國猶序而大夫無貶者
以此嗟夫君臣大分也夷夏大防也春秋之世
亂賊不討可罪矣尤有會以定位推以主盟如
齊晉諸國獨何心歟猾夏不能救可恕矣尤有
資以報怨乘以肆虐如魯齊諸國又何心歟是
故春秋之所以作也故曰春秋謹華夏之辨又
曰春秋嚴亂賊之黨
歸邾子益于邾 齊人歸讙及闡〔俱哀公八年〕
punctuated:
著，彼宋人不戒之災，何足以勤諸國之大會，而徒爲是僕僕邪？其不智亦甚矣！經故人諸大夫而諱魯也。乃若厥愁有會，諸侯謀蔡難也。狐父無功，晉之不能甚矣。經又曷爲諸國猶序，而大夫無貶乎？誠以君子之所自盡者，心也。彼其自遠而會，遣使以請，則諸侯救蔡之心，固有不可誣者。天下之不可强者，力也。要之，蔡德旣棄，楚惡方周，以霸業積衰之餘，其獨如之何邪？夫有其心，則非昧輕重之別比矣；格於力，則非亡義利之分比矣。經所以諸國猶序而大夫無貶者，以此。
嗟夫！君臣，大分也；夷夏，大防也。春秋之世，亂賊不討，可罪矣；尤有會以定位，推以主盟，如齊晉諸國，獨何心歟？猾夏不能救，可恕矣；尤有資以報怨，乘以肆虐，如魯齊諸國，又何心歟？是故《春秋》之所以作也。故曰：「《春秋》謹華夏之辨。」又曰：「《春秋》嚴亂賊之黨。」
歸邾子益于邾。齊人歸讙及闡。〔俱哀公八年〕
translation_en:
…[?] How could the calamity brought upon the people of Song by their lack of precautions warrant troubling the various states with a great assembly, merely to bustle about in this way? Their lack of wisdom was extreme! The Classic therefore calls the grandees merely “men” and conceals Lu’s involvement. As for the meeting at Juechou [?], the feudal lords were deliberating over Cai’s plight. That nothing was accomplished at Hufu shows the extreme incapacity of Jin. Why, then, does the Classic still list the states in order and refrain from disparaging their grandees? It is because the gentleman can fully exert himself in his intentions. They came from afar to assemble and dispatched an envoy to make a request: the feudal lords’ intention to rescue Cai certainly cannot be denied. Yet power is something that cannot be forced. In the end, Cai’s virtue had already been forsaken [?], while Chu’s wickedness was reaching its full extent. With the hegemony long in decline, what could Jin alone do about it? Having such intentions, they cannot be compared to those who fail to distinguish the weighty from the trivial; constrained by their power, they cannot be compared to those who abandon the distinction between righteousness and profit. This is why the Classic still lists the states in order and does not disparage the grandees.
Alas! Between ruler and minister lies a fundamental distinction of status; between the Yi and the Xia lies a fundamental boundary. In the age of the Spring and Autumn Annals, failure to punish rebels and regicides was culpable enough. Yet states such as Qi and Jin went further, assembling to confirm their positions and advancing them to preside over covenants. What could their intentions have been? Inability to rescue the Xia from incursions might be excused. Yet states such as Lu and Qi went further, providing assistance for the settling of grudges and exploiting the circumstances to unleash violence. What, again, could their intentions have been? These are the reasons the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed. Thus it is said: “The Spring and Autumn Annals carefully maintains the distinction concerning the Hua and Xia.” It is also said: “The Spring and Autumn Annals sternly condemns the accomplices of rebels and regicides.”
“Yi, Viscount of Zhu, was returned to Zhu.” “The men of Qi returned Huan and Chan.” 〔Both entries are from the eighth year of Duke Ai.〕

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
陳暹
同考試官教諭汪批二歸字意發明殆盡是蓋
邃於經學者
考試官學正孫批有斷制
考試官教授張批合旨
春秋始因望國釋君而著其改過之美繼卽大
國歸地以顯其改過之美甚矣聖人大改過也
觀於邾益讙闡之歸而致意於齊魯者可見矣
且邾益之歸孰歸之魯哀悔執之之非而歸之
===
也夫人不貴於無過而貴於改過前此邾益之
執出於無故揆之以大字小之仁莫不爲魯咎
者乃今哀也知其爲過復歸之于邾焉邾也無
君而有君益也無國而有國是則今日之得足
以掩前日之失矣噫自九伐之法廢而社稷之
奉無常塗山玉帛之君没齒於强大之庭而不
返者亦多矣改過不吝何幸於魯哀見之經書
曰歸順詞也而魯哀改過之美從可見矣若讙
闡之歸孰歸之齊悼感歸益之義而歸之也夫
punctuated:
陳暹

同考試官教諭汪批：二歸字意發明殆盡，是蓋邃於經學者。
考試官學正孫批：有斷制。
考試官教授張批：合旨。

春秋始因望國釋君而著其改過之美，繼卽大國歸地以顯其改過之美。甚矣，聖人大改過也！觀於邾益、讙闡之歸，而致意於齊魯者，可見矣。且邾益之歸，孰歸之？魯哀悔執之之非而歸之也。夫人不貴於無過，而貴於改過。前此邾益之執，出於無故，揆之以大字小之仁，莫不爲魯咎者。乃今哀也知其爲過，復歸之于邾焉。邾也無君而有君，益也無國而有國，是則今日之得足以掩前日之失矣。噫！自九伐之法廢，而社稷之奉無常，塗山玉帛之君没齒於强大之庭而不返者，亦多矣。改過不吝，何幸於魯哀見之！經書曰「歸」，順詞也，而魯哀改過之美從可見矣。若讙闡之歸，孰歸之？齊悼感歸益之義而歸之也。夫
translation_en:
Chen Xian 陳暹

Associate Examiner Wang, School Instructor, comments: “The meanings of the two occurrences of ‘return’ are elucidated almost exhaustively. This is surely someone deeply versed in classical learning.”
Examiner Sun, School Instructor, comments: “Shows decisive judgment.”
Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “Accords with the purport.”

The Spring and Autumn Annals first records an eminent state’s release of a ruler to make manifest the virtue of correcting its fault; it then records a great state’s restoration of territory to reveal the virtue of correcting its fault. How highly the Sage esteems the correction of faults! This can be seen in his attention to Qi and Lu when considering the return of Yi of Zhu and the restoration of Huan and Chan.

As for the return of Yi of Zhu, who returned him? Duke Ai of Lu regretted the wrong of having detained him and returned him. A person is esteemed not for having no faults, but for correcting them. Previously, Yi of Zhu had been detained without cause. Judged by the benevolent principle that a great state should nurture a small one, everyone held Lu at fault. Now Duke Ai recognized his error and returned him to Zhu. Zhu, having lacked a ruler, once again had one; Yi, having lacked a state, once again possessed one. Thus today’s right action was sufficient to redeem the earlier wrong.

Alas! Since the abolition of the rules governing the nine grounds for punitive expeditions, service to the altars of soil and grain has become insecure. Many rulers bearing jade and silk, like those who assembled at Tushan, have spent the remainder of their lives at the courts of powerful states without returning home. How fortunate that we see in Duke Ai of Lu a willingness to correct his fault without hesitation! The classic writes ‘returned,’ a term expressing conformity to what is right; through this, the virtue of Duke Ai’s correction of his fault becomes apparent.

As for the restoration of Huan and Chan, who restored them? Duke Dao of Qi was moved by the righteousness of returning Yi and restored them. Now …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
莫强於人心而可以誠感前此讙闡之取出於
有名揆之干戈省躬之義莫不爲魯咎者乃今
悼也因其改過復以二邑歸之焉齊無取地之
罪魯無失地之辱是齊之善亦魯之善矣噫自
百里之制紊而疆場之患日恣東周茅土之封
交手於强大之庭而不復者亦多矣自求多福
何幸於魯哀見之經書曰歸順詞也而魯哀改
過之美爲益顯矣是則觀魯之歸邿益則知人
無不可易之行觀齊之歸讙闡則知天下無不
===
可化之人此固聖人重絕人之意也歟抑又論
之負瑕之釋魯固善矣而樓臺之囚誰則致之
二邑之歸齊固善矣而南鄙之伐誰則爲之雖
然益可討也魯之歸也何尤魯可罪也齊之順
也何損是故君子求其在我而已矣
禮記
樂也者聖人之所樂也而可以善民心其
感人深其移風易俗故先王著其教焉
王一言
punctuated:
莫强於人心，而可以誠感。前此讙、闡之取，出於有名，揆之干戈省躬之義，莫不爲魯咎者。乃今悼也，因其改過，復以二邑歸之焉。齊無取地之罪，魯無失地之辱，是齊之善，亦魯之善矣。噫！自百里之制紊，而疆場之患日恣，東周茅土之封，交手於强大之庭而不復者，亦多矣。自求多福，何幸於魯哀見之！經書曰「歸」，順詞也，而魯哀改過之美爲益顯矣。是則觀魯之歸邿益，則知人無不可易之行；觀齊之歸讙、闡，則知天下無不可化之人。此固聖人重絕人之意也歟！抑又論之，負瑕之釋，魯固善矣，而樓臺之囚，誰則致之？二邑之歸，齊固善矣，而南鄙之伐，誰則爲之？雖然，益可討也，魯之歸也何尤？魯可罪也，齊之順也何損？是故君子求其在我而已矣。

禮記

樂也者，聖人之所樂也，而可以善民心。其感人深，其移風易俗，故先王著其教焉。

王一言
translation_en:
…Nothing is more unyielding than the human heart, yet sincerity can move it. The earlier seizure of Huan and Chan had a legitimate pretext. Judged by the principle that one should examine oneself when confronted by armed attack, everyone laid the blame on Lu. Now Duke Dao, responding to Lu’s correction of its fault, returned the two towns. Qi was free of the guilt of taking territory, and Lu was free of the humiliation of losing it. This good deed of Qi was also a good deed of Lu. Alas! Since the system of domains measuring one hundred li fell into disorder, troubles along the borders have grown daily more rampant. Many fiefs granted under the Eastern Zhou with the ceremonial bestowal of thatch and earth have passed into the hands of powerful courts, never to be recovered. How fortunate that in Duke Ai of Lu we see the principle of seeking abundant blessings through one’s own conduct! The classic writes “returned,” a term expressing accordance with what is right; thus the merit of Duke Ai’s correction of his fault becomes still more apparent. Observing Lu’s return of Yi of Shi [邿益, apparently Yi of Zhu, 邾益; ?], we know that no person’s conduct is incapable of change; observing Qi’s return of Huan and Chan, we know that no one in the world is beyond moral transformation. Surely this expresses the Sage’s reluctance to give up on anyone!

Yet let us consider the matter further. Lu’s release of the captive at Fuxia was certainly good, but who had brought about his imprisonment in the tower? Qi’s return of the two towns was certainly good, but who had carried out the attack on Lu’s southern border? Nevertheless, although Yi deserved punishment, what fault was there in Lu’s returning him? Although Lu deserved blame, how did that diminish the rightness of Qi’s action? Thus the noble man seeks only to fulfill what lies within his own power.

Book of Rites

“Music is what the sages delight in, and it can make the people’s hearts good. It moves people deeply and transforms their ways and customs; therefore the former kings established instruction in it.”

Wang Yiyan 王一言

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄧批發揮明盡
考試官學正孫批敷暢
考試官教授張批詞達
記者原樂之用廣而聖王明之以淑天下也蓋
大樂與治道相通者也作之本於心而行之裕
於治先王豈能外是以爲教哉樂記之旨如此
意謂聖人作樂其始也因心以成象而其終也
宣化以成功則樂固聖人善天下之大權焉耳
故聲音發於器舞蹈動諸容是樂也者本諸情
===
焉物感不能違其眞飾夫喜焉度數有以通其
妙聖人之所樂在是也而以之推諸人焉志意
相感而協和之機以神性天流行而合愛之化
自速惟其善民心也内之可以反性情之正而
一德于是乎潛孚外之可以挽風俗之淳而萬
方于是乎丕變夫大樂之化如此是以先王立
學以教民節奏則廣之文采則省之而使民之
繩其德者知所遵省方以設教行列則正之進
退則齊之而使民之善其容者有所守聖作而
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄧批：發揮明盡。
考試官學正孫批：敷暢。
考試官教授張批：詞達。
記者原樂之用廣，而聖王明之以淑天下也。蓋大樂與治道相通者也，作之本於心，而行之裕於治，先王豈能外是以爲教哉？樂記之旨如此。意謂聖人作樂，其始也因心以成象，而其終也宣化以成功，則樂固聖人善天下之大權焉耳。故聲音發於器，舞蹈動諸容，是樂也者，本諸情焉，物感不能違其眞；飾夫喜焉，度數有以通其妙。聖人之所樂在是也。而以之推諸人焉，志意相感而協和之機以神，性天流行而合愛之化自速。惟其善民心也，内之可以反性情之正，而一德于是乎潛孚；外之可以挽風俗之淳，而萬方于是乎丕變。夫大樂之化如此，是以先王立學以教民，節奏則廣之，文采則省之，而使民之繩其德者知所遵；省方以設教，行列則正之，進退則齊之，而使民之善其容者有所守。聖作而
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor, comments: “The exposition is clear and exhaustive.”
Examiner Sun, School Director, comments: “Ample and fluent.”
Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “The wording conveys the meaning.”
The author of the Record traces the far-reaching functions of music and explains how sage kings made them manifest to improve all under Heaven. Great music and the Way of government are interconnected. Its creation is rooted in the heart, and its practice enriches government. How could the former kings have taught without it? Such is the purport of the Record of Music. The meaning is that when sages created music, they began by following the heart to give it perceptible form, and ended by spreading their transforming influence to complete their achievement. Music is thus the great means by which sages improve all under Heaven.
Thus sounds issue from instruments, and dancing moves the body. Music is rooted in the feelings: their response to external things cannot depart from their genuineness. It gives embellishment to joy, and its measures and proportions communicate its subtlety. Herein lies what the sages delight in. When this is extended to others, their intentions resonate with one another, and the workings of concord become wondrous; Heaven-endowed nature flows freely, and the transformation that unites them in mutual love proceeds swiftly of itself. Precisely because music improves the people's hearts, inwardly it can restore the rightness of their nature and feelings, so that a common virtue quietly wins their trust; outwardly it can restore the purity of customs, so that all regions undergo a great transformation.
Such is the transforming influence of great music. Accordingly, the former kings established schools to teach the people: they broadened its rhythms and restrained its embellishments, so that those among the people who sought to regulate their virtue knew what to follow. They toured the regions to impart instruction: they corrected the ranks of the dancers and coordinated their advances and retreats, so that those among the people who sought to improve their deportment had standards to observe. title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
物觀焉蓋溥之四海之廣而不出於吾心之和
也君令而民從焉蓋達之萬民之衆而皆本諸
一順之推也先王之敎孰有大於此者哉是則
聖人之於民分不同而情同大樂之於治施不
一而和一此先王普之以成功而後世準之以
爲的也歟抑論先王之爲樂也平其心而後平
其政和其心而後和其聲其心與天地一元之
氣相感通而後出之於樂始得其聲氣之元而
小者不窕大者不槖卒之上可以省風下可以
===
觀民而後樂可大化可成聖人之心可永於天
下嗚呼聖人之樂不可見矣聖人之心猶有存
焉有志者其毋諉於古樂之不可復
臣下竭力盡能以立功於國君必報之以
爵祿故臣下皆務竭力盡能以立功是
以國安而君寧禮無不答言上之不虛
取於下也上必明正道以道民民道之
而有功然後取其什一故上用足而下
不匱也是以上下和親而不相怨也和
punctuated:
物觀焉，蓋溥之四海之廣，而不出於吾心之和也。君令而民從焉，蓋達之萬民之衆，而皆本諸一順之推也。先王之敎，孰有大於此者哉？是則聖人之於民，分不同而情同；大樂之於治，施不一而和一。此先王普之以成功，而後世準之以爲的也歟？抑論先王之爲樂也，平其心而後平其政，和其心而後和其聲。其心與天地一元之氣相感通，而後出之於樂，始得其聲氣之元，而小者不窕，大者不槖。卒之，上可以省風，下可以觀民，而後樂可大，化可成，聖人之心可永於天下。嗚呼！聖人之樂不可見矣，聖人之心猶有存焉。有志者，其毋諉於古樂之不可復！

臣下竭力盡能以立功於國，君必報之以爵祿，故臣下皆務竭力盡能以立功，是以國安而君寧。禮無不答，言上之不虛取於下也。上必明正道以道民，民道之而有功，然後取其什一，故上用足而下不匱也。是以上下和親而不相怨也。和
translation_en:
…and all beings behold it. Though it extends throughout the vastness of the Four Seas, it does not go beyond the harmony of one's own heart. The ruler commands and the people obey: though this reaches the multitude of all the people, it is entirely rooted in the extension of a single principle of accord. What teaching of the former kings could be greater than this? Thus, although the sage and the people differ in station, they share the same feelings; although great music has diverse applications in government, its harmony is one. Was this not what the former kings spread universally to accomplish their work, and what later generations took as their standard and aim?

Moreover, consider how the former kings made music. They brought peace to their hearts before bringing peace to their government; they harmonized their hearts before harmonizing their sounds. Only after their hearts had entered into sympathetic communion with the primordial vital energy of Heaven and Earth did they express this in music. Only then did they grasp the source of sound and vital energy, so that quiet sounds were not insubstantial and loud sounds were not hollow [?]. Ultimately, those above could examine prevailing customs, and those below could observe the people. Only then could music attain greatness, moral transformation be accomplished, and the sage's heart endure throughout the world. Alas! The music of the sages can no longer be witnessed, yet their hearts still survive. Let those with resolve not plead as an excuse that ancient music cannot be restored!

Ministers exert all their strength and ability to render service to the state, and the ruler must reward them with ranks and emoluments. Thus all ministers strive to exert their strength and ability to render service, and consequently the state is secure and the ruler at peace. No act of ritual propriety goes unanswered: this means that those above do not take from those below without giving anything in return. Those above must make the correct Way clear in order to guide the people. Only after the people follow it and achieve results do those above take one tenth of their produce. Thus those above have sufficient resources for their expenses, while those below suffer no shortage. Consequently, those above and below live in harmony and affection, without resentment toward one another. Harmony…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
寧禮之用也此君臣上下之大義也
方桂
同考試官教諭鄧批〔體認明盡〕
考試官學正孫批〔善檃括〕
考試官教授張批〔莊重〕
君臣盡禮有其效一義之攸在也夫禮行而效
著固也知是之爲義焉爲君臣者宜思所以自
盡矣記燕義者其旨如此且君之燕臣也有旅
酬之爵焉有特賜之爵焉自臣拜君爵言之固
===
所以明臣禮也而禮則何居亦曰思盡瘁於君
耳彼竭力盡能以立功臣職之常也君因之而
有報焉爵以詔其德也祿以顯其庸也則爲臣
者感寵賚之旣隆將勤勞之畢奮肯自怠乎臣
盡臣禮如此由是事無不治而民庶熈内無不
脩而疆境謐淵衷無宵旰之憂福履遂優游之
樂矣何寧如之自君答臣拜言之固所以明君
禮也而禮則何居亦曰不虚取於下耳彼分田
制里以道民君道之正也民因之而有功焉菽
punctuated:
寧，禮之用也。此君臣上下之大義也。

方桂
同考試官教諭鄧批〔體認明盡〕
考試官學正孫批〔善檃括〕
考試官教授張批〔莊重〕

君臣盡禮有其效，一義之攸在也。夫禮行而效著，固也。知是之爲義焉，爲君臣者宜思所以自盡矣。記燕義者，其旨如此。且君之燕臣也，有旅酬之爵焉，有特賜之爵焉。自臣拜君爵言之，固所以明臣禮也。而禮則何居？亦曰思盡瘁於君耳。彼竭力盡能以立功，臣職之常也。君因之而有報焉，爵以詔其德也，祿以顯其庸也。則爲臣者感寵賚之旣隆，將勤勞之畢奮，肯自怠乎？臣盡臣禮如此，由是事無不治而民庶熈，内無不脩而疆境謐，淵衷無宵旰之憂，福履遂優游之樂矣。何寧如之！自君答臣拜言之，固所以明君禮也。而禮則何居？亦曰不虚取於下耳。彼分田制里以道民，君道之正也。民因之而有功焉，菽
translation_en:
…tranquillity are the effects of ritual propriety. This is the great moral obligation binding ruler and ministers, superiors and inferiors.

Fang Gui
Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor (jiaoyu), comments: 〔Clear and thorough comprehension.〕
Examiner Sun, Instructor (xuezheng), comments: 〔Skillful synthesis.〕
Examiner Zhang, Professor (jiaoshou), comments: 〔Dignified and grave.〕

When ruler and ministers fully observe ritual propriety, it produces its effects: herein lies a single moral obligation. That the practice of ritual should yield manifest effects is certainly natural. Recognizing this as a moral obligation, rulers and ministers should consider how to fulfill their respective duties to the utmost. Such is the purport of the author of “The Meaning of the Banquet Ceremony.” When the ruler banquets his ministers, there are cups passed around in reciprocal toasting and cups bestowed as special favors. Viewed from the minister’s bow upon receiving the ruler’s cup, this certainly makes clear the minister’s ritual duty. But wherein does that duty lie? Simply in striving to expend oneself utterly in the ruler’s service. To exert all one’s strength and ability to render meritorious service is the minister’s ordinary duty. The ruler accordingly rewards him: rank proclaims his virtue, and emoluments make manifest his accomplishments. Moved by such abundant favor and gifts, will a minister not exert himself fully in diligent service? Would he willingly grow idle? Such is the minister’s complete fulfillment of his ritual duty. Consequently, all affairs are well governed and the people flourish; internal administration is fully attended to and the frontiers are tranquil. The sovereign’s heart is free of anxieties that keep him occupied from before dawn until late at night, and his blessed condition brings the pleasure of ease and leisure. What tranquillity could equal this!

Viewed from the ruler’s returning the minister’s bow, this certainly makes clear the ruler’s ritual duty. But wherein does that duty lie? Simply in taking nothing from those below without giving something in return. To allot fields and organize settlements so as to guide the people is the proper way of rulership. Through this guidance, the people achieve productive results: beans…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
粟之既登也桑麻之既植也斯爲君者酌稅斂
之攸宜將什一之是賦肯虛取乎君盡君禮如
此由是賦稅供而用充於國征斂薄而財裕於
民上下有相愛之休朝野無交瘉之病矣何和
如之君盡君禮而致和是禮其本而和其用矣
然此非君上之大義乎蓋禮有未盡則無以致
和父母斯民之意終有歉耳如君何臣盡臣禮
而致寧是禮其本而寧其用矣然此非臣下之
大義乎蓋禮有未盡則無以致寧左右厥辟之
===
責終有愧耳如臣何是則禮行於燕飲之間義
存夫君臣之大先王之爲燕也豈徒飲食之娛
而已哉抑君臣之分等之天地若是乎其嚴也
而燕禮之交又惡在其爲嚴歟蓋古之君臣分
未嘗不辨而情未嘗不親惟辨也故禮肅而不
敢踰惟親也故誼結而不可解嗚呼此上下交
孚而德業之所以盛歟
第貳場
論
punctuated:
粟之既登也，桑麻之既植也，斯爲君者酌稅斂之攸宜，將什一之是賦，肯虛取乎？君盡君禮如此，由是賦稅供而用充於國，征斂薄而財裕於民，上下有相愛之休，朝野無交瘉之病矣。何和如之？君盡君禮而致和，是禮其本而和其用矣。然此非君上之大義乎？蓋禮有未盡，則無以致和，父母斯民之意終有歉耳，如君何？臣盡臣禮而致寧，是禮其本而寧其用矣。然此非臣下之大義乎？蓋禮有未盡，則無以致寧，左右厥辟之責終有愧耳，如臣何？是則禮行於燕飲之間，義存夫君臣之大。先王之爲燕也，豈徒飲食之娛而已哉？抑君臣之分，等之天地，若是乎其嚴也，而燕禮之交，又惡在其爲嚴歟？蓋古之君臣，分未嘗不辨，而情未嘗不親。惟辨也，故禮肅而不敢踰；惟親也，故誼結而不可解。嗚呼！此上下交孚而德業之所以盛歟？

第貳場

論
translation_en:
…when the millet has been harvested and the mulberry and hemp planted, the ruler considers the proper measure of taxation and levies only one-tenth. Would he willingly take anything without due cause? Such is the ruler’s fulfillment of the ritual obligations of a ruler. Thus taxes are supplied and the state has sufficient resources for its expenditure; levies are light and the people enjoy ample wealth. Those above and below enjoy mutual affection, and court and countryside are free from the affliction of mutual recrimination. What harmony could equal this? When the ruler fulfills his ritual obligations and thereby brings about harmony, ritual is the foundation and harmony its effect. Yet is this not the ruler’s great moral duty? For if his ritual obligations remain unfulfilled, he has no means of bringing about harmony, and his intention to act as father and mother to these people must ultimately fall short. How, then, can he fulfill his role as ruler? When ministers fulfill their ritual obligations and thereby bring about tranquility, ritual is the foundation and tranquility its effect. Yet is this not the ministers’ great moral duty? For if their ritual obligations remain unfulfilled, they have no means of bringing about tranquility, and they must ultimately feel shame over their responsibility to assist their sovereign. How, then, can they fulfill their role as ministers? Thus ritual is practiced amid feasting and drinking, while moral duty resides in the great relationship between ruler and ministers. Could the former kings have held banquets merely for the pleasures of food and drink? Yet the distinction between ruler and ministers is as strict as that between Heaven and Earth. Where, then, is this strictness in their intercourse during the banquet rites? Among rulers and ministers of antiquity, distinctions of status were always clear, yet their feelings were always close. Because those distinctions were clear, ritual was solemn, and they dared not overstep it; because their feelings were close, bonds of affection were formed that could not be severed. Ah! Is this not how those above and below came to trust one another, and how virtue and achievement flourished?

Second Session

Discourse

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
君相以父母天下爲王道
鄭富
同考試官教諭文批體製渾成如商彞周鼎不事
雕刻而文采蔚然足稱高論
同考試官學正蔡批是作僅數百字耳而意深格
古有淵然之光蒼然之色鏗然之聲一洗時陋噫子獨藝
焉已乎
考試官學正孫批爾雅
考試官教授張批復古之作
===
唯仁人能愛人能長人人之生皆有不忍人之
心有不忍人之心斯有不忍人之政無不仁無
不愛無不足以長人也氣禀拘之物欲蔽之君
子而不仁者蓋有之矣况其下乎是故唯仁人
能愛人唯仁人足以長人也且長人何以取足
於仁人哉大哉乾元萬物資始至哉坤元萬物
資生天地萬物父母也天地能父母萬物萬物
不能自成能於天地必立之君使治教之是曰
元后作民父母父母天下之名所由立也則爲
punctuated:
君相以父母天下爲王道
鄭富

同考試官教諭文批：體製渾成，如商彞周鼎，不事雕刻而文采蔚然，足稱高論。
同考試官學正蔡批：是作僅數百字耳，而意深格古，有淵然之光、蒼然之色、鏗然之聲，一洗時陋。噫！子獨藝焉已乎？
考試官學正孫批：爾雅。
考試官教授張批：復古之作。

唯仁人能愛人，能長人。人之生，皆有不忍人之心；有不忍人之心，斯有不忍人之政，無不仁，無不愛，無不足以長人也。氣禀拘之，物欲蔽之，君子而不仁者蓋有之矣，况其下乎？是故唯仁人能愛人，唯仁人足以長人也。且長人何以取足於仁人哉？大哉乾元，萬物資始；至哉坤元，萬物資生。天地，萬物父母也。天地能父母萬物，萬物不能自成，能於天地，必立之君，使治教之，是曰「元后作民父母」，父母天下之名所由立也。則爲
translation_en:
For the Ruler and His Chief Minister, the Kingly Way Consists in Acting as Parents to All under Heaven
By Zheng Fu

Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: The composition is a perfectly integrated whole, like a Shang ritual vessel or a Zhou tripod. Without elaborate carving, its literary brilliance flourishes. It fully deserves to be called an excellent discourse.

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Assistant Instructor: This piece contains only a few hundred characters, yet its meaning is profound and its style antique.
