It has a deep radiance, an ancient hue, and a ringing resonance, sweeping away the vulgarities of the age. Ah! Is your accomplishment confined to literary skill alone?

Comment by Examiner Sun, Assistant Instructor: Refined and correct.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Instructor: A work that restores the ancient style.

Only the benevolent can love others and lead them. All people are born with a heart that cannot bear the suffering of others. With such a heart comes government that cannot bear the suffering of others: nothing in it lacks benevolence or love, and nothing is inadequate to leading others. Yet people are constrained by their endowment of vital energy and obscured by material desires. Even among gentlemen there are those who lack benevolence; how much more so among those below them? Thus only the benevolent can love others, and only the benevolent are fit to lead others. Why, then, is benevolence sufficient qualification for leading others? Great indeed is the primal power of Qian: all things draw upon it for their beginning. Consummate indeed is the primal power of Kun: all things draw upon it for their birth. Heaven and Earth are the parents of all things. Heaven and Earth can act as parents to all things, but all things cannot bring themselves to completion; this capacity lies with Heaven and Earth [?]. A ruler must therefore be established over them to govern and instruct them. This is what is meant by “The sovereign acts as the people's father and mother,” and it is from this that the designation “parents to all under Heaven” arises. Thus, to be…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
人君止於仁豈非其分之當然而自不容已乎
然能盡分者何鮮也吾之子吾愛之鄰人之子
則鄰人之矣國人之子則國人之矣此天下人
之情也吾讀二帝三王書竊悲聖人之於民雖
微物隱情盡制曲慮無少滲漏而其大者明天
道脩人紀抑洪水驅猛獸禪繼放伐苟利於國
雖身天下之不測舍至愛犯不韙猶不厭為之
此其懷保惠鮮眞若嚴父慈母乳哺嬰兒如或
傷之而鞠育顧復敎詔薰陶無所不用其誠豈
===
忍置一毫私意於其間哉此無他聖人之心至
誠無貳與天同德故視天下萬物莫非分內小
大遠邇無一不在所愛之中蓋仁人之足以長
人也如此後世知求治而不知正君本原闊畧
旣無以通天下之志又不勝其多欲之心以故
一膜之外便為胡越用智自私靡所不至蓋雖
閨門父子猶將有所隔礙而不能通其不好人
之所惡惡人之所好者幾希惡在其為民父母
哉此張子所以深憂朝廷以道學政術為二事
punctuated: 人君止於仁，豈非其分之當然而自不容已乎？然能盡分者何鮮也！吾之子，吾愛之；鄰人之子，則鄰人之矣；國人之子，則國人之矣。此天下人之情也。吾讀二帝三王書，竊悲聖人之於民，雖微物隱情，盡制曲慮，無少滲漏；而其大者，明天道，脩人紀，抑洪水，驅猛獸，禪繼放伐，苟利於國，雖身天下之不測，舍至愛，犯不韙，猶不厭為之。此其懷保惠鮮，眞若嚴父慈母乳哺嬰兒，如或傷之，而鞠育顧復，敎詔薰陶，無所不用其誠，豈忍置一毫私意於其間哉？此無他，聖人之心至誠無貳，與天同德，故視天下萬物莫非分內，小大遠邇，無一不在所愛之中。蓋仁人之足以長人也如此。後世知求治而不知正君，本原闊畧，旣無以通天下之志，又不勝其多欲之心，以故一膜之外，便為胡越，用智自私，靡所不至。蓋雖閨門父子，猶將有所隔礙而不能通，其不好人之所惡、惡人之所好者幾希！惡在其為民父母哉？此張子所以深憂朝廷以道學政術為二事
translation_en:
…for a ruler to abide in benevolence—is this not what his duty requires, something he cannot of himself cease to pursue? Yet how few fully discharge that duty! My own children I love; my neighbors’ children I leave to my neighbors; the children of my countrymen I leave to my countrymen. Such are the feelings of people throughout the world. Reading the writings concerning the Two Emperors and Three Kings, I privately grieve to reflect upon the sages’ care for the people. Even in minor matters and hidden circumstances, they made comprehensive provision and considered every detail, leaving nothing overlooked. In greater matters, they clarified the Way of Heaven, cultivated human relationships, checked floods, drove away fierce beasts, and undertook abdication, succession, banishment, and punitive conquest. If it benefited the realm, even when they had to expose themselves to unfathomable dangers, relinquish those they loved most, or brave condemnation, they never tired of doing so. In cherishing and protecting the people and bestowing kindness upon the distressed, they were truly like stern fathers and loving mothers nursing infants, fearful of causing them any hurt. In nurturing and tending them, instructing and gradually shaping them, they applied their utmost sincerity at every turn. How could they bear to introduce the slightest selfish intention into this?

There is no other explanation: the sages’ hearts were utterly sincere and undivided, sharing Heaven’s virtue. Thus they regarded all things under Heaven as falling within their duty. Great or small, distant or near, nothing lay outside their love. Such is the benevolent person’s fitness to lead others. In later ages, people knew to seek good government but did not know to rectify the ruler. They neglected the source and foundation: they could neither comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven nor master their own hearts’ many desires. Consequently, anything beyond their own skin became as alien to them as Hu and Yue. They employed their intelligence for selfish ends, stopping at nothing. Even within the household, between fathers and sons, barriers arose that prevented mutual understanding. How few of them did not love what others hated and hate what others loved! Where, then, was their claim to be fathers and mothers of the people? This is why Master Zhang was deeply troubled that the court treated learning of the Way and the arts of government as two separate matters…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
而欲行帝王之道者必自使其君愛天下之人
如赤子始程子曰有天德便可語王道此之謂
也
同前
楊子充
同考試官教諭崔批據理立論惻怛由衷且詞采抑揚
足以發先賢之未發不厭重刻
同考試官教諭劉批質而不俚文而不縟開闔變化
理與氣俱讀之起敬
===
考試官學正孫批思致周遠
考試官教授張批沉着弘遠
王道不可以易言也天生民而立之君使司牧
之勿使失性有君而爲之貳使師保之勿使過
度天萬物父母也君受天之子而爲之牧是謂
元后作民父母也相則佐君以成牧之之道也
父母之命出於天而畀之君相謂必惠之保之
其於斯民眞如吾之愛其子可也而或少有私
意存乎其中則一膜之外便爲胡越非父母矣
punctuated:
而欲行帝王之道者，必自使其君愛天下之人如赤子始。程子曰：「有天德，便可語王道。」此之謂也。

同前
楊子充

同考試官教諭崔批：據理立論，惻怛由衷，且詞采抑揚，足以發先賢之未發，不厭重刻。
同考試官教諭劉批：質而不俚，文而不縟，開闔變化，理與氣俱，讀之起敬。
考試官學正孫批：思致周遠。
考試官教授張批：沉着弘遠。

王道不可以易言也。天生民而立之君，使司牧之，勿使失性；有君而爲之貳，使師保之，勿使過度。天，萬物父母也。君受天之子而爲之牧，是謂元后作民父母也。相則佐君以成牧之之道也。父母之命出於天，而畀之君相，謂必惠之保之，其於斯民，眞如吾之愛其子可也。而或少有私意存乎其中，則一膜之外便爲胡越，非父母矣。
translation_en:
…and anyone wishing to practice the Way of the sage emperors and kings must begin by bringing his ruler to love all people under Heaven as newborn children. Master Cheng said, “With Heaven’s virtue, one may then speak of the Kingly Way.” This is what he meant.

Same topic as above
Yang Zichong

Comment by Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor: His argument rests on principle, and his heartfelt compassion comes from within. Moreover, the rise and fall of his eloquent phrasing suffice to express what earlier worthies left unexpressed. It merits being printed again.
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Substantial without being vulgar, elegant without being ornate. Through its unfolding, gathering, and transformations, principle and vital force are both present. Reading it inspires respect.
Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: His thought is comprehensive and far-reaching.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: Steady and assured, broad and far-reaching.

The Kingly Way cannot be spoken of lightly. Heaven gave birth to the people and established a ruler over them, charging him to shepherd them and prevent them from losing their inherent nature. Having established a ruler, it appointed a deputy for him, charging him to instruct and protect the ruler and prevent him from exceeding proper bounds. Heaven is the parent of all things. The ruler receives Heaven’s children into his charge and shepherds them: this is what is meant by the sovereign acting as father and mother to the people. The chief minister assists the ruler in fulfilling the way of shepherding them. The mandate to act as parents comes from Heaven and is bestowed upon the ruler and chief minister. It requires them to show kindness to the people and protect them; they must treat these people truly as we love our own children. But if even a little selfish intent remains within, then those beyond a single membrane become as alien as the Hu and the Yue, and they are no longer parents to the people.…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
棄天地之性矣天之愛民甚矣豈其使一人肆
於民上以從其淫而棄天地之性必不然矣是
故明於天命之故而後可以語王道也父母者
一家之說也吾之子吾體之易也鄉人之子則
異是矣國人之子則又異是矣天下人之子則
又異是矣而又五土異性五方異氣大川廣谷
異地人生其間異俗輕重遲速長短異齊舟車
器械異制飲食衣服異宜非若吾之一家可以
體而一之也而吾不能推情以致理緣俗以立
===
教隨所宜以為之制則元元之子不得所欲者
多矣是不能如慈母之心誠求之也而曰如保
赤子可乎是故察於庶物羣情之變而後可以
語王道也王者之政非苟作者禮樂刑政四達
而不悖皆必有至理存乎其間而一毫私意小
智不與焉故其制度品節之詳終始條理之序
内則盡理外則盡制不容毫髮僭差也易曰后
以財成天地之道輔相天地之宜以左右民此
天時地理人事之紀也道德性命之原也昧此
punctuated: 棄天地之性矣。天之愛民甚矣，豈其使一人肆於民上，以從其淫，而棄天地之性？必不然矣。是故明於天命之故，而後可以語王道也。父母者，一家之說也。吾之子，吾體之易也；鄉人之子則異是矣，國人之子則又異是矣，天下人之子則又異是矣。而又五土異性，五方異氣，大川廣谷異地，人生其間異俗，輕重遲速長短異齊，舟車器械異制，飲食衣服異宜，非若吾之一家可以體而一之也。而吾不能推情以致理，緣俗以立教，隨所宜以為之制，則元元之子不得所欲者多矣。是不能如慈母之心誠求之也，而曰如保赤子，可乎？是故察於庶物羣情之變，而後可以語王道也。王者之政，非苟作者。禮樂刑政，四達而不悖，皆必有至理存乎其間，而一毫私意小智不與焉。故其制度品節之詳，終始條理之序，内則盡理，外則盡制，不容毫髮僭差也。《易》曰：「后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」此天時地理人事之紀也，道德性命之原也。昧此
translation_en:
…and abandon the nature endowed by Heaven and Earth. Heaven’s love for the people is profound indeed. Could it allow one man to act unchecked above the people, indulging his excesses and abandoning the nature endowed by Heaven and Earth? Surely not. Thus, only after understanding the grounds of Heaven’s mandate can one speak of the kingly Way.

Parenthood is a relationship within a single family. My own child is a continuation of my own body [?]. The children of my fellow villagers are different; the children of others in the state are different again; and the children of people throughout the realm are different yet again. Moreover, the five kinds of soil differ in character, and the five regions differ in their vital energies. Great rivers and broad valleys differ in terrain, and the people born among them differ in customs. In lightness and heaviness, slowness and speed, length and shortness, their standards differ; their boats, carriages, implements, and tools differ in design; and different foods, drinks, and clothing suit them. They are unlike my own family, whose members I can embrace as one body. If I cannot extend my sympathetic feelings to bring proper order into effect, establish teachings in accordance with local customs, and devise institutions suited to their circumstances, then many among these children—the common people—will fail to obtain what they desire. This is to fail to seek their needs sincerely, with a loving mother’s heart. Can one then claim to act “as though protecting an infant”? Thus, only after discerning the variations among the many things and the feelings of the people can one speak of the kingly Way.

The government of a true king is not undertaken casually. Ritual, music, punishments, and administration operate everywhere without conflict. Within them there must always be the highest principle, with not the slightest selfish intention or petty cleverness intruding. Thus, in the particulars of their institutions and measured distinctions, and in their orderly arrangement from beginning to end, they fully realize principle within and fully establish regulations without, admitting not the slightest overstepping or error. The Book of Changes says: “The sovereign shapes and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth, assists what is fitting to Heaven and Earth, and thereby guides the people.” These are the governing principles of Heaven’s seasons, Earth’s terrain, and human affairs, and the source of the Way, virtue, human nature, and destiny. To be ignorant of this…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
吾未見其能行父母之政也然則達於三才之
奧道德性命之原而後可以語王道也夫然後
不獨親其親不獨子其子老有所終壯有所用
幼有所長鰥寡孤獨廢疾皆有所養男有分女
有歸則自一家以至於天下皆家矣自一人以
至於億兆人皆子矣是之謂大同然後天不愛
道地不愛寶人不愛情山川鬼神亦莫不寧曁
鳥獸魚鼈咸若是之謂大順大同大順聖神功
化之極也而君相父母天下之事畢矣然則未
===
至於聖神功化之極未可以語王道也雖然豈
外求哉亦在吾君吾相存主之間耳所以存主
之者心也所以存主此心者敬也敬自愼獨始
也世之君相不能愼獨以明其明德故無以通
天下之志而知千萬人之心卽一人之心無以
勝一己之私而以一人之心爲千萬人之心如
是而曰君相可矣將以稱於天下曰父母父母
則未也故曰有天德便可語王道
表
punctuated:
吾未見其能行父母之政也。然則達於三才之奧、道德性命之原，而後可以語王道也。夫然後不獨親其親，不獨子其子，老有所終，壯有所用，幼有所長，鰥寡孤獨廢疾皆有所養，男有分，女有歸，則自一家以至於天下皆家矣，自一人以至於億兆人皆子矣。是之謂大同。然後天不愛道，地不愛寶，人不愛情，山川鬼神亦莫不寧，曁鳥獸魚鼈咸若。是之謂大順。大同大順，聖神功化之極也，而君相父母天下之事畢矣。然則未至於聖神功化之極，未可以語王道也。雖然，豈外求哉？亦在吾君吾相存主之間耳。所以存主之者，心也；所以存主此心者，敬也。敬自愼獨始也。世之君相不能愼獨以明其明德，故無以通天下之志，而知千萬人之心卽一人之心；無以勝一己之私，而以一人之心爲千萬人之心。如是而曰君相可矣，將以稱於天下曰父母父母，則未也。故曰：「有天德便可語王道。」

表
translation_en:
…I have never seen such a person able to govern as a parent to the people. Thus, only after comprehending the mysteries of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and the source of the Way, virtue, human nature, and destiny can one speak of the Kingly Way. Only then will people cherish not merely their own parents and treat not merely their own children as children; the aged will be provided for to the end of their lives, the able-bodied will have employment, and the young will be nurtured. Widowers, widows, orphans, the childless elderly, and those disabled or ill will all receive support. Men will have their allotted duties, and women will have homes in marriage. Then, from a single household to all under Heaven, all will be one family; from a single person to the countless multitudes, all will be children. This is called Great Unity. Then Heaven will not withhold its Way, Earth will not withhold its treasures, and people will not withhold their true feelings. The spirits of mountains and rivers will all be at peace, and birds, beasts, fish, and turtles will all thrive in harmony. This is called Great Accord. Great Unity and Great Accord are the highest achievement of sagely and numinous transformation; with these, the task of rulers and chief ministers in acting as parents to all under Heaven is fulfilled. Thus, until this highest achievement of sagely and numinous transformation is reached, one cannot speak of the Kingly Way.

Yet how could this be sought outside oneself? It lies simply in what our ruler and our chief ministers preserve within themselves and hold as their guiding principle. That by which they preserve and uphold it is the mind; that by which they preserve and govern this mind is reverent attentiveness. Reverent attentiveness begins with vigilance when alone. The rulers and chief ministers of the world cannot remain vigilant when alone so as to illuminate their luminous virtue. Hence they have no means to comprehend the aspirations of all under Heaven and recognize that the minds of countless people are the same as the mind of one person. Nor have they the means to overcome their own selfishness and make the mind of one person the mind of countless people. In this condition they may be called rulers and chief ministers, but they are not yet fit to be acclaimed throughout the world as “our parents, our parents.” Thus it is said: “Only with Heaven’s virtue can one speak of the Kingly Way.”

Memorials

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
擬
聖駕重幸太學祭酒率諸生
謝表
薛欽
同考試官教諭沈批我
皇上崇重
先師之禮超出千古此作揄揚殆盡可以觀
聖化矣
同考試官學正蔡批
===
聖天子道學之正禮樂之備未易窺測乃能模寫如此子其以文鳴盛者邪
考試官學正孫批駢麗有則
考試官教授張批善頌
嘉靖十二年三月十三日欽蒙
聖駕臨幸太學祭酒臣某等謹率諸生奉
表稱
謝者伏以
華蓋天臨再開右文之治辟廱風動式昭左
史之書復覩漢儀肇稱殷禮開
punctuated:
擬聖駕重幸太學祭酒率諸生謝表
薛欽

同考試官教諭沈批：我皇上崇重先師之禮，超出千古。此作揄揚殆盡，可以觀聖化矣。
同考試官學正蔡批：聖天子道學之正，禮樂之備，未易窺測，乃能模寫如此，子其以文鳴盛者邪？
考試官學正孫批：駢麗有則。
考試官教授張批：善頌。

嘉靖十二年三月十三日，欽蒙聖駕臨幸太學，祭酒臣某等謹率諸生奉表稱謝者。伏以：華蓋天臨，再開右文之治；辟廱風動，式昭左史之書。復覩漢儀，肇稱殷禮。開
translation_en:
Draft memorial of thanks on His Majesty’s renewed visit to the Imperial University, submitted by the Chancellor at the head of the students
By Xue Qin

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “The reverence with which our emperor honors the First Teacher surpasses that of all previous ages. This composition praises it almost exhaustively; through it one can perceive the transforming influence of the sage emperor.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Instructor: “The correctness of the sage Son of Heaven’s learning of the Way and the completeness of his rites and music are not easily fathomed. Yet you have portrayed them thus! Are you perhaps one who will celebrate this flourishing age through his writing?”
Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: “Elegant parallel prose, governed by proper rules.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: “Excellent praise.”

On the thirteenth day of the third month of the twelfth year of Jiajing, we reverently received the honor of His Majesty’s visit to the Imperial University. Your servants, the Chancellor So-and-so and others, respectfully lead the students in presenting this memorial of thanks.
We humbly reflect: Your imperial canopy descended from heaven, renewing a reign that honors letters; your influence stirred the Imperial University like the wind, gloriously illuminating the record of the Recorder of the Left. Once more we beheld the ceremonial dignity of Han; now we began to perform the grand rites. Opening…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
講筵而晝接煦士類以春融化軌聿新詞林
協慶臣等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首竊惟太學
乃賢士所關而孔子自生民未有大明六
籍開萬古之羣蒙遠紹百王壽斯文之一
脉自秦灰滅學漢馬少文求儒雅以闡猷
誰云多欲在念起褒成而改謚未知大德
不官中元制建三雍比齊禮修二仲五更
三老塡門雜進乎車輪四辟諸賢列奠祇
陳乎脯醢况復鴻都虎觀徒多蟬噪蛙鳴
===
武德講經沙門雜雅元祐再拜泮水無光
名爲重道崇儒實則背經侮聖僭瀆一律
後世奚觀制作百年
明時有待兹蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
聰明天縱
聲敎雷行繩
祖武而謹日中觀人文以化天下
聖弗自滿而主善爲師
punctuated:
講筵而晝接，煦士類以春融，化軌聿新，詞林協慶。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。竊惟太學乃賢士所關，而孔子自生民未有。大明六籍，開萬古之羣蒙；遠紹百王，壽斯文之一脉。自秦灰滅學，漢馬少文，求儒雅以闡猷，誰云多欲在念？起褒成而改謚，未知大德不官。中元制建三雍，比齊禮修二仲。五更三老，塡門雜進乎車輪；四辟諸賢，列奠祇陳乎脯醢。况復鴻都虎觀，徒多蟬噪蛙鳴；武德講經，沙門雜雅；元祐再拜，泮水無光。名爲重道崇儒，實則背經侮聖，僭瀆一律，後世奚觀？制作百年，明時有待。
兹蓋伏遇皇帝陛下，聰明天縱，聲敎雷行，繩祖武而謹日中，觀人文以化天下，聖弗自滿而主善爲師。
translation_en:
…opening the lecture sessions and receiving scholars by day, warming the ranks of scholars with the genial influence of spring. The course of moral transformation is renewed, and the literary community joins in celebration. We, your servants, are truly delighted and truly joyful; we bow our heads and knock our foreheads upon the ground.
We humbly consider that the Imperial University is where worthy scholars are gathered, while Confucius was without equal since humankind first came into being. He made the Six Classics brilliantly clear, dispelling the accumulated ignorance of all ages; he carried forward the legacy of the hundred kings of antiquity, perpetuating the single thread of this cultural tradition. After Qin reduced learning to ashes, the Han ruler Ma [?] showed little literary cultivation. He sought learned Confucians to elucidate the proper way of government—yet who could say that his mind was free of excessive desires? He raised up the holder of the title Baocheng and changed the posthumous designation [?], not understanding that one of supreme virtue is not confined by official rank. In the Zhongyuan reign, the three ceremonial institutions were established by imperial enactment; under Qi [?], rites were performed in the middle months of spring and autumn. The Five Experienced Men and Three Elders crowded the gates, arriving together in their carriages; for the worthies of the four auxiliary institutions [?], the offerings set out amounted merely to dried meat and minced meat. Moreover, at Hongdu and Huguan there was only much cicada-like clamoring and frog-like croaking. During the Wude reign, Buddhist monks mingled in the august proceedings at lectures on the Classics; during the Yuanyou reign, the double bow brought no luster to the school. In name these acts honored the Way and exalted Confucian learning; in reality they contradicted the Classics and affronted the Sage. All alike were presumptuous and profane: what example could later generations find in them? The establishment of institutions over a hundred years awaited an enlightened age.
Now, however, we have humbly encountered Your Majesty the Emperor, whose intelligence is Heaven-given and whose civilizing influence spreads like thunder. You follow your ancestors’ footsteps and are conscientious at midday [?]; you contemplate human culture in order to transform all under Heaven. Though a sage, you are never self-satisfied, and you take goodness as your teacher…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
手不停披而學古有獲誕登道岸默契
心淵謂王號非孔聖所安而像塑寔夷風未
改無臣爲有尚杜請于門人假幻卽眞奚
甘誣於佛氏遂定
先師之號正名必先乎□更遺像之儀存神
其至矣矧子無先食暨新
啓聖之祠而爵必因生悉定羣賢之配洗往
時之陋制成曠古之偉觀顧惟我
朝以來爰自
===
太祖而下稽古正學首舉彛章釋奠登歌特行
初服乃義起大作爲於
今日而
重臨獨超邁乎前聞蓋道隆則從而隆無嫌
自屈惟
主聖然後知聖不待人言爰涓令辰肆傳
清蹕
六龍翼其戾止道見泰來萬象率以景從喜
先豫動雅樂繼作金絲分孔壁之藏祀事
punctuated:
手不停披而學古有獲，誕登道岸，默契心淵。謂王號非孔聖所安，而像塑寔夷風未改。無臣爲有，尚杜請于門人；假幻卽眞，奚甘誣於佛氏？遂定先師之號，正名必先乎□；更遺像之儀，存神其至矣！矧子無先食，暨新啓聖之祠；而爵必因生，悉定羣賢之配。洗往時之陋制，成曠古之偉觀。
顧惟我朝以來，爰自太祖而下，稽古正學，首舉彛章。釋奠登歌，特行初服。乃義起大作爲於今日，而重臨獨超邁乎前聞。蓋道隆則從而隆，無嫌自屈；惟主聖然後知聖，不待人言。爰涓令辰，肆傳清蹕。六龍翼其戾止，道見泰來；萬象率以景從，喜先豫動。雅樂繼作，金絲分孔壁之藏；祀事
translation_en:
…His hands never cease turning the pages, and his study of antiquity yields understanding. He has grandly reached the shore of the Way and silently grasped the depths of the sage’s heart. He judged that the title of king was not one with which the sage Kong would have been at ease, and that sculpted images were indeed an unreformed foreign custom. Even when his disciples proposed treating him as having retainers when he had none, he rejected their request; how, then, could he willingly suffer the misrepresentation of Buddhist practice, which takes illusion for reality? Thus Your Majesty established his designation as First Teacher: rectification of names must begin with □ [illegible]. You changed the ritual treatment of his images: surely this was the utmost in preserving his spiritual presence! Moreover, a son must not partake of offerings before his father, and so you newly established the Shrine to the Sage’s Progenitor. Titles of nobility must accord with those held in life, and you fully regulated the associated worship of the assembled worthies. You swept away the defective institutions of former times and created a magnificent spectacle unmatched in antiquity.
Considering our dynasty, from Taizu onward, its rulers examined antiquity and rectified learning, giving precedence to the established rites. The sacrificial offerings to Confucius and the songs performed in the hall were specially conducted upon the ruler’s accession. Now, guided by what is right, Your Majesty has undertaken great reforms, and your renewed visit surpasses all previous accounts. For when the Way is exalted, the honors accorded it are correspondingly exalted; you feel no hesitation in humbling yourself. Only a sage ruler can recognize a sage, without needing others to tell him. An auspicious day was therefore selected, and the calls to clear the imperial route were transmitted. The six dragons bore you on your arrival, and the Way witnessed the advent of peace and prosperity. All things followed reverently, joy stirring even before the music began. The elegant ritual music then sounded in succession, its bells and strings sharing in the legacy preserved within the walls of Kong’s house [?]; the sacrificial rites…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
肅將玉帛委
上方之貢
至禮不讓
明德惟馨儀視昔爲有加道于今而益顯旣
寧圭璧遂列縉紳廣厦細旃深繹古人淵
海升堂入室弘開夫子宫墻雲仍來三氏
之雝雝懷深豐芑橋門圜多士之濟濟樂
極菁莪
大禮旣成
===
一人有慶臣等欣逢
盛事愧匪宿儒
賜坐講易書已知過望開卷對賢聖敢不昌
言蓋嘗陋稚圭之說詩解頤亦旣慕正叔
之積誠悟
主伏願
典學念于終始無怠無荒
潛心見於羹墻亦趨亦步與治同道以經法
天合謨曰嘉圖幾而康庶事說天莫辨養
punctuated:
肅將，玉帛委上方之貢。至禮不讓，明德惟馨。儀視昔爲有加，道于今而益顯。旣寧圭璧，遂列縉紳。廣厦細旃，深繹古人淵海；升堂入室，弘開夫子宫墻。雲仍來三氏之雝雝，懷深豐芑；橋門圜多士之濟濟，樂極菁莪。
大禮旣成，一人有慶。臣等欣逢盛事，愧匪宿儒。賜坐講易書，已知過望；開卷對賢聖，敢不昌言？蓋嘗陋稚圭之說詩解頤，亦旣慕正叔之積誠悟主。伏願典學念于終始，無怠無荒；潛心見於羹墻，亦趨亦步。與治同道，以經法天；合謨曰嘉，圖幾而康庶事；說天莫辨，養
translation_en:
…reverently performed, with jade and silk presented as tribute from the imperial household. In the highest rites there is no yielding; luminous virtue alone gives forth fragrance. The ceremonies surpass those of former times, and the Way shines still more clearly today. Once the jade tablets and discs had been duly placed, the assembled officials took their stations. In the spacious hall, upon fine felt mats, the profound learning of the ancients was explored; ascending the hall and entering the inner chamber, the precincts of the Master’s teaching were opened wide. Descendants of the three families arrived in harmony, inspiring deep concern for posterity, as in “Luxuriant Millet.” Around the gate of the encircling waterway gathered a dignified host of scholars, bringing the joy of “Luxuriant Southernwood” to its fullest expression.
The great rite has been completed, and the One Man enjoys felicity. We, your servants, rejoice to have encountered this splendid occasion, ashamed that we are not veteran scholars. To be granted seats and to lecture on the Changes and the Documents already exceeded our hopes. Opening the books and facing the sages and worthies, how could we dare withhold forthright words? We have thought little of Zhigui’s exposition of the Odes that elicited smiles, and have admired Zhengshu’s accumulated sincerity that brought understanding to his ruler. We humbly pray that Your Majesty keep sacred learning in mind from beginning to end, neither slothful nor neglectful; concentrate your heart until the sages seem present in your soup and upon your walls, following their every movement and step. Follow the same Way as good government, and through the Classics take Heaven as your model. Let deliberations accord and be pronounced excellent; attend to the first stirrings of events and bring all affairs into good order. Speak of Heaven without disputation [?], and nurture…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
賢以及萬民臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第參場
策五道
第一問
===
楊子充
同考試官教諭崔批
聖製一策重在我
祖宗明經衛道之意子能敷答詳明末復歸重於科目反本之論誠非
專務文字之學者宜錄以式
同考試官教諭劉批此策稽古正學關繫
今日作人之要機子能因事効忠惓惓不置可以為
明天子獻矣
考試官學正孫批考議詳盡
punctuated:
賢以及萬民。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第參場
策五道
第一問
楊子充
同考試官教諭崔批：「聖製一策，重在我祖宗明經衛道之意。子能敷答詳明，末復歸重於科目反本之論，誠非專務文字之學者，宜錄以式。」
同考試官教諭劉批：「此策稽古正學，關繫今日作人之要機。子能因事効忠，惓惓不置，可以為明天子獻矣。」
考試官學正孫批：「考議詳盡。」
translation_en:
…the worthy, and thereby all the people. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Sagely Majesty with the utmost fervor and trembling reverence. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks and make them known to Your Majesty.
Third Session
Five Policy Questions
First Question
Yang Zichong
Comment by Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor: “This imperially composed policy question centers on our imperial ancestors’ intention to elucidate the Classics and defend the Way. You have developed your answer fully and clearly, and at the end return to emphasize the argument that the examination system should return to its foundations. You are truly a scholar whose concern extends beyond literary composition alone. This should be selected as a model.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “This policy question examines antiquity and rectifies learning, bearing upon the crucial means of nurturing talent today. You have taken the occasion to demonstrate your loyalty with unremitting devotion. This may be presented to our enlightened Son of Heaven.”
Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: “The examination and discussion are thorough and exhaustive.”

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授張批講求切實可錄
昔者夫子之敎始於詩書而終於禮樂蓋
其門弟子身通六藝者七十而可與言詩
獨二子焉其一子夏於春秋猶不能贊一
辭也說經豈不難哉此我
聖祖
神宗罷黜百家表章六學道大如天而祗承終
鮮其人也伏覩
高皇帝開科舉
===
詔易主程氏朱氏古註疏書蔡氏傳古註疏春
秋左氏公羊穀梁胡氏張洽傳詩朱氏傳
古註疏禮記古註疏非朱子學校貢舉議
諸經各立家法而皆以註疏為主之謂乎
又伏覩
文皇帝御製性理大全書序曰乃者命儒臣集
諸家傳註而為大全凡有發明經義者取之
悖於經㫖者去之又
諭諸臣曰務極精備庶幾以垂後世非朱子學
punctuated:
考試官教授張批：講求切實，可錄。

昔者夫子之敎，始於詩書而終於禮樂。蓋其門弟子身通六藝者七十，而可與言詩，獨二子焉。其一子夏，於春秋猶不能贊一辭也。說經豈不難哉？此我聖祖神宗罷黜百家，表章六學，道大如天，而祗承終鮮其人也。伏覩高皇帝開科舉，詔：「易主程氏、朱氏、古註疏；書，蔡氏傳、古註疏；春秋，左氏、公羊、穀梁、胡氏、張洽傳；詩，朱氏傳、古註疏；禮記，古註疏。」非朱子《學校貢舉議》諸經各立家法，而皆以註疏為主之謂乎？又伏覩文皇帝御製《性理大全書》序曰：「乃者命儒臣集諸家傳註而為大全，凡有發明經義者取之，悖於經㫖者去之。」又諭諸臣曰：「務極精備，庶幾以垂後世。」非朱子學
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: “The inquiry is practical and sound; this merits inclusion.”

In former times, the Master’s teaching began with the Odes and Documents and culminated in rites and music. Among his disciples, seventy had personally mastered the Six Arts, yet only two could discuss the Odes with him. Even one of these, Zixia, could not contribute a single word to the Spring and Autumn Annals. Is interpreting the classics not difficult? Thus our sagely ancestors and divine forebears rejected the Hundred Schools and gave prominence to the six branches of classical learning. Their Way was as vast as Heaven, yet those capable of reverently carrying it forward have always been few.

I humbly observe that when Emperor Gao established the civil-service examinations, he decreed: “For the Changes, use as principal authorities Cheng, Zhu, and the ancient commentaries and subcommentaries; for the Documents, Cai’s commentary and the ancient commentaries and subcommentaries; for the Spring and Autumn Annals, the commentaries of Zuo, Gongyang, Guliang, Hu, and Zhang Qia; for the Odes, Zhu’s commentary and the ancient commentaries and subcommentaries; for the Record of Rites, the ancient commentaries and subcommentaries.” Is this not what Master Zhu meant in his Proposal on Schools and Tribute Recommendations: that each classic should have its own established interpretive tradition, while all should take the commentaries and subcommentaries as their principal authorities?

I further humbly observe that Emperor Wen’s imperially composed preface to the Complete Compendium of Human Nature and Principle states: “Recently I ordered the Confucian officials to gather the commentaries of the various schools and compile a comprehensive collection. Whatever elucidates the meaning of the classics is to be included; whatever contradicts their purport is to be excluded.” He further instructed his officials: “Strive for the utmost refinement and completeness, so that this may be handed down to later generations.” Is this not [what is said in] Master Zhu’s Schools …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
校貢舉議易兼取胡瑗石介歐陽脩王安
石邵雍程頤張載呂大臨楊時書兼取劉
敞王安石蘇軾程頤楊時晁說之葉夢得
吳棫薛季宣呂祖謙詩兼取歐陽脩蘇軾
程頤張載王安石呂大臨楊時呂祖謙周
禮則劉敞王安石楊時儀禮則劉敞二戴
禮記則劉敞程頤張載呂大臨春秋則啖
助趙匡陸淳孫明復劉敞程頤胡安國大
學論語中庸孟子則集解等書而蘇軾王
===
雱吳棫胡寅等說亦皆可采之謂乎
文謨
武烈丕顯丕承雖考諸三王而不謬建諸天地
而不悖質諸鬼神而無疑百世以俟聖人
而不惑可也執事以為今諸臣所編大全
書者果能盡合
宸慮否乎竊謂註疏讖緯之文雖所當芟而漢
魏相傳音讀訓詁制度名物所存言無微
而可畧小註引入諸說雖多可取而宋元
punctuated:
校貢舉議》，《易》兼取胡瑗、石介、歐陽脩、王安石、邵雍、程頤、張載、呂大臨、楊時，《書》兼取劉敞、王安石、蘇軾、程頤、楊時、晁說之、葉夢得、吳棫、薛季宣、呂祖謙，《詩》兼取歐陽脩、蘇軾、程頤、張載、王安石、呂大臨、楊時，《周禮》則劉敞、王安石、楊時，《儀禮》則劉敞，二戴《禮記》則劉敞、程頤、張載、呂大臨，《春秋》則啖助、趙匡、陸淳、孫明復、劉敞、程頤、胡安國，《大學》、《論語》、《中庸》、《孟子》則《集解》等書，而蘇軾、王雱、吳棫、胡寅等說亦皆可采之謂乎？
文謨武烈，丕顯丕承，雖考諸三王而不謬，建諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而無疑，百世以俟聖人而不惑，可也。執事以為今諸臣所編《大全》書者，果能盡合宸慮否乎？竊謂註疏讖緯之文雖所當芟，而漢魏相傳音讀、訓詁、制度、名物所存，言無微而可畧。小註引入諸說雖多可取，而宋元
translation_en:
…[Zhu Xi’s] Discussion of Schools and Tribute Examinations: for the Book of Changes, drawing also on Hu Yuan, Shi Jie, Ouyang Xiu, Wang Anshi, Shao Yong, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, Lü Dalin, and Yang Shi; for the Book of Documents, drawing also on Liu Chang, Wang Anshi, Su Shi, Cheng Yi, Yang Shi, Chao Shuozhi, Ye Mengde, Wu Yu, Xue Jixuan, and Lü Zuqian; for the Book of Odes, drawing also on Ouyang Xiu, Su Shi, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, Wang Anshi, Lü Dalin, and Yang Shi; for the Rites of Zhou, on Liu Chang, Wang Anshi, and Yang Shi; for the Ceremonies and Rites, on Liu Chang; for the Records of Rites of the two Dai masters, on Liu Chang, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, and Lü Dalin; for the Spring and Autumn Annals, on Dan Zhu, Zhao Kuang, Lu Chun, Sun Mingfu, Liu Chang, Cheng Yi, and Hu Anguo; and for the Great Learning, Analects, Doctrine of the Mean, and Mencius, on the Collected Explanations and other works, while also admitting the interpretations of Su Shi, Wang Pang, Wu Yu, Hu Yin, and others—is this not what he meant?
Their civil counsels and martial achievements were grandly manifested and grandly carried forward. One may indeed say that, tested against the Three Kings, they show no error; established before Heaven and Earth, they present no contradiction; examined before ghosts and spirits, they admit no doubt; and, even awaiting a sage a hundred generations hence, they give rise to no perplexity. Do you, sir, believe that the Complete Compendia now compiled by the ministers truly accord in every respect with the imperial intent? In my humble view, although passages concerning prophetic texts and apocryphal writings in the commentaries and subcommentaries ought to be excised, the pronunciations, textual glosses, institutions, and names of things preserved therein and transmitted from the Han and Wei contain no statement so minute that it may be omitted. Although many of the interpretations incorporated in the subsidiary notes are worth adopting, during the Song and Yuan…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
之間圖解雜出大意主於自衒而不盡以
釋經擇不可以不精至如胡石以下諸儒
朱子固謂借曰未必盡是亦當究其所以
得失之故而後反求諸心以正其謬宜各
自爲書以備一家而朱子論孟精義等書
則濂洛以來精蘊畧具尤世之不可無者
劉歆有云與其過而廢之寧過而立之况
傳聖人之經乎謂宜及今
聖神天子崇儒右文善繼善述以時明言於
===
朝
請發金匱石室之祕遣使購求四方遺書
簡命大儒詳加討葺使經生學士獲畢力於其
間將來舉子答義各以本註爲主條舉衆
說而斷以已意但令直述聖賢本旨與其
施用之實不必如今時文分段對股敷衍
浮詞一返洪武初
詔不拘舊格唯務經旨通暢之舊以昭
一代制作之大則於世敎固不無小補也失今
punctuated: 之間，圖解雜出，大意主於自衒，而不盡以釋經，擇不可以不精。至如胡石以下諸儒，朱子固謂，借曰未必盡是，亦當究其所以得失之故，而後反求諸心，以正其謬，宜各自爲書，以備一家。而朱子《論孟精義》等書，則濂洛以來精蘊畧具，尤世之不可無者。劉歆有云：「與其過而廢之，寧過而立之。」况傳聖人之經乎？謂宜及今聖神天子崇儒右文，善繼善述，以時明言於朝，請發金匱石室之祕，遣使購求四方遺書，簡命大儒，詳加討葺，使經生學士獲畢力於其間。將來舉子答義，各以本註爲主，條舉衆說，而斷以已意，但令直述聖賢本旨與其施用之實，不必如今時文分段對股，敷衍浮詞。一返洪武初詔不拘舊格、唯務經旨通暢之舊，以昭一代制作之大，則於世敎固不無小補也。失今
translation_en:
…during that period, diagrams and explanations appeared in profusion, chiefly intended for self-display rather than wholly devoted to elucidating the Classics; selection therefore requires the utmost care. As for the scholars from Hu and Shi [?] onward, Master Zhu indeed held that, even if their views were not entirely correct, one should investigate why they were right or wrong, and then turn back to examine one’s own mind in order to correct their errors. Their writings should each form a separate book, preserving the views of an individual school. Master Zhu’s Essential Meanings of the Analects and Mencius and similar works contain in broad outline the profound insights transmitted since the Lian and Luo schools; these, especially, are works the world cannot do without. Liu Xin once said: “Rather than err by discarding it, better to err by establishing it.” How much more does this apply to transmitting the Classics of the sages!

I submit that we should take advantage of the present moment, when our sagely and divine Son of Heaven honors Confucian learning and esteems literary culture, ably carrying forward and elaborating his predecessors’ work, to speak plainly at court. We should request that the treasured holdings of the golden coffers and stone chambers be opened, that envoys be dispatched to purchase surviving books from every region, and that eminent Confucian scholars be selected and commissioned to examine and compile them in detail, allowing students of the Classics and learned men to devote their full efforts to the undertaking. Henceforth, when examination candidates answer questions on the meaning of the Classics, each should take the principal commentary as his basis, enumerate the various interpretations, and adjudicate among them according to his own judgment. They should simply state directly the original purport of the sages and worthies and its practical application, without having to divide their essays into sections and paired passages, elaborating empty phrases as contemporary examination prose does. Let us return entirely to the former practice prescribed by the decree of the early Hongwu reign: to disregard established formats and strive only to make the meaning of the Classics clear and coherent. This would manifest the greatness of our dynasty’s institutional achievements and would surely make some modest contribution to moral instruction in the world. If the present opportunity is missed…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
不圖數年之後經籍散逸俗靡轉甚偏儒
曲士反得乗吾之虛以售其支離徑截之
謬而六經眞為贅矣可不慮哉然吾聞朱
子之議貢舉也門人或疑卒未有考官者
言得人之難也執事誠欲祗若
文命使學者復見天地之純全以漸復先王之
盛必如明道先生熈寧之議特集天下名
儒相與講明正學以次分教中外養賢斂
才然後可以一道德同風俗而盡革其末
===
流之弊若夫端本澄源則又自吾
君取人以身始惟有道者加之意焉謹對
第二問
薛欽
同考試官教諭沈批春秋史學之宗遷固以下豈
足與此子能推本言之而歸重有關於
君德可以占其所存矣
同考試官學正蔡批以誠字立說最得史學之本宜錄
考試官學正孫批論史學得㫖□□
punctuated:
不圖，數年之後，經籍散逸，俗靡轉甚，偏儒曲士反得乗吾之虛，以售其支離徑截之謬，而六經眞為贅矣，可不慮哉？然吾聞朱子之議貢舉也，門人或疑卒未有考官者，言得人之難也。執事誠欲祗若文命，使學者復見天地之純全，以漸復先王之盛，必如明道先生熈寧之議，特集天下名儒，相與講明正學，以次分教中外，養賢斂才，然後可以一道德，同風俗，而盡革其末流之弊。若夫端本澄源，則又自吾君取人以身始，惟有道者加之意焉。謹對。

第二問
薛欽

同考試官教諭沈批：「春秋，史學之宗，遷、固以下豈足與？此子能推本言之，而歸重有關於君德，可以占其所存矣。」

同考試官學正蔡批：「以誠字立說，最得史學之本，宜錄。」

考試官學正孫批：「論史學得㫖□□。」
translation_en:
…if no measures are taken, within a few years the canonical writings will have become scattered and lost, and the decline of prevailing ways will have grown still worse. Narrow-minded scholars and misguided men of learning will instead exploit our weakness to peddle their errors of fragmented interpretation and shortcuts, and the Six Classics will truly become superfluous. Can this fail to cause concern? Yet I have heard that when Master Zhu discussed recruitment through the examinations, some disciples raised the concern that, in the end, there would be no suitable examiners. They were speaking of the difficulty of finding the right men. If you, sir, sincerely wish reverently to follow the imperial mandate for civil governance, to enable scholars once again to perceive the unsullied wholeness of Heaven and Earth, and gradually to restore the flourishing order of the former kings, you must follow Master Mingdao’s proposal of the Xining era: specially assemble the renowned Confucian scholars of the realm to elucidate orthodox learning together, then assign them in due order to teach at the capital and in the provinces, nurturing worthy men and gathering talent. Only then can moral principles be unified, customs made uniform, and all the abuses of subsequent degeneration eradicated. As for rectifying the root and clarifying the source, this must begin with our ruler’s setting a personal example in selecting men. May those who possess the Way give this their attention. Respectfully submitted in reply.

Second Policy Question
Xue Qin

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “The Spring and Autumn Annals is the fountainhead of historical scholarship. How could Sima Qian, Ban Gu, or their successors compare with it? This candidate can trace the matter to its roots in his discussion and ultimately places the emphasis on its bearing upon the ruler’s virtue. From this one can discern what he holds in his heart.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, Director of Studies: “By building his argument around the word ‘sincerity,’ he has grasped the foundation of historical scholarship particularly well. He deserves selection.”

Comment by Examiner Sun, Director of Studies: “His discussion of historical scholarship grasps its essential meaning. [Two illegible characters.]”

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授張批討論精確
春秋之所是天之所命也春秋之所非天
之所討也春秋是非之極與天地合其德
日月合其明四時合其序鬼神合其吉凶
先天而天弗違後天而奉天時況於人乎
明乎此者可與論史矣上焉者知誠之不
可掩也不見是圖敢文過乎而不得書者
鮮矣下焉者知誠之不可掩也君舉必書
肯徇人乎而不敢書者鮮矣執事舉唐虞
===
三代及遷固諸史得失下問夫豈不以古
者左史記言右史記動太史掌六典八法
八則藏約劑正歲年頒告朔辨事協禮讀
誄賜諡而天文繫世昭穆八柄會計納訪
策命事書制祿四方之志三皇五帝之書
萬民之治令皆典于其屬周知天下之故
史佚史克史蘇史黯史趙史墨又世掌之
未嘗易業貳事故其史爲經而唐宋以來
史臣執筆隨諫官上殿徒立故事宰相記
punctuated:
考試官敎授張批：討論精確。

春秋之所是，天之所命也；春秋之所非，天之所討也。春秋是非之極，與天地合其德，日月合其明，四時合其序，鬼神合其吉凶；先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時，況於人乎？明乎此者，可與論史矣。上焉者知誠之不可掩也，不見是圖，敢文過乎？而不得書者鮮矣。下焉者知誠之不可掩也，君舉必書，肯徇人乎？而不敢書者鮮矣。執事舉唐虞、三代及遷、固諸史得失下問，夫豈不以古者左史記言，右史記動，太史掌六典、八法、八則，藏約劑，正歲年，頒告朔，辨事協禮，讀誄賜諡，而天文、繫世、昭穆、八柄、會計、納訪、策命、事書、制祿、四方之志、三皇五帝之書、萬民之治令，皆典于其屬，周知天下之故。史佚、史克、史蘇、史黯、史趙、史墨，又世掌之，未嘗易業貳事，故其史爲經。而唐宋以來，史臣執筆，隨諫官上殿，徒立故事，宰相記
translation_en:
Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: The discussion is precise.

What the Spring and Autumn Annals approves is what Heaven commands; what the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns is what Heaven punishes. In its ultimate judgments of right and wrong, the Spring and Autumn Annals accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth, in illumination with the sun and moon, in order with the four seasons, and in judgments of good and ill fortune with ghosts and spirits. When it precedes Heaven, Heaven does not oppose it; when it follows Heaven, it observes Heaven’s seasons. How much more must this hold for human beings! Those who understand this may be engaged in a discussion of history. Those above, knowing that the truth cannot be concealed, attend to what is unseen: would they dare gloss over their faults? Thus there are few things that historians are prevented from recording. Those below, knowing that the truth cannot be concealed, invariably record the ruler’s actions: would they consent to accommodate anyone’s wishes? Thus there are few things that they dare not record.

You, honored examiners, have condescended to ask about the merits and shortcomings of the various histories of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, and those by Sima Qian and Ban Gu. Surely this is because, in antiquity, the Scribe of the Left recorded words and the Scribe of the Right recorded actions. The Grand Scribe had charge of the Six Statutes, Eight Regulations, and Eight Rules; preserved covenants and contracts; corrected the calendar; promulgated announcements of the first day of the month; distinguished duties and coordinated rites; and read eulogies and conferred posthumous names. Astronomy, genealogical succession, ancestral precedence, the eight instruments of government, accounting, the reception of counsel [?], written investitures, records of affairs, the regulation of stipends, accounts of the four quarters, writings concerning the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, and ordinances governing the people were all in the keeping of his subordinate offices. They comprehensively understood the affairs of the realm. The scribes Yi, Ke, Su, An, Zhao, and Mo, moreover, held these responsibilities hereditarily, never changing their occupation or dividing their attention among other duties. Hence their histories became classics.

Since the Tang and Song, however, the historiographers have taken up their brushes and followed the Remonstrance Officials into the audience hall, merely maintaining an established formality, while the chief councilors recorded…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
注學士脩撰止憑諸司供報事關得失皆
不記錄惟書除目辭見據此銓次謂之日
曆又必錄本進呈有不得書不敢書者異
時脩史率臆度於數百年之後筆削於衆
人之手竄易靡常迄無定論唯漢初太史
公位丞相上郡國計書先上太史公副上
宰相猶有古意而遷固父子家學相傳用
法專一發凡起例動有矩度西都風俗文
體大畧簡朴故辭直事核與後世雕飾駢
===
儷文工而實不至者弗類斯爲彼善邪然
吾觀遷書大抵發憤蠶室之辱意有所鬱
結而不得通欲垂空言以自見耳非有不
虛美隱惡之實也故是非頗謬於聖人而
固不學剽竊殆甚於遷况武帝常怒遷議
已收景武二紀自毀之而封禪平準等書
意多隱訕要亦未爲得書敢書也世徒喜
其文詞辯麗奇偉見史之難爲憾無遷固
之才豈知史之失自遷固始文中子之評
punctuated: 注，學士脩撰，止憑諸司供報，事關得失皆不記錄，惟書除目、辭見。據此銓次，謂之日曆，又必錄本進呈，有不得書、不敢書者。異時脩史，率臆度於數百年之後，筆削於衆人之手，竄易靡常，迄無定論。唯漢初太史公位丞相上，郡國計書先上太史公，副上宰相，猶有古意。而遷固父子家學相傳，用法專一，發凡起例，動有矩度。西都風俗文體大畧簡朴，故辭直事核，與後世雕飾駢儷、文工而實不至者弗類。斯爲彼善邪？然吾觀遷書，大抵發憤蠶室之辱，意有所鬱結而不得通，欲垂空言以自見耳，非有不虛美隱惡之實也。故是非頗謬於聖人，而固不學，剽竊殆甚於遷。况武帝常怒遷議已，收景武二紀，自毀之，而封禪、平準等書，意多隱訕，要亦未爲得書敢書也。世徒喜其文詞辯麗奇偉，見史之難爲，憾無遷固之才，豈知史之失自遷固始？文中子之評
translation_en:
…notes, with academicians undertaking compilation, relying solely on reports supplied by the various offices. Matters bearing on successes and failures were left unrecorded; only lists of appointments and audiences on departure or arrival were entered. These materials were arranged in sequence and called the Daily Calendar. A copy also had to be submitted for imperial inspection, so there were things that could not be written and things that no one dared write. When histories were subsequently compiled, conjectures were generally made several hundred years after the events, and editorial judgments passed through many hands. Alterations were incessant, and no settled assessment was ever reached. Only in the early Han did the Grand Astrologer rank above the Chief Minister: the accounting reports from commanderies and kingdoms were first submitted to the Grand Astrologer, with duplicates sent to the Chief Minister. This still retained something of the ancient spirit. In the families of Sima Qian and Ban Gu, learning was transmitted from father to son; their methods were consistent, and their formulation of principles and establishment of conventions always followed definite standards. The customs and literary style of the Western Han were generally simple and unadorned. Their language was therefore straightforward and their accounts factual, unlike the ornate parallel prose of later generations, accomplished in expression but deficient in substance. Does this make those earlier historians superior?

Yet when I examine Sima Qian’s book, I find that it largely vents his indignation at the humiliation of the castration chamber. His feelings were pent up and could find no release; he merely wished to leave his words to posterity and thereby make himself known. He did not actually achieve the standard of avoiding false praise and the concealment of evil. His judgments of right and wrong thus diverged considerably from those of the sages. Ban Gu, moreover, lacked learning, and his plagiarism was perhaps even worse than Sima Qian’s. Furthermore, Emperor Wu once became angry at Sima Qian for criticizing him [?], seized the two Basic Annals of Emperors Jing and Wu, and personally destroyed them. The Treatises on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices and on the Balanced Standard, among others, contain much veiled disparagement. In the end, Sima Qian cannot be said to have been free to write or to have dared to write without restraint either. People merely delight in the eloquence, beauty, originality, and grandeur of their language. Seeing how difficult it is to write history, they lament the absence of talents like Sima Qian and Ban Gu. How could they know that the failings of historical writing began with Sima Qian and Ban Gu? Wenzhongzi’s assessment …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
已爲不刊則於曄壽喬約諸史奚必置低
昂于其間哉顧甞聞之自古人君出入起
居皆有史女史內史外史是也史無一日
無書以日繫月以月繫時以時繫年是也
而近日記載之畧殆有逾於宋者甞讀虞
書叙堯舜禹臯君臣之明聖率不越乎都
俞吁咈之間非當時善言德行者審視詳
記固未易弁其精意而傳之而公羊曰所
見異詞所聞異詞所傳聞異詞雖孔子作
===
春秋於定哀則其事詳於隱莊則其事畧
况其下乎是則老成之深慮而記曰王前
巫後史中心無爲也以守至正史之有關
於君德又如此執事安得以爲迂緩而忽
之哉謹對
第三問
鄭富
同考試官訓導李 批 辯論師友是非言簡義明蓋
胷中素有定見者
punctuated:
已爲不刊，則於曄、壽、喬、約諸史，奚必置低昂于其間哉？顧甞聞之，自古人君出入起居皆有史，女史、內史、外史是也。史無一日無書，以日繫月，以月繫時，以時繫年是也。而近日記載之畧，殆有逾於宋者。甞讀《虞書》，叙堯、舜、禹、臯君臣之明聖，率不越乎都、俞、吁、咈之間。非當時善言德行者審視詳記，固未易弁其精意而傳之。而《公羊》曰：「所見異詞，所聞異詞，所傳聞異詞。」雖孔子作《春秋》，於定、哀則其事詳，於隱、莊則其事畧，况其下乎？是則老成之深慮。而《記》曰：「王前巫後史，中心無爲也，以守至正。」史之有關於君德又如此，執事安得以爲迂緩而忽之哉？謹對。
第三問
鄭富
同考試官訓導李批：辯論師友是非，言簡義明，蓋胷中素有定見者。
translation_en:
…has already become an unalterable judgment. Why, then, must one rank the histories of Ye, Shou, Qiao, and Yue against one another? Yet I have heard that from antiquity rulers had scribes attending their departures and returns, their rising and resting: the Palace Woman Scribes, Interior Scribes, and Exterior Scribes were such officials. Not a day passed without the scribes making a record, arranging days under months, months under seasons, and seasons under years. Yet the scantiness of recent records seems even to exceed that of the Song.
I once read the Book of Yu. Its account of the enlightened sagacity of the rulers and ministers Yao, Shun, Yu, and Gao scarcely extends beyond their exclamations of praise, assent, hesitation, and dissent. Had those responsible for recording worthy words and virtuous deeds at the time not observed carefully and recorded fully, it would certainly have been difficult to distinguish [?] and transmit their essential meaning. The Gongyang Commentary says: “What was witnessed is worded differently; what was heard is worded differently; what was received through transmitted reports is worded differently.” Even when Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, his accounts of events under Dukes Ding and Ai were detailed, while those under Dukes Yin and Zhuang were brief. How much more must this be true of lesser historians? This, then, is a matter for the profound concern of mature and experienced men.
The Book of Rites says: “Before the king is a shaman, and behind him a scribe; within his heart he takes no arbitrary action, thereby preserving utmost rectitude.” Such, moreover, is the bearing of scribes upon the ruler’s virtue. How could you, sir, dismiss this as impractical and dilatory, and neglect it? I respectfully submit this reply.
Third Question
Zheng Fu
Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor: “He distinguishes and discusses right and wrong concerning teachers and friends. His language is concise and his meaning clear; evidently he has long held settled judgments in his mind.”

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭文批剖析學術淵源之正歸重曾
子其所養可占矣取之
考試官學正孫批有歸宿
考試官教授張批議論明正
孰不爲學學於舜之門舜之徒也學於蹠
之門蹠之徒也孰不爲學學於舜之門由
蹠之道蹠之徒也學於蹠之門由舜之道
舜之徒也昔者吳起師曾參曾參大孝吳
起忘親道相反者也况參旣先起未求將
===
也而絕之起亦盡棄其學學兵法矣起猶
得爲曾子徒乎李斯事荀卿荀卿明王道
李斯棄王法埶相反者也然斯燔詩書滅
禮樂皆卿倨肆無忌謂性爲惡謂禮爲僞
謂孔子子思孟軻亂天下有以啓之斯不
得爲荀子徒乎凡老子所謂道德非吾所
謂道德雜權詐而爲言者也觀其書曰知
其雄守其雌爲天下谿知其白守其黑爲
天下谷其流入於機變殘忍非理所必至
punctuated:
同考試官教諭文批：剖析學術淵源之正，歸重曾子，其所養可占矣。取之。
考試官學正孫批：有歸宿。
考試官教授張批：議論明正。
孰不爲學？學於舜之門，舜之徒也；學於蹠之門，蹠之徒也。孰不爲學？學於舜之門，由蹠之道，蹠之徒也；學於蹠之門，由舜之道，舜之徒也。昔者吳起師曾參，曾參大孝，吳起忘親，道相反者也。况參旣先起未求將也而絕之，起亦盡棄其學，學兵法矣。起猶得爲曾子徒乎？李斯事荀卿，荀卿明王道，李斯棄王法，埶相反者也。然斯燔詩書，滅禮樂，皆卿倨肆無忌，謂性爲惡，謂禮爲僞，謂孔子、子思、孟軻亂天下，有以啓之。斯不得爲荀子徒乎？凡老子所謂道德，非吾所謂道德，雜權詐而爲言者也。觀其書曰：「知其雄，守其雌，爲天下谿；知其白，守其黑，爲天下谷。」其流入於機變殘忍，非理所必至
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor, comments: “He analyzes the authentic sources of learning and gives due weight to Zengzi. From this one can judge his own cultivation. Accept him.”
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “The argument reaches a definite conclusion.”
Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “The argument is clear and correct.”
Who does not pursue learning? One who studies at Shun’s gate is Shun’s disciple; one who studies at Zhi’s gate is Zhi’s disciple. Who does not pursue learning? One who studies at Shun’s gate but follows Zhi’s way is Zhi’s disciple; one who studies at Zhi’s gate but follows Shun’s way is Shun’s disciple. In former times, Wu Qi took Zeng Shen as his teacher. Zeng Shen was supremely filial, whereas Wu Qi forgot his parents: their ways were opposed. Moreover, Zeng Shen had already severed ties with Wu Qi before the latter sought a military command, and Wu Qi entirely abandoned his teaching to study military methods. Could Wu Qi still count as a disciple of Zengzi?
Li Si served Xun Qing as his teacher. Xun Qing elucidated the kingly Way, whereas Li Si abandoned the laws of the ancient kings: their courses were opposed. Yet Li Si’s burning of the Odes and Documents and destruction of ritual and music were all prompted in some measure by Xun Qing’s unrestrained arrogance: he declared human nature evil, called ritual an artificial contrivance, and said that Kongzi, Zisi, and Meng Ke brought disorder to the world. Can Li Si be denied the status of a disciple of Xunzi?
Everything Laozi calls the Way and virtue is different from what we call the Way and virtue: his pronouncements mingle expediency and deceit. Consider what his book says: “Know the male, keep to the female, and become the ravine of the world; know the white, keep to the black, and become the valley of the world.” That this teaching should flow into cunning manipulation and cruelty—is this not its inevitable consequence…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
哉太史公曰申子卑卑施之於名實韓子
引繩墨切事情明是非其極慘礉少恩皆
原於道德之意有以也賈誼少從河南守
吳公吳公故與李斯同邑嘗學事焉吳公
之學雖無可考吾視其所舉大抵悻悻自
好喜功名嬰撫在廷之臣欲出其上故朱
子曰誼本戰國縱橫之學只是較近道理
不至如儀秦蔡范之甚耳則亦安見其真
能寒於水哉易曰頤貞吉養正則吉也觀
===
頤觀其所養也自求口實觀其自養也愚
於明問得養道焉荀卿老聃自養苟正必
不至以其學術禍天下後世以誼之才少
加持養又得聖賢為之依歸殆不止於通
達國體同死生輕去就如遷固所賛而已
故曰洙泗多賢儀秦皆詐非其性異養使
然也其唯曾子乎師孔子父曾皙友顏淵
由賜之流而仁以為己任故竟以魯得之
而傳獨得其宗觀於子思孟子可見矣學
punctuated: 哉？太史公曰：「申子卑卑，施之於名實；韓子引繩墨，切事情，明是非，其極慘礉少恩，皆原於道德之意。」有以也。賈誼少從河南守吳公，吳公故與李斯同邑，嘗學事焉。吳公之學雖無可考，吾視其所舉，大抵悻悻自好，喜功名，嬰撫在廷之臣，欲出其上。故朱子曰：「誼本戰國縱橫之學，只是較近道理，不至如儀秦蔡范之甚耳。」則亦安見其真能寒於水哉？易曰：「頤，貞吉。」養正則吉也。「觀頤」，觀其所養也；「自求口實」，觀其自養也。愚於明問得養道焉。荀卿、老聃自養苟正，必不至以其學術禍天下後世。以誼之才，少加持養，又得聖賢為之依歸，殆不止於通達國體、同死生、輕去就，如遷固所賛而已。故曰：「洙泗多賢，儀秦皆詐，非其性異，養使然也。」其唯曾子乎！師孔子，父曾皙，友顏淵、由、賜之流，而仁以為己任，故竟以魯得之，而傳獨得其宗，觀於子思、孟子可見矣。學
translation_en:
… is it not? The Grand Historian said: “Master Shen concerned himself with petty matters, applying his teachings to names and realities. Master Han employed the measuring line and ink cord, addressed the actual circumstances of affairs, and distinguished right from wrong. At their extremes, their teachings were harsh and unforgiving, yet all originated in the ideas of the Way and its Virtue.” There was reason for this judgment.

In his youth, Jia Yi studied under Lord Wu, Governor of Henan. Lord Wu originally came from the same town as Li Si and had studied under and served him. Although Lord Wu’s learning cannot be ascertained, when I consider the man he recommended, I find him generally headstrong and self-regarding, fond of achievement and fame, “yingfu” [?] toward the ministers at court, and eager to rise above them. Thus Master Zhu said: “Yi’s learning was fundamentally that of the Warring States persuaders who advocated vertical and horizontal alliances. It merely came somewhat closer to moral principle and did not reach the extremes of Zhang Yi, Su Qin, Cai Ze, and Fan Ju.” How, then, can we be sure that he truly became ‘colder than water’—surpassing his teacher?

The Book of Changes says: “Nourishment: steadfast correctness brings good fortune.” Correct nourishment brings good fortune. “Observe nourishment” means observing what a person nourishes; “Seek sustenance for your own mouth” means observing how a person nourishes himself. From your illuminating question, I have, in my humble understanding, grasped the way of nourishment. Had Xun Qing and Lao Dan nourished themselves correctly, their teachings could never have brought calamity upon the world and later generations. With Yi’s talents, had he applied himself a little more to maintaining and nourishing his character, and had he found his guiding support in the sages and worthies, he would surely have achieved more than understanding the essential principles of government, regarding life and death alike, and making light of departure from or continuance in office—the qualities for which Sima Qian and Ban Gu praised him.

Thus it is said: “Among those of the Zhu and Si rivers were many worthies; Zhang Yi and Su Qin were both deceitful. This was not because their natures differed: their nurture made them so.” Surely Master Zeng exemplifies this! His teacher was Confucius, his father Zeng Xi, and his friends Yan Yuan, Zhong You, Duanmu Ci, and their like. He took humaneness as his own responsibility. Thus, despite his dullness, he ultimately attained the Way, and in transmitting it uniquely grasped its fundamental purport. This can be seen in Zisi and Mencius. Students …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
者傳習親師論學取友其唯學曾子乎
第四問
王一言
同考試官教諭鄧批去文就實之意溢于尚友之外
同考試官教諭汪批景先賢律後學一以反本為
說讀之令人灑然
考試官學正孫批詳盡
考試官教授張批知本之論
文之將興者天也成之以人人之立身者
===
德也成之以學斯文之興必有豪傑之士
卓立以表世獨行以高尚者為之先焉苟
不知學猶德之偏也講學以成德德成而
行尊不合於道者鮮矣孰謂天之生才而
有不待學以成者哉閩為東南奧區實禹
貢要荒之外周漢而上文獻不得而徵矣
至唐中葉有歐陽詹氏與韓子聯第稱龍
虎榜而民始知學其舉韓愈為博士固非
同年之私稱何蕃之仁勇亦好德之良也
punctuated:
者傳習、親師、論學、取友，其唯學曾子乎？

第四問
王一言

同考試官教諭鄧批：去文就實之意，溢于尚友之外。
同考試官教諭汪批：景先賢，律後學，一以反本為說，讀之令人灑然。
考試官學正孫批：詳盡。
考試官教授張批：知本之論。

文之將興者，天也；成之以人。人之立身者，德也；成之以學。斯文之興，必有豪傑之士，卓立以表世、獨行以高尚者為之先焉。苟不知學，猶德之偏也。講學以成德，德成而行尊，不合於道者鮮矣。孰謂天之生才，而有不待學以成者哉？閩為東南奧區，實禹貢要荒之外，周漢而上，文獻不得而徵矣。至唐中葉，有歐陽詹氏，與韓子聯第，稱龍虎榜，而民始知學。其舉韓愈為博士，固非同年之私；稱何蕃之仁勇，亦好德之良也。
translation_en:
…those who study, transmitting and practicing what they learn, drawing close to teachers, discussing learning, and choosing friends—should they not take Zengzi as their model?

Fourth Question
Wang Yiyan

Comment by Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor: The intention to set aside literary ornament and pursue substance extends beyond the theme of befriending the worthy of antiquity.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: Honoring earlier worthies and setting standards for later students, the argument consistently advocates returning to the root. Reading it leaves one refreshed.
Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: Thorough and exhaustive.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: An argument that understands the root.

That cultural learning is about to flourish is Heaven’s doing; its fulfillment comes through human beings. What establishes a person in life is virtue; its fulfillment comes through learning. When this cultural tradition flourishes, there must first be outstanding men who stand firm as exemplars for their age and pursue an independent course of lofty conduct. If they do not understand learning, however, their virtue remains partial. Through the examination and discussion of learning, virtue is perfected; when virtue is perfected and conduct elevated, little will fail to accord with the Way. Who could say that among the talents Heaven brings forth, some need not rely on learning for their fulfillment?

Min is a heartland of the southeast, yet it lay beyond even the outermost Yao and Huang domains described in the Tribute of Yu. For the Zhou and Han periods and earlier, neither written records nor worthy men are available as evidence. By the middle of the Tang dynasty, Ouyang Zhan appeared. He passed the examination alongside Master Han on what was called the Dragon and Tiger List, and only then did the people begin to appreciate learning. His recommendation of Han Yu for appointment as an Erudite was certainly no mere favoritism toward a fellow graduate of the same year; his praise of He Fan’s benevolence and courage likewise showed the excellence of his love of virtue.

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
文集之傳雖不逮韓亦韓之儔已陳嘏氏
爲宣宗所知稱琬琰器而民始知仕長於
詞賦有相如之風尤工篆隸亦斯邈之流
也官箴之服雖止郎中亦有用之才已風
氣始開人文始著器業之大譽處之隆遽
已如此烏得不啓宋儒之盛哉楊億之文
蘇子病其詭矣而有忠清直亮之稱不然
孰爲學士而富貴弗之保也蘇頌之節朱
子稱其進退不苟古之大臣不然孰爲舍
===
人而落職弗之顧也曹輔初爲正字小官
耳敢論大事愛君之心也李綱出入將相
憂國忘身充此愛君之心而已是四人者
師友講習不少槩見而立朝大節邦家之
光雖曰未學吾必謂之學已其殆庶幾乎
程氏倡道於洛游楊受之龜山傳之豫章
豫章傳之延平朱子之聞道蓋自延平始
已故一則曰愚聞之師二則曰愚聞之師
其奉韋齋之命而稟學於屏山籍溪白水
punctuated:
文集之傳，雖不逮韓，亦韓之儔已。陳嘏氏爲宣宗所知，稱琬琰器，而民始知仕。長於詞賦，有相如之風；尤工篆隸，亦斯邈之流也。官箴之服，雖止郎中，亦有用之才已。風氣始開，人文始著，器業之大，譽處之隆，遽已如此，烏得不啓宋儒之盛哉？

楊億之文，蘇子病其詭矣，而有忠清直亮之稱。不然，孰爲學士而富貴弗之保也？蘇頌之節，朱子稱其進退不苟，古之大臣。不然，孰爲舍人而落職弗之顧也？曹輔初爲正字，小官耳，敢論大事，愛君之心也。李綱出入將相，憂國忘身，充此愛君之心而已。是四人者，師友講習不少槩見，而立朝大節，邦家之光。雖曰未學，吾必謂之學已，其殆庶幾乎！

程氏倡道於洛，游楊受之。龜山傳之豫章，豫章傳之延平，朱子之聞道，蓋自延平始已。故一則曰「愚聞之師」，二則曰「愚聞之師」。其奉韋齋之命，而稟學於屏山、籍溪、白水
translation_en:
Although his collected writings have not circulated as widely as Han Yu’s, he was nevertheless Han’s peer. Chen Gu won recognition from Emperor Xuanzong, who called him a vessel of precious jade, and the people then began to understand service in office. He excelled in literary compositions and rhapsodies, possessing the manner of Sima Xiangru; he was particularly accomplished in seal and clerical scripts, belonging also to the company of Li Si and Cheng Miao. Although his discharge of official duties extended only to the post of bureau director, he was nevertheless a man of useful talents. Just as the intellectual climate began to open and literary cultivation began to emerge, the greatness of men’s capacities and achievements, and the eminence of their reputation and standing [?], had already reached such heights. How could this have failed to usher in the flourishing of the Confucian scholars of the Song?

Master Su criticized Yang Yi’s writing for its eccentricity, yet Yang enjoyed a reputation for loyalty, purity, uprightness, and integrity. Otherwise, who, serving as an academician, would have declined to safeguard his wealth and eminence? Of Su Song’s integrity, Master Zhu said that he was scrupulous in both advancement and withdrawal, a great minister of the ancient kind. Otherwise, who, serving as a drafting official, would have disregarded dismissal from office? Cao Fu initially served as a proofreader, merely a minor official, yet he dared to discuss great affairs: this sprang from his devotion to his ruler. Li Gang served in military command and as chief councilor; in his concern for the state he forgot himself. This was simply the full realization of that same devotion to his ruler. Of these four men’s study and discussion with teachers and friends, scarcely anything is evident [?]; yet the great integrity they displayed at court brought glory to the state. The saying, “Though others say he has not studied, I would certainly call him learned,” surely comes close to describing them!

Master Cheng proclaimed the Way at Luoyang, and You and Yang received it. Guishan transmitted it to Yuzhang, and Yuzhang transmitted it to Yanping. Master Zhu’s learning of the Way began, indeed, with Yanping. Thus, time and again he said, “I, in my ignorance, heard this from my teacher.” In obeying Weizhai’s command and receiving instruction from Pingshan, Jixi, and Baishui …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
三君子者於韋齋友也其學未嘗不自伊
洛中來而延平所得者深矣先乎此若胡
文定氏得私淑之教於程門程門之得夫
正傳者莫如游楊也文定與之遊而言性
乃有同體異用之說二子寅宏之學又不
能無過與不及之差然正色危言剛大方
直之氣律貪起懦之功皆不忝其父焉噫
胡氏父子祖於伊洛德望偉然而精微未
造學莫便於近其人信矣後乎此若蔡神
===
與氏以聖賢之學教元定元定之教夫三
子者猶之神與也淵紹易學朱子有論撰
詳悉之稱沈紹書學又有須見帝王之心
之論而精識絕才不可屈之志不可窮之
辯則歸之季通焉噫蔡氏父祖子孫識趣
偉然好遯不汚而效用斯阻君子求其在
我者已矣文公季子召對理宗屢有啓迪
之益敭歷中外紹其宦學之傳寅宏淵沈
哲之參乎則在亦孔之鯉也黄勉齋受吾
punctuated: 三君子者，於韋齋友也。其學未嘗不自伊洛中來，而延平所得者深矣。先乎此，若胡文定氏得私淑之教於程門，程門之得夫正傳者莫如游、楊也。文定與之遊，而言性乃有同體異用之說。二子寅、宏之學，又不能無過與不及之差。然正色危言、剛大方直之氣，律貪起懦之功，皆不忝其父焉。噫！胡氏父子祖於伊洛，德望偉然，而精微未造，學莫便於近其人，信矣！後乎此，若蔡神與氏以聖賢之學教元定，元定之教夫三子者，猶之神與也。淵紹易學，朱子有論撰詳悉之稱；沈紹書學，又有須見帝王之心之論。而精識絕才、不可屈之志、不可窮之辯，則歸之季通焉。噫！蔡氏父祖子孫，識趣偉然，好遯不汚，而效用斯阻。君子求其在我者已矣。文公季子召對理宗，屢有啓迪之益，敭歷中外，紹其宦學之傳。寅、宏、淵、沈、哲之參乎，則在亦孔之鯉也。黄勉齋受吾
translation_en:
…the three gentlemen were friends of Weizhai. Their learning invariably derived from the Cheng school of Yi and Luo, but Yanping’s attainment was profound.

Earlier, Hu Wending received instruction indirectly through the Cheng school. Among its followers, none received the authentic transmission more fully than You and Yang. Wending associated with them, yet in discussing human nature he advanced the theory of a shared substance with differing functions. The learning of his two sons, Yin and Hong, likewise could not escape deviations of excess and deficiency. Nevertheless, in their grave bearing and forthright speech, their firm, expansive, upright spirit, and their achievement in restraining the covetous and rousing the timid, neither disgraced his father. Alas! The Hu father and sons took the Cheng school of Yi and Luo as their source and possessed imposing virtue and reputation, yet they had not attained its subtle profundities. Truly, nothing facilitates learning more than personal proximity to the teacher!

Later, Cai Shenyu taught Yuanding the learning of the sages and worthies; Yuanding taught his own three sons just as Shenyu had taught him. Yuan carried on the study of the Book of Changes, and Master Zhu praised the thoroughness of his discussions and writings. Shen carried on the study of the Book of Documents, and there was also the statement that one must discern the minds of the emperors and kings. But penetrating discernment, exceptional talent, an unyielding resolve, and inexhaustible powers of argument were attributed to Jitong. Alas! Across the generations, the Cai family possessed lofty discernment and aspirations, preferring withdrawal and remaining unsullied; yet their opportunity to put their abilities to use was thereby obstructed. The gentleman seeks only what lies within himself.

The youngest son of Wengong was summoned to an audience with Emperor Lizong and repeatedly provided beneficial enlightenment. He served in posts at court and in the provinces, continuing his father’s tradition of official service and learning. If ranked alongside Yin, Hong, Yuan, Shen, and Zhe [?], then Zai, too, was a counterpart to Kongzi’s son Li. Huang Mianzhai received the entrustment of our …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
道之托居敬窮理之功一時同遊無出其
右易禮通解之作發明經旨不負其師劉
雲莊講道武夷爲終焉之計及其仕也應
詔陳言乃請開不諱之門招盡言之士推
時政之得失明朝廷之是非雖未見其易
禮諸解而已知其人巳陳北溪辯陸氏之
學風力甚勁字義之作其庶幾乎廖子晦
守先師之道隱者爲高槎溪之集爲可稱
巳真西山蒙世大禁講學力行采羣書爲
===
衍義受知理宗而偽學之禁於是除焉雖
不及朱子之門亦有功於道者也勿軒以
道淑人從游者眾以經意爲標題輯文公
要語而門人之說皆附錄焉雖不得爲朱
子之徒亦聞風而起者也鄭仲實氏精於
禮學舉要從宜特爲西山所敬而邑人德
之亦是行其所學諸君子者雖道與時違
不獲盡用而講明心學昌斯道之傳不有
先哲孰開我人可忘所自乎黃氏曰孟子
punctuated: 道之托，居敬窮理之功，一時同遊無出其右。易禮通解之作，發明經旨，不負其師。劉雲莊講道武夷，爲終焉之計。及其仕也，應詔陳言，乃請開不諱之門，招盡言之士，推時政之得失，明朝廷之是非。雖未見其易禮諸解，而已知其人巳。陳北溪辯陸氏之學，風力甚勁，《字義》之作，其庶幾乎！廖子晦守先師之道，隱者爲高，《槎溪之集》爲可稱巳。真西山蒙世大禁，講學力行，采羣書爲《衍義》，受知理宗，而偽學之禁於是除焉。雖不及朱子之門，亦有功於道者也。勿軒以道淑人，從游者眾，以經意爲標題，輯文公要語，而門人之說皆附錄焉。雖不得爲朱子之徒，亦聞風而起者也。鄭仲實氏精於禮學，舉要從宜，特爲西山所敬，而邑人德之，亦是行其所學。諸君子者，雖道與時違，不獲盡用，而講明心學，昌斯道之傳。不有先哲，孰開我？人可忘所自乎？黃氏曰：「孟子
translation_en:
…with the transmission of our Way entrusted to him, Huang Mianzhai had no equal among his fellow students of the time in his cultivation of reverent attentiveness and investigation of principle. His comprehensive explanations of the Changes and the rites elucidated the meaning of the classics and did not disappoint his teacher.

Liu Yunzhuang taught the Way at Wuyi, intending to spend the rest of his life there. When he entered office, however, he responded to an imperial edict soliciting opinions by requesting that the court open its doors to unrestricted criticism, invite men who would speak fully and frankly, examine the successes and failures of current policies, and clarify what was right and wrong at court. Although I have not seen his explanations of the Changes and the rites, I already know what sort of man he was.

Chen Beixi disputed the teachings of Master Lu with great vigor and force. His work, The Meaning of Terms, surely came close to the ideal! Liao Zihui upheld the Way of his late teacher; he was esteemed as a recluse, and his Chaxi Collection merits praise. Zhen Xishan lived under the great prohibition of his age [?], teaching, studying, and putting his learning earnestly into practice. Drawing on many books, he compiled the Extended Meaning. He gained Emperor Lizong’s recognition, and the prohibition against “spurious learning” was thereupon lifted. Although he had not studied directly under Master Zhu, he too rendered service to the Way.

Wuxuan used the Way to cultivate goodness in others, and many studied under him. Taking the meanings of the classics as topical headings, he compiled the essential sayings of Master Wengong and appended the explanations of his disciples. Although he could not become a disciple of Master Zhu, he too was inspired to action by hearing of his example. Zheng Zhongshi was accomplished in the study of ritual, grasping its essentials and adapting its practice to circumstances. He was particularly esteemed by Xishan, and the people of his district were grateful to him. He too put his learning into practice.

Although these gentlemen’s Way was at odds with their times and their abilities could not be fully employed, they expounded the learning of the mind and fostered the transmission of this Way. Without these earlier worthies, who would have enlightened us? Can anyone forget the source from which they came? Master Huang said: “Mencius…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
而後周程張子繼其絕至朱子而始著自
其著也而口耳之學興矣是故觀人於朱
子之前者求其有見道之功而不拘其出
處之迹觀人於朱子之後者求其有躬行
之實而不貴其著作之富閩之先哲亦多
矣執事獨舉數子者爲問亦是意乎雖然
孔子之徒宜不在朱子下也惟有子曾子
子思之所記述爲足以傳其他門戶之衆
微言大義日以乖離學朱子者苟眩其名
===
而不究其實得於言而不求之心論譔旣
多簡袤已重賢者識其大者云耳盡信書
而心學累此固八閩之憂亦舉世士習之
訛也善乎趙清獻公之言曰后稷所讀何
書彼非以政爲學者也懼文勝其實爲反
本之論盛宋之時已見其流之弊矣當世
道之責者若之何哉
第五問
趙恒
punctuated:
而後，周、程、張子繼其絕，至朱子而始著。自其著也，而口耳之學興矣。是故觀人於朱子之前者，求其有見道之功，而不拘其出處之迹；觀人於朱子之後者，求其有躬行之實，而不貴其著作之富。」閩之先哲亦多矣，執事獨舉數子者爲問，亦是意乎？雖然，孔子之徒宜不在朱子下也，惟有子、曾子、子思之所記述爲足以傳，其他門戶之衆，微言大義日以乖離。學朱子者，苟眩其名而不究其實，得於言而不求之心，論譔旣多，簡袤已重，賢者識其大者云耳。盡信書而心學累，此固八閩之憂，亦舉世士習之訛也。善乎趙清獻公之言曰：「后稷所讀何書？」彼非以政爲學者也，懼文勝其實，爲反本之論。盛宋之時，已見其流之弊矣。當世道之責者，若之何哉？

第五問
趙恒
translation_en:
…After him, Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhang restored the interrupted transmission, but only with Master Zhu did it become fully manifest. Once it had become manifest, however, learning confined to the lips and ears arose. Thus, in assessing those before Master Zhu, we look for their achievement in perceiving the Way, without being bound by the particulars of their entering office or withdrawing from public life; in assessing those after Master Zhu, we look for the substance of their personal practice, rather than valuing the abundance of their writings.” Fujian, too, has had many earlier worthies. Was this also your intention, honored Examiner, in selecting just these few masters for your question? Even so, the disciples of Confucius surely should not rank below those of Master Zhu. Yet only what Youzi, Zengzi, and Zisi recorded was adequate to transmit the teaching; among the many other schools, the subtle words and great principles grew increasingly divergent. If those who study Master Zhu are dazzled by his name without investigating the substance of his teaching, grasp it in words without seeking it in their hearts, then, however numerous their compositions and however weighty their written volumes [?], it is merely a matter of “the worthy recognizing its greater elements.” To believe books entirely and thereby encumber the learning of the heart-and-mind is indeed a concern for the Eight Min regions of Fujian, but it is also a distortion in scholarly habits throughout the world. How apt were the words of Lord Zhao Qingxian: “What books did Hou Ji read?” He was not advocating treating government itself as learning; fearing that literary refinement would outweigh substance, he argued for a return to the root. Even during the flourishing Song dynasty, the abuses arising from this tendency were already apparent. What, then, should those responsible for the moral order of the age do?

Fifth Question
Zhao Heng

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄧批治盜治心歸於任人立法知所
本矣子其具文武才非邪
同考試官教諭汪批息盜歸重任人得根本之論
矣宜錄
考試官學正孫批有斷制
考試官教授張批據實可取
善治盜者治其心耳矣而法不與焉執法
以禦盜則盜可遏於已發而不能遏之於
未發遏之于未發者所以止盜之心也蓋
===
國依於民民依於官任官以裕民俗民以
止盜治心之術也而法者特其具耳豈可
恃以為安哉今夫盜亦吾民也其稟生理
之全樂室家之好猶夫人也其審善惡之
歸决死生之分猶夫人也惟其困窮累其
心溝壑切於念于是乎棄其身於盜賊以
為旦夕之計而為民牧者又不知所以正
其本而惟法之逞是猶醫者之於病不審
其虛實之理而徒執藥劑以治其標吾見
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄧批：「治盜治心，歸於任人立法，知所本矣。子其具文武才非邪？」
同考試官教諭汪批：「息盜歸重任人，得根本之論矣，宜錄。」
考試官學正孫批：「有斷制。」
考試官教授張批：「據實可取。」
善治盜者治其心耳矣，而法不與焉。執法以禦盜，則盜可遏於已發，而不能遏之於未發。遏之于未發者，所以止盜之心也。蓋國依於民，民依於官，任官以裕民，俗民以止盜，治心之術也。而法者特其具耳，豈可恃以為安哉？今夫盜亦吾民也，其稟生理之全，樂室家之好，猶夫人也；其審善惡之歸，决死生之分，猶夫人也。惟其困窮累其心，溝壑切於念，于是乎棄其身於盜賊，以為旦夕之計。而為民牧者，又不知所以正其本，而惟法之逞，是猶醫者之於病，不審其虛實之理，而徒執藥劑以治其標。吾見
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Deng, an Instructor: “You treat suppressing banditry as a matter of governing people’s hearts, grounding it in appointing men and establishing laws. You understand its foundation. Surely you possess both civil and military talent?”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, an Instructor: “By placing the chief emphasis in ending banditry on appointing men, you have reached the root of the matter. This deserves selection.”
Comment by Examiner Sun, a School Instructor: “Shows decisive judgment.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, an Instructor: “Grounded in reality and worthy of selection.”
Those skilled at controlling banditry merely govern people’s hearts; laws play no part in this. If one relies on enforcing laws to ward off banditry, it can be checked after it has arisen, but cannot be checked before it arises. Checking it before it arises means stopping the intention to become a bandit. The state depends on the people, and the people depend on officials. Appointing officials to enrich the people and reforming the people’s customs [?] to stop banditry are methods of governing hearts. Laws are merely instruments for this: how could one rely on them to secure peace? Now, bandits too are our people. In receiving the full endowment of the principles of life and delighting in the happiness of home and family, they are like everyone else. In discerning where good and evil lead and judging the distinction between life and death, they are like everyone else. It is only because hardship and poverty burden their hearts, and the prospect of dying in a ditch presses upon their thoughts, that they abandon themselves to banditry as a means of surviving from one day to the next. Yet those who shepherd the people do not understand how to put the root of the matter right, but merely give free rein to the law. This is like a physician treating an illness without examining whether it arises from deficiency or excess, simply applying medicines to treat its outward symptoms. I see…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
其藥愈投而病愈滋矣執事憂八閩宼盜
之虞而以古人備盜為問蓋亦豵豕之牙
而為今日東南民慮者至切也愚也願酌
古準今而陳之可乎夫古昔盛時奸究之
戒干羽之舞其民皞皞如也逮周而防制
始立蓋周公以關睢麟趾之意而行周官
之法度於是設士師之職立禦盜之制狗
刑掌之司稽殺刑掌之朝士摶盜掌之司
隷諜盜掌之環人刑賞施于追胥之比則
===
良民安司兵入于數量之辨則亂民飭相
翔誅於聚櫼之守則賓至如歸夜士詔夫
分夜之禁則行人畫一當時之民沐井田
富庶之業而罔淫于禁則是周公所以治
民心者固先有其具而又曲為之制法懸
而民自不犯耳後世之民即周之民而所
以戾于古而誣于法禁愈嚴而盜愈熾者
則以征戍之無已也勞役之無已也科歛
之無已也所謂致之有三豈虛語哉故□
punctuated: 其藥愈投而病愈滋矣。執事憂八閩宼盜之虞，而以古人備盜為問，蓋亦豵豕之牙，而為今日東南民慮者至切也。愚也願酌古準今而陳之，可乎？夫古昔盛時，奸究之戒、干羽之舞，其民皞皞如也。逮周而防制始立，蓋周公以關睢麟趾之意而行周官之法度。於是設士師之職，立禦盜之制：狗刑掌之司稽，殺刑掌之朝士，摶盜掌之司隷，諜盜掌之環人。刑賞施于追胥之比，則良民安；司兵入于數量之辨，則亂民飭；相翔誅於聚櫼之守，則賓至如歸；夜士詔夫分夜之禁，則行人畫一。當時之民沐井田富庶之業，而罔淫于禁，則是周公所以治民心者，固先有其具，而又曲為之制，法懸而民自不犯耳。後世之民即周之民，而所以戾于古而誣于法、禁愈嚴而盜愈熾者，則以征戍之無已也，勞役之無已也，科歛之無已也。所謂致之有三，豈虛語哉？故□
translation_en:
…the more medicine is administered, the worse the illness becomes. You, sir, are concerned about the danger of banditry in the Eight Min regions of Fujian and have therefore asked about the ancients’ precautions against bandits. This, too, is a matter of the boar’s tusk [?], and your concern for the people of the southeast today is most earnest. May I, in my ignorance, weigh ancient practice against present circumstances and set forth my views?

In the flourishing age of antiquity, there were admonitions against wrongdoing [?] and dances with shields and plumes, and the people lived in contentment. With the Zhou, preventive institutions began to be established. The Duke of Zhou implemented the statutes of the Offices of Zhou in the spirit of the poems “The Ospreys” (Guanju) and “The Qilin’s Hooves” (Linzhi). He accordingly established the office of Judicial Officer and instituted measures against banditry. The punishment termed “dog punishment” [?] was administered by the Inspectors; capital punishment by the Court Officers; the apprehension of bandits [?] by the Directors of Bondservants; and surveillance of bandits by the Patrolmen. When punishments and rewards were applied to the groups organized to pursue and search for bandits, law-abiding people enjoyed security. When the Director of Weapons entered into distinctions of numbers and quantities [?], unruly people were brought under discipline. When watchers punished offenders at the guarded barriers [?], guests felt as though they had returned home. When the Night Officers proclaimed the prohibitions governing the divisions of the night, travelers followed uniform rules. The people of that time enjoyed the prosperity afforded by the well-field system and did not transgress the prohibitions. Thus the Duke of Zhou already possessed the means to order the people’s hearts before providing detailed regulations for them. The laws were publicly displayed, and the people of their own accord did not violate them.

The people of later ages are the same as the people of Zhou. Yet they depart from ancient ways and flout the laws; the stricter the prohibitions, the more rampant banditry becomes. This is because military expeditions and garrison service never cease, labor service never ceases, and levies and exactions never cease. Could the saying that three things bring this about be empty words? Therefore, [illegible]…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
命法立於武帝而天漢中之盜自若也盜
賊重法奏於神宗而熈寧中之盜自若也
立鄉村團爲義營者一戶被盜累其一將
新鄭捕亡之術則然耳出庫錢榜置市者
一盜告捕賞錢一市安潜招降之術則然
耳然皆以救一時之急非長治之計也故
愚以爲弭盜之術莫先于任官焉任官之
法莫要于裕民焉任官在於愼俊選以考
其德稽殿最以覈其能明黜陟以勵其心
===
則賢能何有于不勸而貪墨者遠矣裕民
在於孚之以誠慤而民不悖導之以生業
而民不擾省之以誅求而民不匱則禮義
何有于不興而慆淫者寡矣善乎歐陽文
忠公之言曰方今禦盜不過四事曰州郡
置兵爲備也選捕盜之官也明賞罰之法
也去冗官用良吏以撫疲民也夫宋之論
備盜者衆矣而惟用良吏之言可爲後世
法方今閩南之地分爲八郡延建邵汀阻
punctuated:
命法立於武帝，而天漢中之盜自若也；盜賊重法奏於神宗，而熈寧中之盜自若也。立鄉村團爲義營者，一戶被盜，累其一將，新鄭捕亡之術則然耳；出庫錢榜置市者，一盜告捕，賞錢一市，安潜招降之術則然耳。然皆以救一時之急，非長治之計也。故愚以爲弭盜之術，莫先于任官焉；任官之法，莫要于裕民焉。任官在於愼俊選以考其德，稽殿最以覈其能，明黜陟以勵其心，則賢能何有于不勸，而貪墨者遠矣。裕民在於孚之以誠慤而民不悖，導之以生業而民不擾，省之以誅求而民不匱，則禮義何有于不興，而慆淫者寡矣。
善乎歐陽文忠公之言曰：「方今禦盜不過四事：曰州郡置兵爲備也，選捕盜之官也，明賞罰之法也，去冗官用良吏以撫疲民也。」夫宋之論備盜者衆矣，而惟用良吏之言可爲後世法。方今閩南之地分爲八郡，延、建、邵、汀阻
translation_en:
…the law concerning life [?] was established under Emperor Wu, yet banditry persisted unabated during the Tianhan era. The stringent law against bandits was submitted to Emperor Shenzong, yet banditry persisted unabated during the Xining era. Organizing village militia groups into volunteer battalions and holding their commander accountable whenever a single household suffered robbery—such was Xinzheng’s method of apprehending fugitives. Taking money from the treasury and posting notices in the marketplace, rewarding the reporting and capture of a single bandit with money for an entire marketplace [?]—such was An Qian’s method of inducing surrender. Yet these were all expedients for an immediate crisis, not plans for lasting order. Thus, in my humble opinion, nothing takes precedence over appointing officials as a means of suppressing banditry; and in the conduct of official service, nothing matters more than enriching the people. Appointing officials requires care in selecting outstanding men and examining their virtue, scrutiny of performance rankings to verify their abilities, and clear demotions and promotions to spur their commitment. How could worthy and capable men then fail to be encouraged? Corrupt officials would be kept far away. Enriching the people requires winning their trust through sincerity and honesty so that they do not rebel, guiding them toward productive livelihoods so that they are not unsettled, and reducing exactions so that they do not suffer want. How could ritual propriety and righteousness then fail to flourish? Those given to excess and dissipation would be few.
How excellent were the words of Ouyang, posthumously titled Wenzhong: “At present, defending against bandits involves only four matters: stationing troops in prefectures for preparedness; selecting officials to apprehend bandits; making the rules of reward and punishment clear; and eliminating superfluous officials and employing good ones to care for the exhausted people.” Many men of the Song discussed defenses against bandits, but it is the advice to employ good officials that can serve as a model for later generations. At present, the territory of southern Min is divided into eight prefectures. Yanping, Jianning, Shaowu, and Tingzhou rely on the barriers of…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
山依谷剷巄而耕壘石而種其爲平原沃
土無幾也福興泉漳帶海襟江高原爲礫
卑隰爲滷其爲平原沃土亦無幾也其間
租稅農桑有常徵矣漁鹽鈔鐵有常課矣
而額外之誅求取括者尚無已也如是而
官課得謂之輕乎濱海有水寨之兵阻山
有坑隘之守又有憲臣以專督海之任而
簿尉鄉閭之巡邏者無稽焉如是而禁網
得謂之闊乎故山海之民有流而爲盜者
===
无怪乎其然也蓋利在于山則荷戈斬木
以冒盜礦之禁利在于海則浮艦揭貲以
冒通番之禁玆欲禦之則險夷之習旣不
相如主客之形又甚懸絕我集彼散我散
彼集是彼坐得勝筭而我卒受其敗耳是
宜有以厪執事之慮也玆欲爲安閩之計
以圖善後之策宜無有出於任官之說者
先臣文莊丘濬之議有曰得一良令如得
勝兵三千人得一良守如得勝兵三萬人
punctuated: 山依谷，剷巄而耕，壘石而種，其爲平原沃土無幾也。福興泉漳，帶海襟江，高原爲礫，卑隰爲滷，其爲平原沃土亦無幾也。其間租稅農桑有常徵矣，漁鹽鈔鐵有常課矣，而額外之誅求取括者尚無已也。如是而官課得謂之輕乎？濱海有水寨之兵，阻山有坑隘之守，又有憲臣以專督海之任，而簿尉鄉閭之巡邏者無稽焉。如是而禁網得謂之闊乎？故山海之民有流而爲盜者，无怪乎其然也。蓋利在于山，則荷戈斬木，以冒盜礦之禁；利在于海，則浮艦揭貲，以冒通番之禁。玆欲禦之，則險夷之習旣不相如，主客之形又甚懸絕。我集彼散，我散彼集，是彼坐得勝筭，而我卒受其敗耳。是宜有以厪執事之慮也。玆欲爲安閩之計，以圖善後之策，宜無有出於任官之說者。先臣文莊丘濬之議有曰：「得一良令，如得勝兵三千人；得一良守，如得勝兵三萬人
translation_en:
…among mountains and along valleys, they cut away ridges to plough and pile up stones to plant; level, fertile land is scarce. Fuzhou, Xinghua, Quanzhou, and Zhangzhou border the sea and are girdled by rivers. Their uplands are gravelly and their lowlands saline; there, too, level, fertile land is scarce. Regular levies are imposed on farming and sericulture, and regular duties on fishing, salt, paper currency [?], and iron. Yet demands and exactions beyond the prescribed quotas still have no end. Under such circumstances, can government levies be called light? Along the coast are troops stationed at naval stockades; in the mountains are guards at ravines and passes. There is also a censorial official specifically charged with supervising maritime affairs, while the patrols conducted by registrars and county defenders through the villages receive no scrutiny [?]. Under such circumstances, can the net of prohibitions be called loose? It is therefore no wonder that some inhabitants of the mountains and coast drift into banditry.

Where profit lies in the mountains, they shoulder weapons and fell trees, risking violation of the prohibition on illicit mining; where profit lies at sea, they launch ships and raise capital, risking violation of the prohibition on intercourse with foreign peoples. If we now seek to suppress them, our familiarity with difficult and open terrain is unequal, and the respective positions of those on their own ground and those coming from outside are vastly different. When we concentrate, they disperse; when we disperse, they concentrate. Thus they readily secure the advantage needed for victory, while we ultimately suffer defeat. This should surely engage your concern.

To devise a plan for pacifying Fujian and securing its lasting peace, nothing should surpass the proposal to appoint suitable officials. The late minister Qiu Jun, posthumously titled Wenzhuang, stated in his deliberations: “Obtaining one good district magistrate is like obtaining three thousand victorious soldiers; obtaining one good prefect is like obtaining thirty thousand victorious soldiers…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
得一良部使者如得勝兵三十萬人此實
有得於歐陽子之旨而深切于八閩弭盜
之防者與故治山得一賈琮則尺書移檄
而不患巷路之無歌治海得一龔遂則單
車就道而不患兵戈之不解之二子者非
所謂勝兵者乎雖然其要在守令其機在
部使而其權在
朝廷必也緩治盜而急治民後催科而先撫
字而又躬儉約以憫民窮秉權衡以平民
===
志燭幾微以悉民隱廣孚惠以賙民乏崇
裕柔以亮民昧則民將有生之樂無死之
虞雖賞之不竊矣所謂治心者此也由是
而猶有盜焉則於海也擇其水陸交會之
區於山也相其原野開闢之處聚一鄉之
民蠲其稅役而專戰鬪之習如新鄭立義
營之法可也或積盜得之資節其冗費以
給勇敢之士如安潛賞告捕之法亦可也
此亦一時應變之宜也非可恃以為安也
punctuated: 得一良部使者，如得勝兵三十萬人。此實有得於歐陽子之旨，而深切于八閩弭盜之防者與！故治山得一賈琮，則尺書移檄，而不患巷路之無歌；治海得一龔遂，則單車就道，而不患兵戈之不解。之二子者，非所謂勝兵者乎？雖然，其要在守令，其機在部使，而其權在朝廷。必也緩治盜而急治民，後催科而先撫字，而又躬儉約以憫民窮，秉權衡以平民志，燭幾微以悉民隱，廣孚惠以賙民乏，崇裕柔以亮民昧，則民將有生之樂，無死之虞，雖賞之不竊矣。所謂治心者，此也。由是而猶有盜焉，則於海也，擇其水陸交會之區；於山也，相其原野開闢之處，聚一鄉之民，蠲其稅役，而專戰鬪之習，如新鄭立義營之法可也。或積盜得之資，節其冗費，以給勇敢之士，如安潛賞告捕之法亦可也。此亦一時應變之宜也，非可恃以為安也。
translation_en:
…To obtain one good regional inspector is like obtaining three hundred thousand victorious troops. This truly grasps Master Ouyang’s meaning and bears directly upon measures to suppress banditry in the Eight Min regions of Fujian! Thus, to govern the mountains, obtain a Jia Cong: with a brief letter and the circulation of a proclamation, there need be no fear that the lanes and roads will lack songs of praise. To govern the coast, obtain a Gong Sui: let him take to the road in a single carriage, and there need be no fear that armed conflict will not cease.
