考試官教授張批：復古之作。

唯仁人能愛人，能長人。人之生，皆有不忍人之心；有不忍人之心，斯有不忍人之政，無不仁，無不愛，無不足以長人也。氣禀拘之，物欲蔽之，君子而不仁者蓋有之矣，况其下乎？是故唯仁人能愛人，唯仁人足以長人也。且長人何以取足於仁人哉？大哉乾元，萬物資始；至哉坤元，萬物資生。天地，萬物父母也。天地能父母萬物，萬物不能自成，能於天地，必立之君，使治教之。是曰：「元后作民父母。」父母天下之名所由立也。則為
translation_en:
The ruler and his chief minister take acting as father and mother to all under Heaven as the Way of the True King
By Zheng Fu

Comment by Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor: Its form is an integrated whole, like a Shang ritual vessel or a Zhou tripod. Without elaborate carving, its literary beauty flourishes. It fully deserves to be called an elevated discourse.

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, School Instructor: This composition amounts to only a few hundred characters, yet its meaning is profound and its style antique. It has a deep radiance, an ancient hue, and a ringing sound, sweeping away the vulgarities of the age. Ah! Is your accomplishment confined to literary skill alone?

Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: Refined and correct.

Comment by Examiner Zhang, Prefectural School Instructor: A work that restores the ancient style.

Only the humane person can love others and lead them. All people are born with a heart that cannot bear the suffering of others. With such a heart comes government that cannot bear the suffering of others: nothing in it is inhumane, nothing unloving, and nothing insufficient for leading others. Yet people are constrained by their endowment of vital energy and obscured by material desires. There have indeed been gentlemen who lacked humanity; how much more so those beneath them? Thus only the humane person can love others, and only the humane person is fit to lead them.

But why does fitness to lead others depend upon humanity? “Great is the primal power of Qian: the myriad things draw upon it for their beginning. Consummate is the primal power of Kun: the myriad things draw upon it for their birth.” Heaven and Earth are the father and mother of the myriad things. Heaven and Earth can act as their father and mother, but the myriad things cannot bring themselves to completion. The passage concerning their capacity in relation to Heaven and Earth is unclear [?]; a ruler must be established for them to govern and instruct them. This is what is meant by: “The sovereign acts as father and mother to the people.” This is the origin of the designation “father and mother to all under Heaven.” Thus, to be…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
人君止於仁豈非其分之當然而自不容已乎
然能盡分者何鮮也吾之子吾愛之鄰人之子
則鄰人之矣國人之子則國人之矣此天下人
之情也吾讀二帝三王書竊悲聖人之於民雖
微物隱情盡制曲慮無少滲漏而其大者明天
道脩人紀抑洪水驅猛獸禪繼放伐苟利於國
錐身天下之不測舍至愛犯不韙猶不厭爲之
此其懷保惠鮮眞若嚴父慈母乳哺嬰兒如或
傷之而鞠育顧復教詔薰陶無所不用其誠豈
===
忍置一毫私意於其間哉此無他聖人之心至
誠無貳與天同德故視天下萬物莫非分內小
大遠邇無一不在所愛之中蓋仁人之足以長
人也如此後世知求治而不知正君本原闊畧
旣無以通天下之志又不勝其多欲之心以故
一膜之外便爲胡越用智自私靡所不至蓋雖
閨門父子猶將有所隔礙而不能通其不好人
之所惡惡人之所好者幾希惡在其爲民父母
哉此張子所以深憂朝廷以道學政術爲二事
punctuated: 人君止於仁，豈非其分之當然而自不容已乎？然能盡分者何鮮也！吾之子，吾愛之；鄰人之子，則鄰人之矣；國人之子，則國人之矣。此天下人之情也。吾讀二帝三王書，竊悲聖人之於民，雖微物隱情，盡制曲慮，無少滲漏；而其大者，明天道，脩人紀，抑洪水，驅猛獸，禪繼放伐，苟利於國，錐身天下之不測，舍至愛，犯不韙，猶不厭爲之。此其懷保惠鮮，眞若嚴父慈母乳哺嬰兒，如或傷之，而鞠育顧復，教詔薰陶，無所不用其誠，豈忍置一毫私意於其間哉？此無他，聖人之心至誠無貳，與天同德，故視天下萬物莫非分內，小大遠邇，無一不在所愛之中。蓋仁人之足以長人也如此。後世知求治而不知正君，本原闊畧，旣無以通天下之志，又不勝其多欲之心，以故一膜之外，便爲胡越，用智自私，靡所不至。蓋雖閨門父子，猶將有所隔礙而不能通，其不好人之所惡、惡人之所好者幾希！惡在其爲民父母哉？此張子所以深憂朝廷以道學政術爲二事
translation_en:
…for a ruler to abide in benevolence—is this not what his duty requires, something he cannot allow himself to cease doing? Yet how few can fully discharge that duty! My own child I love; a neighbor’s child I leave to the neighbor; a compatriot’s child I leave to that compatriot. Such are the feelings of people throughout the world. Reading the writings concerning the Two Emperors and Three Kings, I am deeply moved by how the sages treated the people. Even in minor matters and hidden circumstances, they made comprehensive provision and considered every detail, overlooking nothing. In greater matters, they clarified the Way of Heaven, cultivated the bonds of human relationships, checked the floods, drove away fierce beasts, abdicated or succeeded to the throne, and banished or attacked rulers. If it benefited the realm, they thrust themselves into unfathomable danger [?], relinquished those they loved most, and risked condemnation, yet never tired of doing so. In cherishing and protecting the people, showing them kindness and relieving their distress, they were truly like stern fathers and loving mothers nursing infants, fearful lest any harm befall them. In nurturing and tending them, instructing and shaping them, they applied their sincerity to the utmost. How could they bear to introduce the slightest selfish intention into this?

There is no other explanation: the sages’ hearts were utterly sincere and undivided, sharing Heaven’s virtue. Thus they regarded all things under Heaven as falling within their responsibility. Great or small, distant or near, nothing lay outside their love. Such is the benevolent person’s fitness to lead others. In later ages, people knew to seek good government but did not know to rectify the ruler; they neglected the very foundation. Unable either to give expression to the aspirations of all under Heaven or to master their own hearts’ many desires, they consequently regarded anyone beyond a single membrane as alien as the peoples of Hu and Yue, and went to every length in using their ingenuity for selfish ends. Even within the household, fathers and sons would encounter barriers that prevented mutual understanding. How few avoided loving what the people hated and hating what the people loved! How could they be called the people’s parents? This is why Master Zhang was deeply troubled that the court treated the learning of the Way and the arts of government as two separate matters…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
而欲行帝王之道者必自使其君愛天下之人
如赤子始程子曰有天德便可語王道此之謂
也
同前
楊子充
同考試官教諭崔批據理立論惻怛由衷且詞采抑揚
足以發先賢之未發不厭重刻
同考試官教諭劉批質而不俚文而不縟開闔變化
理與氣俱讀之起敬
===
考試官學正孫批思致周遠
考試官教授張批沉着弘遠
王道不可以易言也天生民而立之君使司牧
之勿使失性有君而爲之貳使師保之勿使過
度天萬物父母也君受天之子而爲之牧是謂
元后作民父母也相則佐君以成牧之之道也
父母之命出於天而畀之君相謂必惠之保之
其於斯民真如吾之愛其子可也而或少有私
意存乎其中則一膜之外便爲胡越非父母矣
punctuated:
而欲行帝王之道者，必自使其君愛天下之人如赤子始。程子曰：「有天德，便可語王道。」此之謂也。

同前。
楊子充。

同考試官教諭崔批：據理立論，惻怛由衷，且詞采抑揚，足以發先賢之未發，不厭重刻。
同考試官教諭劉批：質而不俚，文而不縟，開闔變化，理與氣俱，讀之起敬。
考試官學正孫批：思致周遠。
考試官教授張批：沉着弘遠。

王道不可以易言也。天生民而立之君，使司牧之，勿使失性；有君而爲之貳，使師保之，勿使過度。天，萬物父母也。君受天之子而爲之牧，是謂元后，作民父母也。相則佐君以成牧之之道也。父母之命出於天，而畀之君相，謂必惠之保之，其於斯民，真如吾之愛其子可也。而或少有私意存乎其中，則一膜之外便爲胡越，非父母矣。
translation_en:
…and anyone wishing to put the Way of the sage emperors and kings into practice must begin by bringing his ruler to love all people under Heaven as newborn children. Master Cheng said, “With Heaven’s virtue, one may then speak of the Kingly Way.” This is what he meant.

Same topic as above.
Yang Zichong.

Comment by Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor: His argument is grounded in principle, and his compassionate concern comes from the heart. Moreover, the rise and fall of his eloquent language brings out what earlier worthies left unexpressed. It merits being printed again.
Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: Plain but not vulgar, polished but not ornate; its unfolding, gathering, and transformations unite principle with vital force. Reading it inspires respect.
Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: His thought is comprehensive and far-reaching.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: Steady and assured, broad and far-reaching.

The Kingly Way cannot be spoken of lightly. Heaven gave birth to the people and established a ruler over them, charging him to oversee and shepherd them and prevent them from losing their nature. Having established a ruler, it provided him with a deputy, charging him to instruct and protect the people and prevent them from overstepping proper bounds. Heaven is the parent of all things. The ruler receives Heaven’s children into his care and shepherds them: this is what it means to be the sovereign, serving as the people’s parent. The chief minister assists the ruler in fulfilling the Way of shepherding them. The mandate to act as parents comes from Heaven and is entrusted to the ruler and chief minister. It requires them to benefit and protect the people; only if they truly treat these people as Heaven loves its children will they fulfill it. Yet if even a little selfish intent remains within, then those beyond a single membrane become as alien as the peoples of Hu and Yue, and they are no longer parents.…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
棄天地之性矣天之愛民甚矣豈其使一人肆
於民上以從其淫而棄天地之性必不然矣是
故明於天命之故而後可以語王道也父母者
一家之說也吾之子吾體之易也鄉人之子則
異是矣國人之子則又異是矣天下人之子則
又異是矣而又五土異性五方異氣大川廣谷
異地人生其間異俗輕重遲速長短異齊舟車
器械異制飲食衣服異宜非若吾之一家可以
體而一之也而吾不能推情以致理緣俗以立
===
教隨所宜以爲之制則元元之子不得所欲者
多矣是不能如慈母之心誠求之也而曰如保
赤子可乎是故察於庶物羣情之變而後可以
語王道也王者之政非苟作者禮樂刑政四達
而不悖皆必有至理存乎其間而一毫私意小
智不與焉故其制度品節之詳終始條理之序
內則盡理外則盡制不容毫髮僭差也易曰后
以財成天地之道輔相天地之宜以左右民此
天時地理人事之紀也道德性命之原也昧此
punctuated:
棄天地之性矣。天之愛民甚矣，豈其使一人肆於民上，以從其淫，而棄天地之性？必不然矣。是故明於天命之故，而後可以語王道也。
父母者，一家之說也。吾之子，吾體之易也；鄉人之子則異是矣，國人之子則又異是矣，天下人之子則又異是矣。而又五土異性，五方異氣，大川廣谷異地，人生其間異俗，輕重遲速長短異齊，舟車器械異制，飲食衣服異宜，非若吾之一家，可以體而一之也。而吾不能推情以致理，緣俗以立教，隨所宜以爲之制，則元元之子不得所欲者多矣。是不能如慈母之心誠求之也，而曰如保赤子，可乎？是故察於庶物羣情之變，而後可以語王道也。
王者之政，非苟作者。禮樂刑政，四達而不悖，皆必有至理存乎其間，而一毫私意小智不與焉。故其制度品節之詳，終始條理之序，內則盡理，外則盡制，不容毫髮僭差也。《易》曰：「后以財成天地之道，輔相天地之宜，以左右民。」此天時地理人事之紀也，道德性命之原也。昧此
translation_en:
…and abandon the nature bestowed by Heaven and Earth. Heaven’s love for the people is profound indeed. Could it allow one man to act without restraint above the people, indulging his excesses and abandoning the nature bestowed by Heaven and Earth? Surely not. Thus, only after understanding the grounds of Heaven’s mandate can one speak of the kingly Way.
Being a father or mother is a relationship spoken of within a single family. My child is a transformation of my own body; the children of my fellow villagers are different, those of my fellow countrymen different again, and those of all people under Heaven still further removed. Moreover, the five kinds of soil differ in their nature, and the five regions in their vital influences. Great rivers and broad valleys differ in terrain, and the people born among them differ in customs. Lightness and heaviness, slowness and swiftness, length and shortness differ in their proportions; boats, carriages, implements, and tools differ in their construction; food, drink, and clothing differ according to what is suitable. These people cannot be treated as one body and united as readily as those of my own family. If I cannot extend my sympathetic feelings to realize proper order, establish instruction in accordance with local customs, and make regulations suited to circumstances, then many among the common people, my children, will fail to obtain what they desire. This would be a failure to seek sincerely with the heart of a loving mother. Could I then claim to act ‘as though tending an infant’? Thus, only after discerning the variations among the many things and the feelings of the people can one speak of the kingly Way.
The government of a true king is not something undertaken heedlessly. Ritual, music, punishments, and administration extend everywhere without conflicting, for the highest principle must be present within them all, with not the slightest selfish intention or petty cleverness intruding. Hence, in the particulars of institutions and their graded regulations, and in their orderly sequence from beginning to end, principle is fully realized inwardly and regulation fully implemented outwardly; not the slightest overstepping or deviation is permitted. The Book of Changes says: ‘The ruler shapes and completes the Way of Heaven and Earth, assists what is fitting in Heaven and Earth, and thereby supports the people.’ This is the framework of Heaven’s seasons, Earth’s configurations, and human affairs; it is the source of the Way, virtue, human nature, and destiny. To be ignorant of this …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
吾未見其能行父母之政也然則達於三才之
奧道德性命之原而後可以語王道也夫然後
不獨親其親不獨子其子老有所終壯有所用
幼有所長鰥寡孤獨廢疾皆有所養男有分女
有歸則自一家以至於天下皆家矣自一人以
至於億兆人皆子矣是之謂大同然後天不愛
道地不愛寶人不愛情山川鬼神亦莫不寧曁
鳥獸魚鼈咸若是之謂大順大同大順聖神功
化之極也而君相父母天下之事畢矣然則未
===
至於聖神功化之極未可以語王道也雖然豈
外求哉亦在吾君吾相存主之間耳所以存主
之者心也所以存主此心者敬也敬自愼獨始
也世之君相不能愼獨以明其明德故無以通
天下之志而知千萬人之心卽一人之心無以
勝一己之私而以一人之心爲千萬人之心如
是而曰君相可矣將以稱於天下曰父母父母
則未也故曰有天德便可語王道
表
punctuated:
吾未見其能行父母之政也。然則達於三才之奧、道德性命之原，而後可以語王道也。夫然後不獨親其親，不獨子其子，老有所終，壯有所用，幼有所長，鰥寡孤獨廢疾皆有所養，男有分，女有歸，則自一家以至於天下皆家矣，自一人以至於億兆人皆子矣。是之謂大同。然後天不愛道，地不愛寶，人不愛情，山川鬼神亦莫不寧，曁鳥獸魚鼈咸若。是之謂大順。大同大順，聖神功化之極也，而君相父母天下之事畢矣。然則未至於聖神功化之極，未可以語王道也。雖然，豈外求哉？亦在吾君吾相存主之間耳。所以存主之者，心也；所以存主此心者，敬也。敬自愼獨始也。世之君相不能愼獨以明其明德，故無以通天下之志，而知千萬人之心卽一人之心；無以勝一己之私，而以一人之心爲千萬人之心。如是而曰君相可矣，將以稱於天下曰父母父母，則未也。故曰：「有天德便可語王道。」

表
translation_en:
…I have never seen such a person able to carry out government as a parent to the people. Thus, only after comprehending the mysteries of the Three Powers—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—and the sources of the Way, virtue, human nature, and destiny can one speak of the kingly Way. Only then will people cherish not only their own parents and treat not only their own children as children; the aged will have provision to the end of their lives, the able-bodied will have employment, and the young will have nurture as they grow. Widowers, widows, orphans, the childless elderly, and those disabled or ill will all receive support. Men will have their allotted roles, and women will have homes in marriage. Then, extending from a single household to all under Heaven, all will be one family; extending from a single person to the countless multitudes, all will be regarded as children. This is called the Great Unity. Then Heaven will not withhold its Way, Earth will not withhold its treasures, and people will not withhold their true feelings. The spirits of mountains and rivers will all be at peace, and birds, beasts, fish, and turtles will all flourish in harmony. This is called the Great Accord. The Great Unity and the Great Accord are the culmination of sagely and spirit-like achievement and transformation; with them, the work of ruler and chief minister as parents to all under Heaven is complete. Thus, until this culmination of sagely and spirit-like achievement and transformation has been reached, one cannot yet speak of the kingly Way.

Yet must this be sought outside oneself? It lies simply in what our ruler and our chief minister preserve within themselves and take as their guiding principle. That by which they preserve and govern it is the heart; that by which they preserve and govern this heart is reverent attentiveness. Reverent attentiveness begins with vigilance when alone. Rulers and chief ministers of this age cannot exercise vigilance when alone so as to illuminate their luminous virtue. Thus they have no means of comprehending the aspirations of all under Heaven and recognizing that the hearts of millions are the same as the heart of one person. Nor have they the means to overcome their own selfishness and make the heart of one person the heart of millions. In this condition, they may indeed be called rulers and chief ministers; but they cannot yet be acclaimed throughout the world as “our father and mother, our father and mother.” Hence the saying: “Possess the virtue of Heaven, and one may then speak of the kingly Way.”

Memorials

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
擬
聖駕重幸太學祭酒率諸生
謝表
薛欽
同考試官教諭沈批我
皇上崇重
先師之禮超出千古此作揄揚殆盡可以觀
聖化矣
同考試官學正蔡批
===
聖天子道學之正禮樂之備未易窺測乃能模寫如此子其以文鳴盛者邪
考試官學正孫批駢麗有則
考試官教授張批善頌
嘉靖十二年三月十三日欽蒙
聖駕臨幸太學祭酒臣某等謹率諸生奉
表稱
謝者伏以
華蓋天臨再闡右文之治璧雝風動式昭左
史之書復覩漢儀肇稱殷禮開
punctuated:
擬聖駕重幸太學祭酒率諸生謝表
薛欽
同考試官教諭沈批：我皇上崇重先師之禮，超出千古，此作揄揚殆盡，可以觀聖化矣。
同考試官學正蔡批：聖天子道學之正，禮樂之備，未易窺測，乃能模寫如此，子其以文鳴盛者邪？
考試官學正孫批：駢麗有則。
考試官教授張批：善頌。
嘉靖十二年三月十三日，欽蒙聖駕臨幸太學，祭酒臣某等謹率諸生奉表稱謝者。伏以：華蓋天臨，再闡右文之治；璧雝風動，式昭左史之書。復覩漢儀，肇稱殷禮，開
translation_en:
Draft memorial of thanks presented by the Libationer, leading the students, upon the Emperor’s second visit to the Imperial University
By Xue Qin 薛欽

Comment by Associate Examiner Shen 沈, School Instructor: “The reverence our Emperor displays in the rites honoring the First Teacher surpasses that of all antiquity. This composition celebrates it almost exhaustively; through it one can perceive the sage sovereign’s transforming influence.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Cai 蔡, School Instructor: “The correctness of the sage Son of Heaven’s learning of the Way and the completeness of his rites and music are not easily fathomed. Yet you have depicted them thus! Are you perhaps one who will celebrate this flourishing age through literature?”

Comment by Examiner Sun 孫, School Instructor: “The elegant parallel prose observes proper rules.”

Comment by Examiner Zhang 張, Prefectural School Instructor: “Excellent praise.”

On the thirteenth day of the third month of the twelfth year of Jiajing, we reverently received the honor of Your Majesty’s visit to the Imperial University. Your servants, the Libationer So-and-so and the others, respectfully lead the students in presenting this memorial of thanks.

We humbly reflect: Your imperial canopy descended from Heaven, once again manifesting a government that honors letters; the Imperial University stirred beneath your influence, duly illuminating the writings of the Recorder of the Left. Once more we beheld the ceremonial splendor of the Han and began to perform the grand rites. Opening…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
講筵而晝接煦士類以春融化軌聿新詞林
協慶臣等誠懽誠忭稽首頓首竊惟太學
乃賢士所關而孔子自生民未有大明六
籍開萬古之羣蒙遠紹百王壽斯文之一
脉自秦灰滅學漢馬少文求儒雅以闡猷
誰云多欲在念起褒成而改諡未知大德
不官中元制建三雍比齊禮修二仲五更
三老填門雜進乎車輪四辟諸賢列奠祗
陳乎脯醢况復鴻都虎觀徒多蟬噪蛙鳴
===
武德講經沙門雜雅元祐再拜泮水無光
名為重道崇儒實則背經侮聖僭瀆一律
後世奚觀制作百年
明時有待兹蓋伏遇
皇帝陛下
聰明天縱
聲教雷行繩
祖武而謹日中觀人文以化天下
聖弗自滿而主善為師
punctuated:
講筵而晝接，煦士類以春融，化軌聿新，詞林協慶。臣等誠懽誠忭，稽首頓首。竊惟太學乃賢士所關，而孔子自生民未有。大明六籍，開萬古之羣蒙；遠紹百王，壽斯文之一脉。自秦灰滅學，漢馬少文，求儒雅以闡猷，誰云多欲在念？起褒成而改諡，未知大德不官。中元制建三雍，比齊禮修二仲。五更三老，填門雜進乎車輪；四辟諸賢，列奠祗陳乎脯醢。况復鴻都虎觀，徒多蟬噪蛙鳴；武德講經，沙門雜雅；元祐再拜，泮水無光。名為重道崇儒，實則背經侮聖，僭瀆一律，後世奚觀？制作百年，明時有待。
兹蓋伏遇皇帝陛下，聰明天縱，聲教雷行。繩祖武而謹日中，觀人文以化天下。聖弗自滿，而主善為師。
translation_en:
…the imperial lecture sessions are opened, and audiences granted in the daylight; scholars are warmed as by the genial spring. The pattern of moral transformation is renewed, and the literary community joins in celebration. We, your servants, are truly joyful and truly delighted; we bow our heads to the ground and repeatedly kowtow.
We humbly reflect that the Imperial University is where the fortunes of worthy scholars are bound up, while Confucius has had no equal since humankind first came into being. He brilliantly elucidated the Six Classics, dispelling the collective ignorance of countless ages; he carried forward the legacy of the kings of old, perpetuating the single line of this cultural tradition. After Qin reduced learning to ashes, the Han “horse” was deficient in culture [?]. Learned scholars were sought to elucidate the grand design—who could say that excessive desires occupied the ruler’s thoughts? Yet in raising up the Marquis Baocheng and changing the posthumous title, they failed to understand that great virtue cannot be confined to an official position. In the Zhongyuan era, regulations established the Three Ritual Institutions; following the Qi precedent [?], ceremonies were performed in the middle months of spring and autumn. The ritually honored elders, the Five Experienced and the Three Venerable, thronged the gates, their carriage wheels advancing in confusion; offerings were arrayed for the worthies of the “four bi” [?], but consisted merely of dried meat and meat sauce. Moreover, at Hongdu and the Tiger Observatory, there was only an abundance of cicada-chatter and frog-croaking. When the Classics were expounded during the Wude era, Buddhist monks mingled with the learned; when repeated bows were performed during the Yuanyou era, no glory accrued to the school’s waters. In name, these acts honored the Way and exalted Confucian learning; in reality, they contradicted the Classics and insulted the Sage. All alike were presumptuous and profane: what could later generations find in them to emulate? A century of institutional development awaited an enlightened age.
Now we have humbly encountered Your Majesty the Emperor, whose intelligence is Heaven-bestowed and whose moral influence spreads like thunder. You follow in your ancestors’ footsteps and attend carefully to the midday [?]; you contemplate human culture in order to transform all under Heaven. Sagely, yet never self-satisfied, you take goodness as your foremost teacher …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
手不停披而學古有獲誕登道岸默契
心淵謂王號非孔聖所安而像塑寔夷風未
改無臣為有尚杜請于門人假幻即眞奚
甘誣於佛氏遂定
先師之號正名必先乎載更遺像之儀存神
其至矣矧子無先食暨新
啓聖之祠而爵必因生悉定羣賢之配洗往
時之陋制成曠古之偉觀顧惟我
朝以來爰自
===
太祖而下稽古正學首舉彝章釋奠登歌特行
初服乃義起大作為於
今日而
重臨獨超邁乎前聞盖道隆則從而隆無嫌
自屈惟
主聖然後知聖不待人言爰涓令辰肆傳
清蹕
六龍翼翼其戾止道見泰來萬象率以景從喜
先豫動雅樂繼作金絲分孔壁之藏祀事
punctuated:
手不停披而學古有獲，誕登道岸，默契心淵。謂王號非孔聖所安，而像塑寔夷風未改。無臣為有，尚杜請于門人；假幻即眞，奚甘誣於佛氏？遂定先師之號，正名必先乎；載更遺像之儀，存神其至矣！矧子無先食，暨新啓聖之祠；而爵必因生，悉定羣賢之配。洗往時之陋制，成曠古之偉觀。
顧惟我朝以來，爰自太祖而下，稽古正學，首舉彝章。釋奠登歌，特行初服。乃義起大作為於今日，而重臨獨超邁乎前聞。盖道隆則從而隆，無嫌自屈；惟主聖然後知聖，不待人言。爰涓令辰，肆傳清蹕。六龍翼翼其戾止，道見泰來；萬象率以景從，喜先豫動。雅樂繼作，金絲分孔壁之藏；祀事
translation_en:
…Your hands never cease turning the pages, and your study of antiquity yields understanding. You have grandly ascended the shore of the Way and silently comprehended the depths of the sage’s mind. You judged that the title of king was not one with which the sage Kong would have been comfortable, and that sculpted images perpetuated an unreformed foreign custom. When his disciples would have treated him as having retainers although he had none, he rejected their proposal; how, then, could he willingly suffer the Buddhists’ misrepresentation, which takes illusion for reality? Thus you established his title as Former Teacher: surely the rectification of names must come first. You also changed the prescribed form of his representation: how consummately this preserves his spirit! Moreover, since a son must not receive offerings before his father, you newly established the Shrine of the Sage’s Progenitor. Since titles must accord with those held in life, you also settled all the arrangements for the associated worship of the worthies. You swept away the defective institutions of former times and created a magnificent spectacle unparalleled in antiquity.
Considering our dynasty, from Taizu onward, its rulers examined antiquity and set learning aright, giving precedence to the established rites. The sacrificial offerings to the sage and the hymns sung in the hall were specially performed at the beginning of the reign [?]. Yet it is today that righteousness has inspired these great undertakings, and your renewed imperial visit surpasses all earlier accounts. For when the Way is exalted, you exalt it accordingly, without considering it demeaning to yourself. Only a sagely sovereign can recognize the sage, without waiting for others to tell him. An auspicious day was therefore selected, and commands to clear the way for the imperial procession were proclaimed. The six dragons advanced with solemn dignity and arrived: in the Way, auspicious concord became manifest. All creation followed like a shadow, stirred beforehand by joy and gladness. The ceremonial music then sounded; bells and strings shared in the legacy preserved within the walls of Kong’s house. The sacrificial service…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
肅將玉帛委
上方之貢
至禮不讓
明德惟馨儀視昔為有加道于今而益顯旣
寧圭璧逐列縉紳廣厦細旃深繹古人淵
海升堂入室弘開夫子宫墻雲仍來三氏
之雝雝懐深豐芑橋門圜多士之濟濟樂
極菁莪
大禮旣成
===
一人有慶臣等欣逢
盛事愧匪宿儒
賜坐講易書已知過望開卷對賢聖敢不昌
言蓋嘗陋稚圭之說詩解頤亦旣慕正叔
之積誠悟
主伏願
典學念于終始無怠無荒
潛心見於羹墻亦趨亦步與治同道以經法
天合謨曰嘉圖幾而康庶事說天莫辨養
punctuated:
肅將玉帛，委上方之貢。至禮不讓，明德惟馨。儀視昔為有加，道于今而益顯。旣寧圭璧，逐列縉紳，廣厦細旃，深繹古人淵海；升堂入室，弘開夫子宫墻。雲仍來三氏之雝雝，懐深豐芑；橋門圜多士之濟濟，樂極菁莪。大禮旣成，一人有慶。
臣等欣逢盛事，愧匪宿儒。賜坐講易書，已知過望；開卷對賢聖，敢不昌言？蓋嘗陋稚圭之說詩解頤，亦旣慕正叔之積誠悟主。伏願典學念于終始，無怠無荒；潛心見於羹墻，亦趨亦步；與治同道，以經法天；合謨曰嘉，圖幾而康庶事。說天莫辨，養
translation_en:
…reverently presenting jade and silk, and laying out offerings supplied by the imperial household. In the highest rites there is no yielding precedence; only luminous virtue gives forth fragrance. The ceremonial forms surpass those of former times, and the Way shines still more clearly today. Once the jade tablets and discs had been duly laid to rest, the assembled officials took their places [?]. In spacious halls, upon fine felt mats, they expounded the oceanic depths of the ancients’ teachings; ascending the hall and entering the inner chamber, they opened wide the precincts of the Master’s learning. Distant descendants of the three clans came in harmony, evoking profound solicitude for posterity, as in the poem “Luxuriant Millet.” Around the gate of the academy gathered a dignified multitude of scholars, their joy in cultivated talent reaching its height, as in “Luxuriant Wormwood.” The great rite was accomplished; the One Man received blessings.
We, your servants, rejoice to have encountered this splendid occasion, yet feel ashamed that we are not seasoned scholars. To be granted seats to lecture on the Changes and the Documents already exceeded our hopes. Opening the books and confronting the worthies and sages, how could we dare withhold forthright words? We have long thought little of Zhigui’s exposition of the Odes that made his listeners smile, while admiring Zhengshu’s accumulation of sincerity to awaken his ruler’s understanding. We humbly pray that Your Majesty will keep canonical learning in mind from beginning to end, neither neglecting it nor becoming idle; that through concentrated reflection you will see the sages before you in broth and upon walls, following their every movement; that you will accord with the Way in governing and take Heaven as your model through the Classics; and that, joining in counsels pronounced excellent, you will attend to the first stirrings of events and bring the many affairs of government into good order. Discourse on Heaven admits no distinction [?]; nurturing…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
賢以及萬民臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第參場
策五道
第一問
===
楊子充
同考試官教諭崔批
聖製一策重在我
祖宗明經衞道之意子能敷答詳明末復歸重於科目反本之論誠非
專務文字之學者宜錄以式
同考試官教諭劉批此策稽古正學關繫
今日作人之要機子能因事効忠惓惓不置可以為
明天子獻矣
考試官學正孫批考議詳盡
punctuated:
賢以及萬民。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第參場，策五道。第一問。

楊子充。

同考試官教諭崔批：聖製一策，重在我祖宗明經衞道之意。子能敷答詳明，末復歸重於科目反本之論，誠非專務文字之學者，宜錄以式。

同考試官教諭劉批：此策稽古正學，關繫今日作人之要機。子能因事効忠，惓惓不置，可以為明天子獻矣。

考試官學正孫批：考議詳盡。
translation_en:
…worthy men, and thereby reach all the people. We, your servants, gaze toward Heaven and look up to Your Majesty, overwhelmed by fervent emotion and trembling reverence. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session: Five Policy Questions. First Question.

Yang Zichong.

Comment by Associate Examiner Cui, Instructor: “This imperially composed policy question chiefly concerns the intention of our imperial ancestors to elucidate the Classics and defend the Way. You have developed your answer clearly and in detail, and at the end again give central importance to the argument that the examination system should return to its foundations. You are truly no scholar devoted solely to literary composition. This should be included as a model.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: “This policy question examines antiquity and rectifies learning; it concerns the essential means of cultivating talent today. You have used this occasion to demonstrate your loyalty, with unflagging devotion. This may be presented to our enlightened Son of Heaven.”

Comment by Examiner Sun, Instructor: “The investigation and discussion are thorough and exhaustive.”

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授張批講求切實可錄
昔者夫子之教始於詩書而終於禮樂蓋
其門弟子身通六藝者七十而可與言詩
獨二子焉其一子夏於春秋猶不能贊一
辭也說經豈不難哉此我
聖祖
神宗罷黜百家表章六學道大如天而祗承終
鮮其人也伏覩
高皇帝開科舉
===
詔易主程氏朱氏古註疏書蔡氏傳古註疏春
秋左氏公羊穀梁胡氏張洽傳詩朱氏傳
古註疏禮記古註疏非朱子學校貢舉議
諸經各立家法而皆以註疏為主之謂乎
又伏覩
文皇帝御製性理大全書序曰乃者命儒臣集
諸家傳註而為大全凡有發明經義者取之
悖於經旨者去之又
諭諸臣曰務極精備庶幾以垂後世非朱子學
punctuated:
考試官教授張批：講求切實，可錄。
昔者夫子之教，始於詩書而終於禮樂。蓋其門弟子身通六藝者七十，而可與言詩獨二子焉。其一子夏，於春秋猶不能贊一辭也。說經豈不難哉！此我聖祖神宗罷黜百家、表章六學，道大如天，而祗承終鮮其人也。伏覩高皇帝開科舉，詔：《易》主程氏、朱氏、古註疏；《書》，蔡氏傳、古註疏；《春秋》，左氏、公羊、穀梁、胡氏、張洽傳；《詩》，朱氏傳、古註疏；《禮記》，古註疏。非朱子《學校貢舉議》諸經各立家法，而皆以註疏為主之謂乎？又伏覩文皇帝御製《性理大全書》序曰：「乃者命儒臣集諸家傳註而為大全，凡有發明經義者取之，悖於經旨者去之。」又諭諸臣曰：「務極精備，庶幾以垂後世。」非朱子學
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: “The inquiry is practical and sound; this may be selected.”
In former times, the Master’s teaching began with the Odes and Documents and culminated in rites and music. Among his disciples, seventy personally mastered the Six Arts, yet only two were fit to discuss the Odes with him. One of these, Zixia, could still contribute not a single word to the Spring and Autumn Annals. Is explaining the classics not difficult indeed! Thus our sage ancestors and divine forebears rejected the Hundred Schools and exalted the six disciplines [?]. Their Way was as vast as Heaven, yet those who reverently upheld it remained few.
I humbly observe that when Emperor Gao established the civil-service examinations, he decreed that the Changes should follow the works of Cheng and Zhu and the ancient commentaries and subcommentaries; the Documents, Cai’s commentary and the ancient commentaries and subcommentaries; the Spring and Autumn Annals, the commentaries of Zuo, Gongyang, Guliang, Hu, and Zhang Qia; the Odes, Zhu’s commentary and the ancient commentaries and subcommentaries; and the Record of Rites, the ancient commentaries and subcommentaries. Is this not what Master Zhu meant in his Discussion of Schools and Recruitment through Examinations: that each classic should have its own established interpretive tradition, while all should take the commentaries and subcommentaries as their foundation?
I further humbly observe that Emperor Wen’s imperially composed preface to the Complete Compendium of Human Nature and Principle states: “Recently I ordered the Confucian officials to gather the commentaries of the various schools into a complete compendium, including whatever elucidates the meaning of the classics and excluding whatever contradicts their purport.” He further instructed his officials: “Strive for the utmost precision and completeness, so that this may be handed down to later generations.” Is this not Master Zhu’s discussion of schools …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
校貢舉議易兼取胡瑗石介歐陽脩王安
石邵雍程頤張載呂大臨楊時書兼取劉
敞王安石蘇軾程頤楊時晁說之葉夢得
吳棫薛季宣呂祖謙詩兼取歐陽脩蘇軾
程頤張載王安石呂大臨楊時呂祖謙周
禮則劉敞王安石楊時儀禮則劉敞二戴
禮記則劉敞程頤張載呂大臨春秋則啖
助趙正陸淳孫明復劉敞程頤胡安國大
學論語中庸孟子則集解等書而蘇軾王
===
雩吳棫胡寅等說亦皆可采之謂乎
文謨
武烈丕顯丕承雖考諸三王而不謬建諸天地
而不悖質諸鬼神而無疑百世以俟聖人
而不惑可也執事以爲今諸臣所編大全
書者果能盡合
宸慮否乎竊謂註疏讖緯之文雖所當芟而漢
魏相傳音讀訓詁制度名物所存言無微
而可畧小註引入諸說雖多可取而宋元
punctuated:
校貢舉議》，《易》兼取胡瑗、石介、歐陽脩、王安石、邵雍、程頤、張載、呂大臨、楊時；《書》兼取劉敞、王安石、蘇軾、程頤、楊時、晁說之、葉夢得、吳棫、薛季宣、呂祖謙；《詩》兼取歐陽脩、蘇軾、程頤、張載、王安石、呂大臨、楊時、呂祖謙；《周禮》則劉敞、王安石、楊時；《儀禮》則劉敞；二戴《禮記》則劉敞、程頤、張載、呂大臨；《春秋》則啖助、趙正、陸淳、孫明復、劉敞、程頤、胡安國；《大學》、《論語》、《中庸》、《孟子》則《集解》等書，而蘇軾、王雩、吳棫、胡寅等說亦皆可采之謂乎？
文謨武烈，丕顯丕承，雖考諸三王而不謬，建諸天地而不悖，質諸鬼神而無疑，百世以俟聖人而不惑，可也。執事以爲今諸臣所編《大全》書者，果能盡合宸慮否乎？竊謂註疏讖緯之文雖所當芟，而漢魏相傳音讀、訓詁、制度、名物所存，言無微而可畧。小註引入諸說，雖多可取，而宋元
translation_en:
…Proposal on Schools and Recruitment through Tribute Examinations: for the Changes, also drawing on Hu Yuan, Shi Jie, Ouyang Xiu, Wang Anshi, Shao Yong, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, Lü Dalin, and Yang Shi; for the Documents, also drawing on Liu Chang, Wang Anshi, Su Shi, Cheng Yi, Yang Shi, Chao Shuozhi, Ye Mengde, Wu Yu, Xue Jixuan, and Lü Zuqian; for the Odes, also drawing on Ouyang Xiu, Su Shi, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, Wang Anshi, Lü Dalin, Yang Shi, and Lü Zuqian; for the Rites of Zhou, on Liu Chang, Wang Anshi, and Yang Shi; for the Ceremonies and Rites, on Liu Chang; for the Records of Rites of the two Dai masters, on Liu Chang, Cheng Yi, Zhang Zai, and Lü Dalin; for the Spring and Autumn Annals, on Dan Zhu, Zhao Zheng [?], Lu Chun, Sun Mingfu, Liu Chang, Cheng Yi, and Hu Anguo; and for the Great Learning, Analects, Doctrine of the Mean, and Mencius, on works such as the Collected Explanations, while also admitting the interpretations of Su Shi, Wang Yu [?], Wu Yu, Hu Yin, and others—is this not what that proposal meant?
The civil counsels and martial achievements of the imperial forebears have been splendidly manifested and carried forward. Indeed, one may say that, tested against the Three Kings, they contain no error; established before Heaven and Earth, they involve no contradiction; examined before ghosts and spirits, they admit no doubt; and even after a hundred generations, they could await a sage without misgiving. Do you gentlemen consider that the Complete Compendia now compiled by the assembled officials truly accord in every respect with the imperial intentions? I venture to suggest that, although passages concerning prophetic texts and apocryphal writings in the commentaries and subcommentaries should be excised, where these preserve pronunciations, explanations of words, institutions, and the names and particulars of things transmitted from the Han and Wei, no statement is so minute that it may be omitted. Although many of the interpretations incorporated into the minor annotations are worth adopting, during the Song and Yuan…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
之間圖解雜出大意主於自衒而不盡以
釋經擇不可以不精至如胡石以下諸儒
朱子固謂惜曰未必盡是亦當究其所以
得失之故而後反求諸心以正其謬宜各
自爲書以備一家而朱子論孟精義等書
則濂洛以來精蘊畧具尤世之不可無者
劉歆有云與其過而廢之寧過而立之况
傳聖人之經乎謂宜及今
聖神天子崇儒右文善繼善述以時明言於
===
朝
請發金匱石室之祕遣使購求四方遺書
簡命大儒詳加討葺使經生學士獲畢力於其
間將來舉子答義各以本註爲主條舉衆
說而斷以已意但令直述聖賢本旨與其
施用之實不必如今時文分段對股敷衍
浮詞一返洪武初
詔不拘舊格唯務經旨通暢之舊以昭
一代制作之大則於世教固不無小補也失今
punctuated: 之間，圖解雜出，大意主於自衒，而不盡以釋經，擇不可以不精。至如胡石以下諸儒，朱子固謂惜曰未必盡是，亦當究其所以得失之故，而後反求諸心，以正其謬。宜各自爲書，以備一家。而朱子《論孟精義》等書，則濂洛以來精蘊畧具，尤世之不可無者。劉歆有云：「與其過而廢之，寧過而立之。」况傳聖人之經乎？謂宜及今聖神天子崇儒右文、善繼善述，以時明言於朝，請發金匱石室之祕，遣使購求四方遺書，簡命大儒，詳加討葺，使經生學士獲畢力於其間。將來舉子答義，各以本註爲主，條舉衆說，而斷以已意，但令直述聖賢本旨與其施用之實，不必如今時文分段對股、敷衍浮詞。一返洪武初詔不拘舊格、唯務經旨通暢之舊，以昭一代制作之大，則於世教固不無小補也。失今
translation_en:
…during that period, diagrams and explanations appeared in profusion, chiefly intended for self-display rather than wholly devoted to explaining the Classics; selection therefore must be discerning. As for Hu, Shi, and the other scholars [?], Zhu Xi himself expressed regret and said that their interpretations were not necessarily all correct [?]. We should also investigate why they succeeded or failed, and then turn back to seek understanding within our own minds, correcting their errors. Their writings should each form a separate book, preserving each school's interpretation. Zhu Xi's Essential Meanings of the Analects and Mencius and similar works, however, contain in outline the essential insights transmitted from the Lian and Luo traditions onward, and are particularly indispensable to the world. Liu Xin once said: “Rather than err by discarding something, it is better to err by establishing it.” How much more does this apply to transmitting the sages' Classics?

I submit that we should take advantage of this time, when our sagely and divinely wise Son of Heaven honors Confucian learning and literary culture, and ably carries forward and develops his predecessors' achievements, to speak plainly at court. We should request that the hidden holdings of the golden coffers and stone chambers be opened, that envoys be dispatched to purchase surviving books throughout the realm, and that eminent Confucian scholars be selected and commissioned to examine and compile them thoroughly, allowing students of the Classics and men of learning to devote their full efforts to the undertaking.

In future, when examination candidates answer questions on the meaning of the Classics, each should take the primary commentary as his basis, enumerate the various interpretations, and judge them according to his own understanding. They should simply be required to state directly the original intentions of the sages and worthies and their practical application, without having to divide their writing into sections and paired passages or elaborate empty phrases as in today's examination prose. We should return entirely to the earlier practice prescribed by the edict at the beginning of the Hongwu reign: to be unbound by old formats and strive only to explain the meaning of the Classics clearly and fluently. This would manifest the grandeur of our dynasty's institutions and would surely make some modest contribution to the moral instruction of the age. If we let the present opportunity slip…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
不圖數年之後經籍散逸俗靡轉甚偏儒
曲士反得乗吾之虛以售其支離徑截之
謬而六經眞爲贅矣可不慮哉然吾聞朱
子之議貢舉也門人或疑卒未有考官者
言得人之難也執事誠欲祗若
文命使學者復見天地之純全以漸復先王之
盛必如明道先生熈寧之議特集天下名
儒相與講明正學以次分敎中外養賢斂
才然後可以一道德同風俗而盡革其末
===
流之弊若夫端本澄源則又自吾
君取人以身始惟有道者加之意焉謹對
第二問
薛欽
同考試官敎諭沈 批 春秋史學之宗遷固以下豈
足與此子能推本言之而歸重有關於
君德可以占其所存矣
同考試官學正蔡 批 以誠字立說最得史學之本宜錄以為式
考試官學正孫 批 論史學得旨□
punctuated:
不圖，數年之後，經籍散逸，俗靡轉甚，偏儒曲士反得乗吾之虛，以售其支離徑截之謬，而六經眞爲贅矣，可不慮哉？然吾聞朱子之議貢舉也，門人或疑卒未有考官者，言得人之難也。執事誠欲祗若文命，使學者復見天地之純全，以漸復先王之盛，必如明道先生熈寧之議，特集天下名儒，相與講明正學，以次分敎中外，養賢斂才，然後可以一道德，同風俗，而盡革其末流之弊。若夫端本澄源，則又自吾君取人以身始，惟有道者加之意焉。謹對。
第二問
薛欽
同考試官敎諭沈批：春秋，史學之宗，遷固以下豈足與？此子能推本言之，而歸重有關於君德，可以占其所存矣。
同考試官學正蔡批：以誠字立說，最得史學之本，宜錄以為式。
考試官學正孫批：論史學得旨□
translation_en:
…if we make no plans, within a few years the classical texts will have become scattered and lost, and the deterioration of customs will have grown still worse. Narrow-minded scholars and misguided literati will then exploit our weakness to peddle their errors of fragmented interpretation and shortcuts, and the Six Classics will truly become superfluous. Can we fail to be concerned? Yet I have heard that when Master Zhu discussed recruitment through examinations, some of his disciples doubted whether, in the end, anyone would be available to serve as examiner. They were speaking of the difficulty of finding suitable men. If you truly wish reverently to follow the imperial command, enabling scholars once again to perceive the purity and completeness of Heaven and Earth and gradually restoring the flourishing order of the former kings, you must follow Master Mingdao’s proposal of the Xining era: specially assemble the renowned Confucian scholars of the realm to elucidate orthodox learning together, then assign them in turn to teach in the capital and the provinces, nurturing worthy men and gathering talent. Only then can moral principles be unified, customs made uniform, and all the abuses of later degeneration eliminated. As for rectifying the root and clearing the source, this must begin with our ruler recruiting men through his own personal example. May those who possess the Way give this their attention. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Second Question
Xue Qin
Comment by Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor: “The Spring and Autumn Annals is the fountainhead of historical scholarship. How could Sima Qian, Ban Gu, or their successors compare with it? This candidate can trace the subject to its roots in his discussion and ultimately place the emphasis on its bearing upon the ruler’s virtue. From this we may discern what he holds in his heart.”
Comment by Associate Examiner Cai, School Instructor: “He builds his argument around the word ‘sincerity,’ grasping particularly well the foundation of historical scholarship. This should be recorded as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: “His discussion of historical scholarship grasps its essential purport □ [illegible].”

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授張批討論精確
春秋之所是天之所命也春秋之所非天
之所討也春秋是非之極與天地合其德
日月合其明四時合其序鬼神合其吉凶
先天而天弗違後天而奉天時况於人乎
明乎此者可與論史矣上焉者知誠之不
可掩也不見是圖敢文過乎而不得書者
鮮矣下焉者知誠之不可掩也君舉必書
肯狥人乎而不敢書者鮮矣執事舉唐虞
===
三代及遷固諸史得失下問夫豈不以古
者左史記言右史記動太史掌六典八法
八則藏約劑正歲年頒告朔辨事協禮讀
誄賜謚而天文繫世昭穆八柄會計納訪
策命事書制祿四方之志三皇五帝之書
萬民之治令皆典于其屬周知天下之故
史佚史克史蘇史黯史趙史墨又世掌之
未甞易業貳事故其史爲經而唐宋以來
史臣執筆隨諫官上殿徒立故事宰相記
punctuated:
考試官教授張批：討論精確。
春秋之所是，天之所命也；春秋之所非，天之所討也。春秋是非之極，與天地合其德，日月合其明，四時合其序，鬼神合其吉凶，先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時，况於人乎？明乎此者，可與論史矣。上焉者知誠之不可掩也，不見是圖，敢文過乎？而不得書者鮮矣。下焉者知誠之不可掩也，君舉必書，肯狥人乎？而不敢書者鮮矣。執事舉唐虞、三代及遷固諸史得失下問，夫豈不以古者左史記言，右史記動，太史掌六典、八法、八則，藏約劑，正歲年，頒告朔，辨事協禮，讀誄賜謚，而天文、繫世、昭穆、八柄、會計、納訪、策命、事書、制祿、四方之志、三皇五帝之書、萬民之治令，皆典于其屬，周知天下之故。史佚、史克、史蘇、史黯、史趙、史墨，又世掌之，未甞易業貳事，故其史爲經。而唐宋以來，史臣執筆，隨諫官上殿，徒立故事，宰相記
translation_en:
Examiner Zhang, an Instructor, comments: “The discussion is precise.”
What the Spring and Autumn Annals approves is what Heaven ordains; what the Spring and Autumn Annals condemns is what Heaven punishes. In its ultimate judgments of right and wrong, the Spring and Autumn Annals accords in virtue with Heaven and Earth, in illumination with the sun and moon, in order with the four seasons, and in judgments of good and ill fortune with spirits and gods. When it precedes Heaven, Heaven does not oppose it; when it follows Heaven, it observes Heaven’s proper times. How much more must this hold for human beings! With one who understands this, it is possible to discuss history. Those above know that the truth cannot be concealed. Attending even to what is unseen, would they dare disguise their faults? Thus there will be few things that cannot be recorded. Those below know that the truth cannot be concealed. Since every action of the ruler must be recorded, would they willingly yield to personal considerations? Thus there will be few things they dare not record.
You, honored examiners, have graciously asked about the merits and shortcomings of the histories of Tang and Yu, of the Three Dynasties, and of Sima Qian, Ban Gu, and others. Surely this is because, in antiquity, the Left Historiographer recorded words and the Right Historiographer recorded actions. The Grand Astrologer administered the Six Statutes, Eight Regulations, and Eight Rules; preserved covenants and contracts; corrected the calendrical year; promulgated announcements of the first day of each month; distinguished official duties and coordinated ritual observances; and read eulogies when posthumous names were bestowed. Moreover, celestial phenomena, genealogies, ancestral precedence, the eight instruments of sovereign authority, accounts, the reception of counsel, written investitures, records of events, the regulation of stipends, records of the four regions, writings of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, and ordinances governing all the people were all in the custody of his subordinate offices. He thus possessed comprehensive knowledge of the affairs of the realm. Shi Yi, Shi Ke, Shi Su, Shi An, Shi Zhao, and Shi Mo furthermore held their duties hereditarily, never changing their occupation or dividing their attention among other tasks. Their histories therefore became classics. Since the Tang and Song dynasties, however, historiographers have taken up their brushes and followed remonstrance officials into the audience hall merely to maintain established practice, while the chief councilors recorded…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
注學士脩撰止憑諸司供報事關得失皆
不記錄惟書除目辭見據此銓次謂之日
曆又必錄本進呈有不得書不敢書者異
時脩史率臆度於數百年之後筆削於衆
人之手竄易靡常迄無定論唯漢初太史
公位丞相上郡國計書先上太史公副上
宰相猶有古意而遷固父子家學相傳用
法專一發凡起例動有矩度西都風俗文
體大畧簡朴故辭直事核與後世雕飾駢
===
儷文工而實不至者弗類斯為彼善邪然
吾觀遷書大抵發憤蠶室之辱意有所鬱
結而不得通欲垂空言以自見耳非有不
虛美隱惡之實也故是非頗謬於聖人而
固不學剽竊殆甚於遷况武帝常怒遷議
已收景武二紀自毁之而封禪平準等書
意多隱訕要亦未為得書敢書也世徒喜
其文詞辨麗奇偉見史之難為憾無遷固
之才豈知史之失自遷固始文中子之評
punctuated: 注，學士脩撰，止憑諸司供報，事關得失皆不記錄，惟書除目、辭見，據此銓次，謂之日曆。又必錄本進呈，有不得書、不敢書者。異時脩史，率臆度於數百年之後，筆削於衆人之手，竄易靡常，迄無定論。唯漢初太史公位丞相上，郡國計書先上太史公，副上宰相，猶有古意。而遷固父子家學相傳，用法專一，發凡起例，動有矩度。西都風俗文體大畧簡朴，故辭直事核，與後世雕飾駢儷、文工而實不至者弗類。斯為彼善邪？然吾觀遷書，大抵發憤蠶室之辱，意有所鬱結而不得通，欲垂空言以自見耳，非有不虛美隱惡之實也。故是非頗謬於聖人，而固不學，剽竊殆甚於遷。况武帝常怒遷議已，收景武二紀，自毁之，而封禪、平準等書，意多隱訕，要亦未為得書、敢書也。世徒喜其文詞辨麗奇偉，見史之難為，憾無遷固之才，豈知史之失自遷固始？文中子之評
translation_en:
…the chief ministers made records, and the academicians compiled them, relying solely on reports supplied by the various offices. Matters bearing on successes and failures were left unrecorded; only lists of appointments and audiences for departure or presentation were entered. These were selected and arranged into what were called daily calendars. Copies also had to be submitted for imperial inspection, so there were things that could not be written and things that no one dared write. When histories were compiled later, they generally rested on conjectures made several hundred years after the events, with editing passing through many hands. Alterations were incessant, and no settled judgment was ever reached.
Only in the early Han did the Grand Astrologer rank above the Counselor-in-Chief: the accounting reports of commanderies and kingdoms were submitted first to the Grand Astrologer, with duplicates sent to the chief minister. This still retained something of ancient practice. In the families of Sima Qian and Ban Gu, learning was transmitted from father to son. Their methods were consistent, and their establishment of general principles and conventions always followed definite standards. The customs and literary style of the Western Han were broadly simple and unadorned; hence their language was straightforward and their accounts of events substantial. They differed from later writers whose ornate parallel prose was skillful but lacked substance. Does this make the former superior?
Yet when I examine Qian’s history, I find that it largely vents his indignation at the humiliation of castration. His feelings were pent up and could find no release; he merely wished to leave words to posterity through which he could make himself known. He did not truly fulfill the principle of avoiding unwarranted praise and concealing no evil [?]. Thus his judgments of right and wrong diverged considerably from those of the sages. Gu, moreover, lacked learning, and his plagiarism was perhaps even worse than Qian’s. Furthermore, Emperor Wu was often angered by Qian’s criticism of him [?], confiscated the two Basic Annals of Emperors Jing and Wu, and destroyed them himself. The treatises on the Feng and Shan Sacrifices and on the Balanced Standard, among others, contain much veiled disparagement. Ultimately, then, Qian too cannot be said to have been free to write or to have dared to write.
People merely delight in the eloquence, beauty, originality, and grandeur of their language. Recognizing how difficult it is to write history, they lament the absence of talents like Qian and Gu. How could they know that the failings of historical writing began with Qian and Gu? Wenzhongzi’s assessment…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
已爲不刋則於曄壽喬約諸史奚必置低
昂于其間哉顧甞聞之自古人君出入起
居皆有史女史内史外史是也史無一日
無書以日繫月以月繫時以時繫年是也
而近日記載之畧殆有逾於宋者甞讀虞
書叙堯舜禹臯君臣之明聖率不越乎都
俞吁咈之間非當時善言德行者審視詳
記固未易弁其精意而傳之而公羊曰所
見異詞所聞異詞所傳聞異詞雖孔子作
===
春秋於定哀則其事詳於隱莊則其事畧
况其下乎是則老成之深慮而記曰王前
巫後史中心無爲也以守至正史之有關
於君德又如此執事安得以爲迂緩而忽
之哉謹對
第三問
鄭富
同考試官訓導李 批 辨論師友是非言簡義明蓋
胸中素有定見者
punctuated:
已爲不刋，則於曄、壽、喬、約諸史，奚必置低昂于其間哉？顧甞聞之，自古人君出入起居，皆有史，女史、内史、外史是也。史無一日無書，以日繫月，以月繫時，以時繫年是也。而近日記載之畧，殆有逾於宋者。甞讀《虞書》，叙堯、舜、禹、臯君臣之明聖，率不越乎都俞吁咈之間。非當時善言德行者審視詳記，固未易弁其精意而傳之。而《公羊》曰：「所見異詞，所聞異詞，所傳聞異詞。」雖孔子作《春秋》，於定、哀則其事詳，於隱、莊則其事畧，况其下乎？是則老成之深慮。而《記》曰：「王前巫，後史，中心無爲也，以守至正。」史之有關於君德又如此，執事安得以爲迂緩而忽之哉？謹對。

第三問
鄭富
同考試官訓導李批：「辨論師友是非，言簡義明，蓋胸中素有定見者。」
translation_en:
…is already an immutable judgment; why, then, must one rank the histories of Ye, Shou, Qiao, and Yue against one another? Yet I have heard that, from antiquity, rulers had scribes recording their departures and returns and their daily activities: the Palace Women Scribes, Interior Scribes, and Exterior Scribes served this purpose. There was no day on which the scribes made no record: they arranged days under months, months under seasons, and seasons under years. Yet the scantiness of recent records probably exceeds even that of the Song.

I once read the Book of Yu. Its account of the enlightened sageliness of the rulers and ministers Yao, Shun, Yu, and Gao is largely confined to their exchanges of praise, assent, reservation, and dissent. Had those who recorded their excellent words and virtuous conduct at the time not observed carefully and recorded fully, it would certainly have been difficult to distinguish [?] and transmit their essential meaning. The Gongyang Commentary says: “What was witnessed is worded differently; what was heard is worded differently; what was learned through transmitted reports is worded differently.” Even when Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, his accounts of events under Dukes Ding and Ai were detailed, while those under Dukes Yin and Zhuang were brief. How much more must this apply to lesser historians? This reflects the profound deliberation of an experienced elder. The Book of Rites says: “Before the king stood the invocator, and behind him the scribe; at his center he remained without contrived action, thereby maintaining utmost rectitude.” Such, moreover, is the bearing of the historian’s office upon the ruler’s virtue. How could you, honored officials, dismiss it as impractical and dilatory, and neglect it? Respectfully submitted in reply.

Third Question
Zheng Fu
Associate Examiner Li, Assistant Instructor, comments: “He distinguishes and discusses right and wrong concerning teachers and friends. His wording is concise and his meaning clear. Evidently he has long held settled judgments in his own mind.”

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭文批剖析學術淵源之正歸重孟
子其所養可占矣取之
考試官學正孫批有歸宿
考試官教授張批議論明正
孰不爲學學於舜之門舜之徒也學於蹠
之門蹠之徒也孰不爲學學於舜之門由
蹠之道蹠之徒也學於蹠之門由舜之道
舜之徒也昔者吳起師曾參曾參大孝吳
起忘親道相反者也況參旣先起未求將
===
也而絕之起亦盡棄其學學兵法矣起猶
得爲曾子徒乎李斯事荀卿荀卿明王道
李斯棄王法勢相反者也然斯燔詩書滅
禮樂皆卿倨肆無忌謂性爲惡謂禮爲僞
謂孔子子思孟軻亂天下有以啓之斯不
得爲荀子徒乎凡老子所謂道德非吾所
謂道德雜權詐而爲言者也觀其書曰知
其雄守其雌爲天下谿知其白守其黑爲
天下谷其流入於機變殘忍非理所必至
punctuated:
同考試官教諭文批：剖析學術淵源之正，歸重孟子，其所養可占矣。取之。
考試官學正孫批：有歸宿。
考試官教授張批：議論明正。
孰不爲學？學於舜之門，舜之徒也；學於蹠之門，蹠之徒也。孰不爲學？學於舜之門，由蹠之道，蹠之徒也；學於蹠之門，由舜之道，舜之徒也。昔者吳起師曾參，曾參大孝，吳起忘親，道相反者也。況參旣先起未求將也而絕之，起亦盡棄其學，學兵法矣。起猶得爲曾子徒乎？李斯事荀卿，荀卿明王道，李斯棄王法，勢相反者也。然斯燔詩書，滅禮樂，皆卿倨肆無忌，謂性爲惡，謂禮爲僞，謂孔子、子思、孟軻亂天下，有以啓之。斯不得爲荀子徒乎？凡老子所謂道德，非吾所謂道德，雜權詐而爲言者也。觀其書曰：「知其雄，守其雌，爲天下谿；知其白，守其黑，爲天下谷。」其流入於機變殘忍，非理所必至
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Wen, Instructor, comments: “He analyzes the orthodox sources of learning and gives primary weight to Mengzi. From this one can judge his cultivation. Accept him.”
Examiner Sun, Instructor, comments: “The argument reaches a definite conclusion.”
Examiner Zhang, Professor, comments: “The reasoning is clear and correct.”
Who does not pursue learning? One who studies at Shun’s gate is Shun’s disciple; one who studies at Zhi’s gate is Zhi’s disciple. Who does not pursue learning? One who studies at Shun’s gate but follows Zhi’s way is Zhi’s disciple; one who studies at Zhi’s gate but follows Shun’s way is Shun’s disciple.
Formerly, Wu Qi took Zeng Shen as his teacher. Zeng Shen was profoundly filial, whereas Wu Qi forgot his parents: their ways were opposed. Moreover, Shen had already severed ties with Qi before Qi sought a general’s command [?], and Qi completely abandoned his teachings and studied military methods. Can Qi still be counted as a disciple of Master Zeng?
Li Si served Xun Qing. Xun Qing elucidated the kingly Way, whereas Li Si discarded the laws of the ancient kings: their positions were opposed. Yet Si’s burning of the Books of Odes and Documents and his destruction of rites and music were all prompted in some measure by Qing’s unrestrained arrogance: he declared human nature evil, called ritual artificial, and said that Kongzi, Zisi, and Meng Ke brought disorder to the world. Can Si not be counted as a disciple of Master Xun?
What Laozi calls the Way and virtue is not what we call the Way and virtue; his discourse mingles them with expediency and deceit. Look at what his book says: “Know the male, keep to the female, and become the ravine of the world; know the white, keep to the black, and become the valley of the world.” That this teaching should degenerate into cunning and cruelty—is this not its inevitable outcome…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
哉太史公曰申子卑卑施之於名實韓子
引繩墨切事情明是非其極慘礉少恩皆
原於道德之意有以也賈誼少從河南守
吳公吳公故與李斯同邑嘗學事焉吳公
之學雖無可考吾視其所舉大抵悻悻自
好喜功名嬰撫在廷之臣欲出其上故朱
子曰誼本戰國縱橫之學只是較近道理
不至如儀秦蔡范之甚耳則亦安見其眞
能寒於水哉易曰頤貞吉養正則吉也觀
===
頤觀其所養也自求口實觀其自養也愚
於明問得養道焉荀卿老聃自養苟正必
不至以其學術禍天下後世以誼之才少
加持養又得聖賢爲之依歸殆不止於通
達國體同死生輕去就如遷固所賛而已
故曰洙泗多賢儀秦皆詐非其性異養使
然也其唯曾子乎師孔子父曾皙友顏淵
由賜之流而仁以爲已任故竟以魯得之
而傳獨得其宗觀於子思孟子可見矣學
punctuated: 哉？太史公曰：「申子卑卑，施之於名實；韓子引繩墨，切事情，明是非，其極慘礉少恩，皆原於道德之意。」有以也。賈誼少從河南守吳公，吳公故與李斯同邑，嘗學事焉。吳公之學雖無可考，吾視其所舉，大抵悻悻自好，喜功名，嬰撫在廷之臣，欲出其上。故朱子曰：「誼本戰國縱橫之學，只是較近道理，不至如儀秦蔡范之甚耳。」則亦安見其眞能寒於水哉？《易》曰：「頤，貞吉。」養正則吉也。「觀頤」，觀其所養也；「自求口實」，觀其自養也。愚於明問得養道焉。荀卿、老聃自養苟正，必不至以其學術禍天下後世。以誼之才，少加持養，又得聖賢爲之依歸，殆不止於通達國體、同死生、輕去就，如遷固所賛而已。故曰：「洙泗多賢，儀秦皆詐，非其性異，養使然也。」其唯曾子乎？師孔子，父曾皙，友顏淵、由、賜之流，而仁以爲已任，故竟以魯得之，而傳獨得其宗。觀於子思、孟子可見矣。學
translation_en:
…is it not? The Grand Astrologer said: “Master Shen confined himself to the particulars, applying his teachings to names and actualities. Master Han applied the measuring line, addressed the realities of affairs, and distinguished right from wrong; carried to their extreme, his teachings were harsh and unmerciful. Both originated in the ideas of the Way and its virtue.” There was reason for this judgment. In his youth, Jia Yi studied under Lord Wu, Governor of Henan. Lord Wu originally came from the same locality as Li Si and had studied under him. Although Lord Wu’s learning cannot be investigated, when I consider the man he recommended, I find him generally obstinate and self-regarding, fond of achievement and fame, seeking to control the ministers at court [?] and wishing to rise above them. Thus Master Zhu said: “Jia Yi’s learning was fundamentally that of the Warring States persuaders who advocated vertical and horizontal alliances. It merely came somewhat closer to moral principle and did not go to the extremes of Zhang Yi, Su Qin, Cai Ze, and Fan Ju.” How, then, can we see that he truly became ‘colder than water’—surpassing his teacher?

The Book of Changes says: “Nourishment: constancy brings good fortune.” Nourishing what is correct thus brings good fortune. “Observe nourishment” means observing what a person nourishes; “seek sustenance for your own mouth” means observing how a person nourishes himself. From your illuminating question, I have gained an understanding of the way of cultivation. Had Xun Qing and Lao Dan cultivated themselves correctly, they would certainly not have brought calamity upon the world and later generations through their teachings. With Jia Yi’s talent, had he exercised a little more discipline and cultivation, and also found his guide and ultimate refuge in the sages and worthies, he would surely have achieved more than understanding the fundamentals of government, regarding life and death alike, and taking lightly whether he left office or remained—the qualities for which Sima Qian and Ban Gu praised him. Thus it is said: “Among those of the Zhu and Si rivers were many worthies, while Zhang Yi and Su Qin were both deceitful. This was not because their natures differed: cultivation made them so.” Was Zengzi not the outstanding example? He had Confucius as his teacher, Zeng Xi as his father, and Yan Yuan, Zhong You, Duanmu Ci, and their fellows as his friends; he took benevolence as his own responsibility. Thus, despite his dullness, he ultimately attained the Way and alone grasped its essential lineage in transmitting it. This can be seen by considering Zisi and Mencius. Those who study…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
者傳習親師論學取友其唯學曾子乎
第四問
王一言
同考試官教諭鄧批去文就實之意溢于尚友之外
同考試官教諭汪批景先賢律後學一以反本爲
說讀之令人灑然
考試官學正孫批詳盡
考試官教授張批知本之論
文之將興者天也成之以人人之立身者
===
德也成之以學斯文之興必有豪傑之士
卓立以表世獨行以高尚者爲之先焉茍
不知學猶德之偏也講學以成德德成而
行尊不合於道者鮮矣孰謂天之生才而
有不待學以成者哉閩爲東南奧區實禹
貢要荒之外周漢而上文獻不得而徵矣
至唐中葉有歐陽詹氏與韓子聯第稱龍
虎榜而民始知學其舉韓愈爲博士固非
同年之私稱何蕃之仁勇亦好德之良也
punctuated:
者傳習、親師、論學、取友，其唯學曾子乎？
第四問
王一言
同考試官教諭鄧批：去文就實之意，溢于尚友之外。
同考試官教諭汪批：景先賢，律後學，一以反本爲說，讀之令人灑然。
考試官學正孫批：詳盡。
考試官教授張批：知本之論。
文之將興者，天也；成之以人。人之立身者，德也；成之以學。斯文之興，必有豪傑之士，卓立以表世，獨行以高尚者，爲之先焉。茍不知學，猶德之偏也。講學以成德，德成而行尊，不合於道者鮮矣。孰謂天之生才，而有不待學以成者哉？閩爲東南奧區，實禹貢要荒之外。周漢而上，文獻不得而徵矣。至唐中葉，有歐陽詹氏，與韓子聯第，稱龍虎榜，而民始知學。其舉韓愈爲博士，固非同年之私；稱何蕃之仁勇，亦好德之良也。
translation_en:
…those who study, transmitting and practicing what they learn, drawing close to teachers, discussing learning, and choosing friends—should they not take Zengzi as their model?
Fourth Policy Question
Wang Yiyan
Comment by Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor: The intention to leave ornament behind and attend to substance extends beyond the theme of befriending the ancients.
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: He admires former worthies and sets standards for later students, consistently arguing for a return to fundamentals. Reading this leaves one refreshed.
Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: Thorough and exhaustive.
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: A discourse that understands the fundamentals.
That culture is about to flourish is Heaven’s doing; its fulfillment comes through human beings. What establishes a person in life is virtue; its fulfillment comes through learning. When this cultural tradition flourishes, there must first be outstanding men who stand prominently as models for their age and pursue independent conduct with lofty aspirations. Yet if they do not understand learning, their virtue remains one-sided. Through the investigation and discussion of learning, they perfect their virtue; once virtue is perfected and conduct becomes worthy of respect, seldom will anything fail to accord with the Way. Who could say that among the talents Heaven brings forth, some can attain fulfillment without learning?
Min is a secluded region of the southeast, lying indeed beyond the outer yao and huang zones described in the Tribute of Yu. For the Zhou and Han periods and earlier, written records and worthy men cannot be adduced as evidence. By the middle of the Tang dynasty, Ouyang Zhan passed the examination alongside Master Han, on what was called the ‘Dragon and Tiger List,’ and the people began to appreciate learning. His recommendation of Han Yu as an Erudite was certainly no act of favoritism toward a fellow graduate of the same year; his praise of He Fan’s benevolence and courage likewise showed the excellence of his love of virtue.

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
文集之傳雖不逮韓亦韓之儔已陳嘏氏
爲宣宗所知稱琬琰器而民始知仕長於
詞賦有相如之風尤工篆隸亦斯邈之流
也官箴之服雖止郎中亦有用之才已風
氣始開人文始著器業之大譽處之隆遽
已如此烏得不啟宋儒之盛哉楊億之文
蘇子病其詭矣而有忠清直亮之稱不然
孰爲學士而富貴弗之保也蘇頌之節朱
子稱其進退不苟古之大臣不然孰爲舍
===
人而落職弗之顧也曹輔初爲正字小官
耳敢論大事愛君之心也李綱出入將相
憂國忘身充此愛君之心而已是四人者
師友講習不𡮢槩見而立朝大節邦家之
光雖曰未學吾必謂之學已其殆庶幾乎
程氏倡道於洛游楊受之龜山傳之豫章
豫章傳之延平朱子之聞道蓋自延平始
已故一則曰愚聞之師二則曰愚聞之師
其奉韋齋之命而稟學於屏山籍溪白水
punctuated:
文集之傳雖不逮韓，亦韓之儔已。陳嘏氏爲宣宗所知，稱琬琰器，而民始知仕。長於詞賦，有相如之風，尤工篆隸，亦斯邈之流也。官箴之服雖止郎中，亦有用之才已。風氣始開，人文始著，器業之大、譽處之隆，遽已如此，烏得不啟宋儒之盛哉？
楊億之文，蘇子病其詭矣，而有忠清直亮之稱。不然，孰爲學士而富貴弗之保也？蘇頌之節，朱子稱其進退不苟，古之大臣。不然，孰爲舍人而落職弗之顧也？曹輔初爲正字，小官耳，敢論大事，愛君之心也。李綱出入將相，憂國忘身，充此愛君之心而已。是四人者，師友講習不𡮢槩見，而立朝大節，邦家之光。「雖曰未學，吾必謂之學已」，其殆庶幾乎！
程氏倡道於洛，游楊受之，龜山傳之豫章，豫章傳之延平，朱子之聞道蓋自延平始已。故一則曰「愚聞之師」，二則曰「愚聞之師」。其奉韋齋之命，而稟學於屏山、籍溪、白水
translation_en:
…Although his collected writings have not circulated as widely as Han Yu’s, he was nevertheless Han’s peer. Chen Gu came to the notice of Emperor Xuanzong and was praised as a vessel of precious jade; the people then began to understand service in office. He excelled in lyric compositions and rhapsodies, displaying the style of Sima Xiangru, and was particularly accomplished in seal and clerical scripts, belonging also to the company of Li Si and Cheng Miao. Although his discharge of official duties extended only to service as a bureau director, he too possessed talents useful to the state. Just as the intellectual climate began to open and cultural accomplishment to emerge, the greatness of these men’s capacities and achievements, and the eminence of their reputations and standing, were already such as this. How could they have failed to prepare the way for the flourishing of Confucian learning under the Song?
Master Su criticized Yang Yi’s writing for its oddity, yet Yang was renowned for loyalty, integrity, uprightness, and candor. Otherwise, who, holding office as an academician, would have declined to safeguard his wealth and rank? As for Su Song’s integrity, Master Zhu praised him as a great minister of antiquity, scrupulous in both accepting office and withdrawing from it. Otherwise, who, serving as a drafting official, would have disregarded dismissal from office? Cao Fu initially served as a proofreader, merely a minor official, yet dared to discuss great affairs: this expressed his devotion to his ruler. Li Gang served in both military command and the chief ministership, forgetting himself in his concern for the state. This was simply the full realization of that same devotion to the ruler. Accounts of these four men’s study and discussion with teachers and friends are not readily to be found, yet their great integrity at court brought glory to the realm. “Though someone might say that he has not studied, I would certainly say that he has.” Surely these men came close to that ideal!
The Cheng masters first expounded the Way at Luoyang, and You and Yang received it. Guishan transmitted it to Yuzhang, and Yuzhang transmitted it to Yanping. Master Zhu’s learning of the Way began, it would seem, with Yanping. Thus he said time and again, “I, in my ignorance, heard this from my teacher.” In obedience to Weizhai’s command, he received instruction from Pingshan, Jixi, and Baishui…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
三君子者於韋齋友也其學未嘗不自伊
洛中來而延平所得者深矣先乎此若胡
文定氏得私淑之教於程門程門之得夫
正傳者莫如游楊也文定與之遊而言性
乃有同體異用之說二子寅宏之學又不
能無過與不及之差然正色危言剛大方
直之氣律貪起懦之功皆不忝其父焉噫
胡氏父子祖於伊洛德望偉然而精微未
造學莫便於近其人信矣後乎此若蔡神
===
與氏以聖賢之學教元定元定之教夫三
子者猶之神與也淵紹易學朱子有論撰
詳悉之稱沈紹書學又有須見帝王之心
之論而精識絕才不可屈之志不可窮之
辨則歸之季通焉噫蔡氏父祖子孫識趣
偉然好遯不汚而效用斯阻君子求其在
我者已矣文公季子召對理宗屢有啓迪
之益敭歷中外紹其宦學之傳寅宏淵沈
晳之參乎則在亦孔之鯉也黄勉齋受吾
punctuated: 三君子者，於韋齋友也。其學未嘗不自伊洛中來，而延平所得者深矣。先乎此，若胡文定氏得私淑之教於程門，程門之得夫正傳者莫如游楊也。文定與之遊，而言性乃有同體異用之說。二子寅宏之學，又不能無過與不及之差。然正色危言，剛大方直之氣，律貪起懦之功，皆不忝其父焉。噫！胡氏父子祖於伊洛，德望偉然，而精微未造，學莫便於近其人，信矣！後乎此，若蔡神與氏以聖賢之學教元定，元定之教夫三子者，猶之神與也。淵紹易學，朱子有論撰詳悉之稱；沈紹書學，又有須見帝王之心之論。而精識絕才、不可屈之志、不可窮之辨，則歸之季通焉。噫！蔡氏父祖子孫，識趣偉然，好遯不汚，而效用斯阻，君子求其在我者已矣。文公季子召對理宗，屢有啓迪之益，敭歷中外，紹其宦學之傳。寅宏淵沈，晳之參乎？則在亦孔之鯉也。黄勉齋受吾
translation_en:
…these three gentlemen were friends of Weizhai. Their learning invariably derived from the tradition of the Yi and Luo rivers, but Yanping’s attainment was profound indeed. Earlier, Hu Wending received instruction indirectly from the Cheng school. Among that school’s followers, none received its authentic transmission more fully than You and Yang. Wending associated with them, yet in discussing human nature he advanced the doctrine of a shared substance with differing functions. The learning of his two sons, Yin and Hong, likewise could not avoid deviations of excess and deficiency. Nevertheless, in their grave demeanor and forthright speech, their strong, expansive, upright spirit, and their achievements in restraining the greedy and rousing the timid, neither disgraced his father. Alas! The Hu father and sons took the Yi–Luo tradition as their source and were imposing in virtue and reputation, yet had not attained its subtleties. Truly, nothing facilitates learning more than personal proximity to its teacher!

Later, Cai Shenyu taught Yuanding the learning of the sages and worthies; Yuanding taught his own three sons just as Shenyu had taught him. Yuan carried on the study of the Book of Changes, and Master Zhu praised the thoroughness of his discussions and writings. Shen carried on the study of the Book of Documents, maintaining that one must discern the minds of the ancient emperors and kings. But penetrating insight, exceptional talent, an indomitable resolve, and inexhaustible powers of argument were attributed to Jitong. Alas! Across the generations, the Cai family possessed remarkable discernment and aspirations. They cherished retirement and remained untainted, but their opportunities to put their abilities to use were thereby obstructed. The gentleman seeks only what lies within his own power.

The youngest son of Lord Wen was summoned to an imperial audience with Lizong and repeatedly offered beneficial enlightenment. Serving in posts both at court and in the provinces, he continued his father’s tradition of official service and learning. Were Yin, Hong, Yuan, and Shen like Shen in relation to his father Xi? Then Zai, too, was like Li in relation to his father Confucius. Huang Mianzhai was entrusted with our …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
道之托居敬窮理之功一時同遊無出其
右易禮通解之作發明經旨不負其師劉
雲莊講道武夷爲終焉之計及其仕也應
詔陳言乃請開不諱之門招盡言之士推
時政之得失明朝廷之是非雖未見其易
禮諸解而已知其人巳陳北溪辯陸氏之
學風力甚勁字義之作其庶幾乎廖子晦
守先師之道隱者爲高槎溪之集爲可稱
巳眞西山蒙世大禁講學力行采羣書爲
===
衍義受知理宗而僞學之禁於是除焉雖
不及朱子之門亦有功於道者也勿軒以
道淑人從游者衆以經意爲標題輯文公
要語而門人之說皆附錄焉雖不得爲朱
子之徒亦聞風而起者也鄭仲實氏精於
禮學擧要從宜特爲西山所敬而邑人德
之亦是行其所學諸君子者雖道與時違
不獲盡用而講明正學昌斯道之傳不有
先哲孰開我人可忘所自乎黃氏曰孟子
banxin: 鄉試錄 七十一 周章
punctuated: 道之托，居敬窮理之功，一時同遊無出其右。易禮通解之作，發明經旨，不負其師。劉雲莊講道武夷，爲終焉之計；及其仕也，應詔陳言，乃請開不諱之門，招盡言之士，推時政之得失，明朝廷之是非。雖未見其易禮諸解，而已知其人巳。陳北溪辯陸氏之學，風力甚勁，《字義》之作，其庶幾乎！廖子晦守先師之道，隱者爲高，《槎溪之集》爲可稱巳。眞西山蒙世大禁，講學力行，采羣書爲《衍義》，受知理宗，而僞學之禁於是除焉。雖不及朱子之門，亦有功於道者也。勿軒以道淑人，從游者衆，以經意爲標題，輯文公要語，而門人之說皆附錄焉。雖不得爲朱子之徒，亦聞風而起者也。鄭仲實氏精於禮學，擧要從宜，特爲西山所敬，而邑人德之，亦是行其所學。諸君子者，雖道與時違，不獲盡用，而講明正學，昌斯道之傳。不有先哲，孰開我？人可忘所自乎？黃氏曰：「孟子
translation_en: …the charge of transmitting the Way. In his achievements in maintaining reverence and fully investigating principle, none of his fellow scholars at the time surpassed him. His comprehensive explanations of the Changes and the Rites [?] elucidated the meaning of the classics and did credit to his teacher. Liu Yunzhuang taught the Way at Wuyi, intending to spend the remainder of his life there. When he entered office, however, he responded to an imperial edict inviting counsel by requesting that the court open its doors to unrestricted criticism, summon men who would speak their minds fully, examine the successes and failures of current policies, and distinguish right from wrong at court. Although I have not seen his various explanations of the Changes and the Rites, I already know what sort of man he was. Chen Beixi disputed the teachings of Master Lu with great vigor and force. His Explanation of Terms surely came close to the ideal! Liao Zihui upheld the Way of his late teacher; his distinction lay in his life of retirement, and his Chaxi Collection merits praise. Zhen Xishan, facing the great prohibition of his age [?], pursued scholarly inquiry and earnestly put his learning into practice. Drawing on many books, he compiled the Extended Meaning. He gained the recognition of Emperor Lizong, and the prohibition on “spurious learning” was thereupon lifted. Although he never studied directly under Master Zhu, he too rendered service to the Way. Wuxuan improved others through the Way, and many studied under him. Using the meanings of the classics as headings, he compiled the essential sayings of Master Wengong, appending the explanations of his disciples. Although he could not become a disciple of Master Zhu, he too was inspired to action by hearing of his example. Zheng Zhongshi was accomplished in the study of ritual, grasping its essentials and adapting them to circumstances. Xishan held him in particular esteem, and the people of his county were grateful for his beneficence: he too put his learning into practice. Although the Way upheld by these gentlemen was at odds with their times, and their abilities could not be fully employed, they expounded orthodox learning and furthered the transmission of this Way. Without these earlier worthies, who would have enlightened us? Can people forget the source from which they came? Master Huang said: “Mencius …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
而後周程張子繼其絕至朱子而始著自
其著也而口耳之學興矣是故觀人於朱
子之前者求其有見道之功而不拘其出
處之迹觀人於朱子之後者求其有躬行
之實而不貴其著作之富閩之先哲亦多
矣執事獨舉數子者爲問亦是意乎雖然
孔子之徒宜不在朱子下也惟有子曾子
子思之所記述爲足以傳其他門戶之衆
微言大義日以乖離學朱子者苟眩其名
===
===
而不究其實得於言而不求之心論譔旣
多簡袠已重賢者識其大者云耳盡信書
而心學累此固八閩之憂亦舉世士習之
訛也善乎趙清獻公之言曰后稷所讀何
書彼非以政爲學者也懼文勝其實爲反
本之論盛宋之時已見其流之弊矣當世
道之責者若之何哉
第五問趙恒
punctuated:
而後，周、程、張子繼其絕，至朱子而始著。自其著也，而口耳之學興矣。是故觀人於朱子之前者，求其有見道之功，而不拘其出處之迹；觀人於朱子之後者，求其有躬行之實，而不貴其著作之富。」閩之先哲亦多矣，執事獨舉數子者爲問，亦是意乎？雖然，孔子之徒宜不在朱子下也，惟有子、曾子、子思之所記述爲足以傳。其他門戶之衆，微言大義日以乖離。學朱子者，苟眩其名而不究其實，得於言而不求之心，論譔旣多，簡袠已重，賢者識其大者云耳。盡信書而心學累，此固八閩之憂，亦舉世士習之訛也。善乎趙清獻公之言曰：「后稷所讀何書？」彼非以政爲學者也，懼文勝其實，爲反本之論。盛宋之時，已見其流之弊矣。當世道之責者，若之何哉？

第五問，趙恒。
translation_en:
…After him, Masters Zhou, Cheng, and Zhang renewed the interrupted transmission; only with Master Zhu did it become manifest. Once it became manifest, however, learning that passed merely from ear to mouth arose. Thus, when assessing men before Master Zhu, we seek their achievements in apprehending the Way, without restricting our judgment to the outward circumstances of their entering office or withdrawing from public life. When assessing men after Master Zhu, we seek evidence of their personal practice, without prizing the abundance of their writings.” Fujian, too, has had many earlier worthies. In selecting just these few masters for your question, did you have this same intention?

Nevertheless, the disciples of Confucius surely ought not to rank below Master Zhu. Yet only the records of Youzi, Zengzi, and Zisi proved sufficient to transmit the teaching. Among the numerous other schools, subtle words and great principles became increasingly distorted. If those who study Master Zhu are dazzled by his reputation without investigating the substance of his teaching, grasp its words without seeking it in their own hearts, then, however numerous their treatises and weighty their volumes, one can only say, “The worthy recognize its greater essentials.” To trust books entirely and thereby encumber the learning of the mind is indeed a concern for the Eight Min regions of Fujian, but it is also an error in scholarly practice throughout the world.

How fine were the words of Zhao, the Duke Qingxian: “What books did Hou Ji read?” He was not treating government as learning; rather, fearing that literary refinement would outweigh substance, he argued for a return to the root. Even in the flourishing Song dynasty, he had already discerned the abuses into which this tendency would develop. What, then, should those responsible for the moral order of the age do?

Fifth policy question: Zhao Heng.

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭鄧批治盜治心歸於任人立法知所
本矣于其具文武才非邪
同考試官教諭汪批息盜歸重任人得根本之論
矣宜錄
考試官學正孫批有斷制
考試官教授張批據實可取
善治盜者治其心耳矣而法不與焉執法
以禦盜則盜可遏於已發而不能遏之於
未發遏之于未發者所以止盜之心也蓋
===
國依於民民依於官任官以裕民裕民以
止盜治心之術也而法者特其具耳豈可
恃以為安哉今夫盜亦吾民也其稟生理
之全樂室家之好猶夫人也其審善惡之
歸决死生之分猶夫人也惟其困窮累其
心溝壑切於念于是乎棄其身於盜賊以
為旦夕之計而為民牧者又不知所以正
其本而惟法之逞是猶醫者之於病不審
其虛實之理而徒執藥劑以治其標吾見
punctuated:
同考試官教諭鄧批：治盜治心，歸於任人立法，知所本矣。于其具文武才非邪？
同考試官教諭汪批：息盜歸重任人，得根本之論矣，宜錄。
考試官學正孫批：有斷制。
考試官教授張批：據實可取。
善治盜者，治其心耳矣，而法不與焉。執法以禦盜，則盜可遏於已發，而不能遏之於未發。遏之于未發者，所以止盜之心也。蓋國依於民，民依於官。任官以裕民，裕民以止盜，治心之術也，而法者特其具耳，豈可恃以為安哉？今夫盜亦吾民也，其稟生理之全，樂室家之好，猶夫人也；其審善惡之歸，决死生之分，猶夫人也。惟其困窮累其心，溝壑切於念，于是乎棄其身於盜賊，以為旦夕之計。而為民牧者，又不知所以正其本，而惟法之逞。是猶醫者之於病，不審其虛實之理，而徒執藥劑以治其標。吾見
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor: “Controlling banditry means governing people’s hearts. By grounding this in appointing men and establishing laws, the writer understands where the foundation lies. Does he not possess both civil and military talents [?]?”
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “In putting the emphasis on appointing men as the means to end banditry, he has reached the root of the matter. This answer should be selected.”
Comment by Examiner Sun, School Instructor: “Shows decisiveness and judgment.”
Comment by Examiner Zhang, Professor: “Grounded in realities and worthy of acceptance.”
Those skilled at controlling banditry simply govern people’s hearts; laws have no part in this. If one relies on enforcing laws to ward off banditry, it can be checked after it has arisen, but cannot be prevented before it arises. To check it before it arises is to put an end to the desire to become a bandit. The state depends on the people, and the people depend on officials. Appointing officials to improve the people’s livelihood, and improving their livelihood to end banditry—this is the art of governing hearts. Laws are merely its instruments. How could one rely on them to secure peace?
Now bandits, too, are our people. They are like everyone else in being endowed with the full principles of human life and taking pleasure in the affections of home and family. They are like everyone else in discerning the consequences of good and evil and judging the distinction between life and death. It is only because hardship and poverty burden their hearts, and the prospect of dying in a ditch presses upon their thoughts, that they abandon themselves to banditry as a means of surviving from one day to the next. Yet those who shepherd the people do not understand how to set matters right at their root and instead give free rein to the law. This is like a physician treating illness who fails to examine the underlying conditions of depletion and repletion, but merely applies medicines to treat its outward symptoms. I see…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
其藥愈投而病愈滋矣執事憂八閩宼盜
之虞而以古人備盜為問蓋亦穔豕之牙
而為今日東南民慮者至切也愚也願酌
古準今而陳之可乎夫古昔盛時奸宄之
戒干羽之舞其民皞皞如也逮周而防制
始立蓋周公以關雎麟趾之意而行周官
之法度於是設士師之職立禦盜之制徇
刑掌之司稽殺刑掌之朝士摶盜掌之司
隸諜盜掌之環人刑賞施于追胥之比則
===
良民安司兵入于數量之辨則亂民飭相
翔誅於聚橾之守則賓至如歸夜士詔夫
分夜之禁則行人畫一當時之民沐井田
富庶之業而罔淫于禁則是周公所以治
民心者固先有其具而又曲為之制法懸
而民自不犯耳後世之民卽周之民而所
以戾于古而誣于法禁愈嚴而盜愈熾者
則以征戍之無已也勞役之無已也科歛
之無已也所謂致之有三豈虛語哉故沈
punctuated: 其藥愈投而病愈滋矣。執事憂八閩宼盜之虞，而以古人備盜為問，蓋亦穔豕之牙，而為今日東南民慮者至切也。愚也願酌古準今而陳之，可乎？夫古昔盛時，奸宄之戒，干羽之舞，其民皞皞如也。逮周而防制始立，蓋周公以《關雎》《麟趾》之意而行《周官》之法度。於是設士師之職，立禦盜之制：徇刑掌之司稽，殺刑掌之朝士，摶盜掌之司隸，諜盜掌之環人。刑賞施于追胥之比，則良民安；司兵入于數量之辨，則亂民飭；相翔誅於聚橾之守，則賓至如歸；夜士詔夫分夜之禁，則行人畫一。當時之民，沐井田富庶之業，而罔淫于禁，則是周公所以治民心者，固先有其具，而又曲為之制，法懸而民自不犯耳。後世之民卽周之民，而所以戾于古而誣于法，禁愈嚴而盜愈熾者，則以征戍之無已也，勞役之無已也，科歛之無已也。所謂致之有三，豈虛語哉？故沈
translation_en:
…the more medicine is administered, the worse the illness grows. You, sir, are concerned about the danger of banditry in the Eight Min regions of Fujian and have asked about the ancients’ precautions against bandits. This, too, is surely a matter of dealing with the boar’s tusks [?], and reflects your most earnest concern for the people of the southeast today. May I, in my ignorance, weigh ancient precedents against present circumstances and set forth my views?

In antiquity’s flourishing age, there were admonitions against wrongdoing and dances with shields and feathers; the people lived in simple contentment. Only with the Zhou were systematic precautions established. The Duke of Zhou implemented the regulations of the Offices of Zhou in the spirit of “Guanju” (Ospreys) and “Linzhi” (The Qilin’s Hoof). Accordingly, he established the office of Judicial Officer and instituted measures against banditry. The Investigator administered exemplary punishments; the Court Gentleman administered capital punishments; the Director of Convict Labor was responsible for apprehending bandits; and the Patrolman was responsible for detecting them. Punishments and rewards were applied to the groups organized to pursue and search for bandits, and thus the law-abiding people enjoyed security. The Director of Weapons brought matters within distinctions of number and quantity [?], and thus disorderly people were disciplined. The xiangxiang [?] punished offenses in connection with the assembled watch [?], and thus visitors felt as though they had come home. The Night Patrolmen proclaimed the prohibitions for the divisions of the night, and thus travelers were subject to uniform rules.

The people of that time enjoyed the prosperity afforded by the well-field system and did not transgress the prohibitions. Thus, the Duke of Zhou already possessed the means to govern the people’s hearts before devising detailed regulations for them. Once the laws were publicly displayed, the people naturally refrained from violating them. The people of later ages are the same as those of the Zhou. Yet they depart from ancient ways and flout the laws; the stricter the prohibitions, the more rampant the banditry. This is because military expeditions and garrison service never cease, labor service never ceases, and levies and exactions never cease. Could the saying that three things bring this about be empty words? Thus, the shen[ming] law …

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
命法立於武帝而天漢中之盜自若也盜
賊重法奏於神宗而熈寧中之盜自若也
立鄉村團爲義營者一戶被盜累其一將
新鄭捕亡之術則然耳出庫錢榜置市者
一盜告捕賞錢一市安潜招降之術則然
耳然皆以救一時之急非長治之計也故
愚以爲弭盜之術莫先于任官焉任官之
法莫要于裕民焉任官在於慎俊選以考
其德稽殿最以覈其能明黜陟以勵其心
===
則賢能何有于不勸而貪墨者遠矣裕民
在於孚之以誠慤而民不悖導之以生業
而民不擾省之以誅求而民不匱則禮義
何有于不興而慆淫者寡矣善乎歐陽文
忠公之言曰方今禦盜不過四事曰州郡
置兵爲備也選捕盜之官也明賞罰之法
也去冗官用良吏以撫疲民也夫宋之論
備盜者衆矣而惟用良吏之言可爲後世
法方今閩南之地分爲八郡延建邵汀阻
punctuated:
命法立於武帝，而天漢中之盜自若也；盜賊重法奏於神宗，而熈寧中之盜自若也。立鄉村團爲義營者，一戶被盜，累其一將，新鄭捕亡之術則然耳；出庫錢榜置市者，一盜告捕，賞錢一市，安潜招降之術則然耳。然皆以救一時之急，非長治之計也。故愚以爲弭盜之術，莫先于任官焉；任官之法，莫要于裕民焉。任官在於慎俊選以考其德，稽殿最以覈其能，明黜陟以勵其心，則賢能何有于不勸，而貪墨者遠矣。裕民在於孚之以誠慤而民不悖，導之以生業而民不擾，省之以誅求而民不匱，則禮義何有于不興，而慆淫者寡矣。
善乎歐陽文忠公之言曰：「方今禦盜，不過四事：曰州郡置兵爲備也，選捕盜之官也，明賞罰之法也，去冗官、用良吏以撫疲民也。」夫宋之論備盜者衆矣，而惟用良吏之言可爲後世法。方今閩南之地分爲八郡，延建邵汀阻
translation_en:
…the law imposing death for failure to suppress bandits was established under Emperor Wu, yet banditry continued unabated during the Tianhan era. The stringent law against bandits was submitted to Emperor Shenzong, yet banditry continued unabated during the Xining era. Organizing village militia groups into volunteer battalions and holding their commander responsible when a single household was robbed—such was Xinzheng’s method of apprehending fugitives. Taking treasury funds and posting notices in the marketplace, so that when one bandit was reported and captured, an entire market received monetary rewards [?]—such was An Qian’s method of inducing surrender. Yet these measures merely met an immediate emergency; they were no plans for lasting order. Thus, in my humble view, nothing takes precedence over appointing officials as a means of suppressing banditry, and nothing is more essential to the proper exercise of office than enriching the people. In appointing officials, carefully select outstanding men to assess their virtue, examine their performance ratings to verify their ability, and make dismissals and promotions clear to spur their resolve. How, then, could the worthy and capable fail to be encouraged? Corrupt officials would be kept at a distance. To enrich the people, win their trust through sincerity and honesty, so that they do not rebel; guide them toward productive livelihoods, so that they are not unsettled; and reduce exactions upon them, so that they do not suffer want. How, then, could ritual propriety and righteousness fail to flourish? Those given to dissipation and excess would be few.
Excellent are the words of Lord Ouyang, posthumously titled Wenzhong: “At present, defending against bandits requires only four things: stationing troops in prefectures for defense; selecting officials to apprehend bandits; making the rules for rewards and punishments clear; and eliminating superfluous officials and employing good ones to care for the exhausted people.” Many men of the Song discussed defenses against bandits, but it is the advice to employ good officials that can serve as a model for later ages. At present, the territory of southern Min is divided into eight prefectures. Yan, Jian, Shao, and Ting are protected by…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
山依谷剷麓而耕壘石而種其爲平原沃
土無幾也福興泉漳帶海襟江高原爲礫
卑隰爲滷其爲平原沃土亦無幾也其間
租稅農桑有常徵矣漁鹽鈔鐵有常課矣
而額外之誅求取括者尚無已也如是而
官課得謂之輕乎濱海有水寨之兵阻山
有坑隘之守又有憲臣以專督海之任而
簿尉鄉閭之巡邏者無稽焉如是而禁網
得謂之闊乎故山海之民有流而爲盜者
===
無怪乎其然也蓋利在于山則荷戈斬木
以冒盜礦之禁利在于海則浮艦揭貲以
冒通番之禁玆欲禦之則險夷之習既不
相如主客之形又甚懸絕我集彼散我散
彼集是彼坐得勝筭而我卒受其敝耳是
宜有以厪執事之慮也玆欲爲安閩之計
以圖善後之策宜無有出於任官之說者
先臣文莊丘濬之議有曰得一良令如得
勝兵三千人得一良守如得勝兵三萬人
banxin: 福建鄉試錄 七十六
punctuated:
山依谷，剷麓而耕，壘石而種，其爲平原沃土無幾也。福興泉漳，帶海襟江，高原爲礫，卑隰爲滷，其爲平原沃土亦無幾也。其間租稅農桑有常徵矣，漁鹽鈔鐵有常課矣，而額外之誅求取括者尚無已也。如是而官課得謂之輕乎？濱海有水寨之兵，阻山有坑隘之守，又有憲臣以專督海之任，而簿尉鄉閭之巡邏者無稽焉。如是而禁網得謂之闊乎？故山海之民有流而爲盜者，無怪乎其然也。蓋利在于山，則荷戈斬木，以冒盜礦之禁；利在于海，則浮艦揭貲，以冒通番之禁。玆欲禦之，則險夷之習既不相如，主客之形又甚懸絕。我集彼散，我散彼集，是彼坐得勝筭，而我卒受其敝耳。是宜有以厪執事之慮也。
玆欲爲安閩之計，以圖善後之策，宜無有出於任官之說者。先臣文莊丘濬之議有曰：「得一良令，如得勝兵三千人；得一良守，如得勝兵三萬人，
translation_en:
…mountains and valleys, clearing the foothills to plough and piling up stones to plant; little of their land consists of fertile plains. Fuzhou, Xinghua, Quanzhou, and Zhangzhou are girdled by the sea and enfolded by rivers. Their uplands are gravelly and their lowlands saline; they too have little fertile plain. There are regular exactions on agricultural and sericultural production, and fixed levies on fishing, salt, paper currency [?], and iron. Yet demands and extraction beyond the prescribed quotas still know no end. Under such circumstances, can official levies be called light? Along the coast are troops stationed at naval stockades; amid the mountains are guards at ravines and passes. There is also a censorial official charged specifically with overseeing maritime affairs, while the patrols conducted in the villages by registrars and commandants receive no scrutiny [?]. Under such circumstances, can the net of prohibitions be called loose? It is therefore no wonder that some people of the mountains and coast drift into banditry.
Where profit lies in the mountains, they shoulder weapons and fell trees, defying the prohibition on illicit mining. Where profit lies at sea, they launch ships and raise capital, defying the prohibition on intercourse with foreign peoples. If we now seek to check them, our familiarity with difficult and easy terrain is unequal, and the positions of those on their own ground and those coming from outside differ enormously. When we concentrate, they disperse; when we disperse, they concentrate. Thus they readily secure the advantage, while we ultimately suffer the harm. This ought to engage your concern.
In devising a plan to pacify Fujian and secure its lasting peace, nothing should surpass the proposal to appoint suitable officials. The late minister Qiu Jun, posthumously titled Wenzhuang, stated in a deliberation: “To obtain one good district magistrate is like obtaining three thousand victorious soldiers; to obtain one good prefect is like obtaining thirty thousand victorious soldiers…

title: 嘉靖十三年福建鄉試錄
text:
得一良部使者如得勝兵三十萬人此實
有得於歐陽子之旨而深切于八閩弭盜
之防者與故治山得一賈琮則尺書移檄
而不患巷路之無歌治海得一龔遂則單
車就道而不患兵戈之不解之二子者非
所謂勝兵者乎雖然其要在守令其機在
部使而其權在
朝廷必也緩治盜而急治民後催科而先撫
字而又躬儉約以憫民窮秉權衡以平民
===
志燭幾微以悉民隱廣孚惠以賙民乏崇
裕柔以亮民昧則民將有生之樂無死之
虞雖賞之不竊矣所謂治心者此也由是
而猶有盜焉則於海也擇其水陸交會之
